jobDescription:
Join Us at MSF – A Meaningful, People-Centric Career in SSD/RE
At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
This is an individual contributor role in the Resourcing and Ecosystem (RE) Division of the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF). 
RE aims to cultivate a future-ready social service sector that delivers quality services, is well-resourced, and has high levels of community engagement and contribution.
jobResponsibilities:
Drive the digital transformation of Singapore's social service sector and shape how technology can improve lives across our communities! 

You will develop strategic policies and plans that enable the digital transformation of Singapore’s social service sector, in collaboration with key internal and external stakeholders. 

For example, you will:  

·	Work with key operational ‘business’ units to identify opportunities for digital innovation and transformation and conduct technology pilots within national social service programmes; 

·	Design and review funding policies and strategies for technology adoption within the social service sector; 

·	Review existing social service data platforms and infrastructure to map integration opportunities, identify interoperability enhancements, and develop recommendations for addressing unmet data sharing use cases across the sector; and

·	Establish comprehensive data governance and cybersecurity policies that align with national standards, whilst addressing the unique requirements of the social service sector. 

This is an individual contributor role, with the opportunity to progress into being the project lead of several key technology projects.
jobRequirements:
•	Background in engineering, science and technology, public policy or other relevant fields. Postgraduate qualifications will be advantageous. 

•	At least 2 years of experience in public policy, science and technology, and/or cybersecurity strategy. 

•	Strong analytical thinking, communication, and stakeholder management skills. 

Experience with digital transformation projects, particularly in the context of social service delivery, will be highly advantageous.

jobTitle: Asst Engineering Manager (Landfill Management and Operations Dept) - Contract
agencyDescription:
The National Environment Agency (NEA) is the leading public organisation responsible for ensuring a clean and sustainable environment for Singapore. Its key roles are to improve and sustain a clean environment, promote sustainability and resource efficiency, maintain high public health standards, provide timely and reliable meteorological information, and encourage a vibrant hawker culture. NEA works closely with its partners and the community to develop and spearhead environmental and public health initiatives and programmes. It is committed to motivating every individual to care for the environment as a way of life, in order to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore for present and future generations.

For more information, visit www.nea.gov.sg
jobDescription: Landfill Management and Operations Department (LMOD) oversee Tuas Marine Transfer Station and Semakau Landfill which is Singapore’s only landfill for waste disposal.
jobResponsibilities:
The job description of an AEM at Tuas Marine Transfer Station (TMTS) and Semakau Landfill (SL) are as follows:

  • To assist the engineer in overseeing and ensuring safe waste receiving operations at TMTS & SL slipways

  • To coordinate operational and safety matters with TMTS/SL stakeholders to ensure operations at TMTS/SL such as landfill, O&M of M&E equipment, O&M of tugs & barges (T&B) are conducted according to plan.

  • To supervise contractors in carrying out the work/services on site. Ensuring that all work is carried out safely and do not disrupt operations. Attend to any maintenance or repair works to ensure that it is completed within the set timeline.

  • To assist engineer in the review of the traffic management plans within TMTS/SL.

  • To prepare and call quotations for buildings and the facility’s infrastructure maintenance. Successful candidates will also need to review and ensure sufficient supply of spare parts for landfill equipment.

  • To perform any other works, duties and responsibilities as assigned by supervisors.
jobRequirements:
• At least a diploma in any engineering discipline as recognised by the Professional Engineer Board.

  • At least 3 years of working experience in construction, waste management or facility management industry.

  • Candidate with procurement experience and contract management experience is preferred.

  • Possess good interpersonal and communication skills

  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Able to work independently with minimal supervision

  • Able to work in harsh environment/conditions

  • Will be working on morning/afternoon shifts, including weekends

  • Willing and able to be deployed at both locations (TMTS and SL)

  • As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription: As an Outdoor Adventure Educator (OAE), you will have the opportunity to lead camping activities, facilitate learning, and ensure the well-being of students at MOE Outdoor Adventure Learning Centres.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Conduct outdoor adventure camp activities and facilitate students’ reflection and learning.
•	Ensure students' safety through safety instructions and adherence to procedures.
•	Provide administrative and logistical support for camp activities.
•	Plan and evaluate camp programme, to ensure achievement of learning outcomes.

As an OAE, you will typically facilitate 4D3N or 3D2N camps as part of a 5-day work week, which may include Saturdays.

Under our Work-Rest-Learn cycle, you will be given a rest day (Off-in-Lieu) after each camp, followed by non-camp weekdays dedicated to preparation for the next camp and professional learning. This rhythm supports both recovery and continuous growth between each camp deployment.
jobRequirements:
•	Passion for character development in our students.
•	Keen interest in outdoor adventure activities.
•	Ability to connect and establish rapport with students.
•	Capability to perform and supervise activities at height and in waters.
•	Ability to work collaboratively in a team.
•	Physical fitness and mental resilience to carry out responsibilities effectively.
•	Experience in conducting outdoor activities for students would be an advantage.

In general, applicants can expect to hear from us within 4 weeks of the close of the application window. In the event where we receive a high number of applications, applicants will receive an update on their status within 6 weeks of the close of the window.

If you are shortlisted, you will be required to attend a 1-day compulsory selection programme at an MOE Outdoor Adventure Learning Centre (OALC), where you will be assessed on your competencies for various height- and water-based activities, including ability to swim in coastal waters. Candidates who are further shortlisted following the selection programme will be required to attend a 1-day attachment programme at an MOE OALC, which provides a preview of the job and comprises further assessments by MOE. For more details, please visit our MOE OAE Career website.

If you are facing issues submitting your application through the Careers@Gov portal, please contact us at Careers.gov.technicalhelp@psd.gov.sg for assistance.

jobTitle: Laboratory Officer (Red Cell Reference Lab) - Patient Services Division
agencyDescription:
The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) applies medical, pharmaceutical and scientific expertise through its three professional groups, Health Products Regulation, Blood Services and Applied Sciences, to protect and advance national health and safety. HSA is a multidisciplinary authority. It serves as the national regulator for health products, ensuring they are wisely regulated to meet standards of safety, quality and efficacy. As the national blood service, it is responsible for providing a safe and adequate blood supply. It also applies specialised scientific, forensic, investigative and analytical capabilities in serving the administration of justice. 

For more details, visit http://www.hsa.gov.sg/. 

For more updates on public health and safety matters, follow us on Twitter at www.twitter.com/HSAsg and LinkedIn at https://sg.linkedin.com/company/health-sciences-authority.
jobDescription: We are looking for a committed individual to be part of the Blood Services Group (BSG), Patient Services Division. The appointee for this position will be a laboratory officer in the Red Cell Reference Laboratory, which provides patient-centric laboratory services in the area of red cell immunohaematology. As a Laboratory Officer in Red Cell Reference Laboratory, you will be rostered to do shift work. The shifts are 12-hours long with a combination of morning and night shifts, i.e. 8am to 8pm, and 8pm to 8am. You will also be required to work weekend and public holiday shifts as rostered.
jobResponsibilities:
Responsibilities:-

  • To perform all tests and processes in the assigned laboratory in BSG, within set standard operating procedures and guidelines, with the objective of ensuring an efficient blood programme, and the quality and safety of the national blood supply.
  • Prepare specialised blood components for patients with specific requirements
  • Operate specialised laboratory procedures for transplant support services
  • Provide support in the red cell reference laboratory which provides specialised referral services to hospitals and clinical laboratories that encounter difficulties in red cell antibody investigation and resolution of ABO discrepancies.
jobRequirements:
Requirements:-

  • Relevant academic qualifications in Science, Medical Laboratory Technology or equivalent
  • 3 – 5 years working experience in an immunohaematology laboratory
  • Knowledgeable about basic laboratory practices and procedures, including safety requirements
  • Good laboratory technical skills
  • Comfortable working with the computer and using specialisted laboratory software
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills
  • Willing to work 12-hour shifts, which will include overnight shift, weekends and public holiday shifts.

The appointee can look forward to a salary package comprising of basic salary, shift allowances, shoe allowance, bonus payments and other staff benefits.

Shortlisted candidates would be contacted within 30 days from the closing date of the advertisement. We regret that only shortlisted candidates would be notified.

jobDescription: Families are the bedrock of our society. The goal of Family Life Group (FLG) is to build strong and resilient families, supporting them through all life stages. As the central division for FLG, the Operations Planning & Transformation (OPT) division is responsible for ops strategy, corporate planning, data and digitalisation, transformation as well as organisational development strategies for FLG.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be leading a team to drive digital and technology transformation plans across Family Life Group, to improve business outcomes such as user experience, service delivery and programme efficacy. Our aim is to strengthen access to FLG services and programmes and deliver MSF’s strategic outcomes of encouraging marriage and parenthood.

The role involves the following:
•	Conducting systems-level review and planning of FLG’s digital, AI and technology capabilities to optimise FLG services and programmes that involves both Ministry and Whole-of-Government (WOG) stakeholders.
•	Identifying technological gaps and opportunities to improve service delivery and programme implementation to better serve families through all stages of life.
•	Evaluating and addressing cross-cutting service gaps and enhance customer experience.
•	Spearheading FLG’s digital and technology priorities and plans.
•	Identify and develop technology use cases that can transform core businesses/service delivery in FLG. This include working with key stakeholders to discover, design, prototype (e.g. proof-of-concepts) to scale up.
jobRequirements:
To meet the challenges of this role, you should possess:

At least 8 years of experience in digital transformation, such as digitalisation of operations, leveraging digital tech to improve business outcomes, creating digital products or platforms or encouraging innovation and experimentation in digital-tech or AI. 

KEY TRAITS
-	Strong analytical and critical thinking, writing and communication skills.
-	Ability to analyse issues from a strategic and systems perspective, while having a good grasp of details and processes.
-	Strong stakeholder engagement and management skills.
-	Experience in leading teams in transformation related work.
-	Strong problem-solving skills with proven ability to deliver impact in greenfield environments
-	Strong interest in digital technology and emerging technologies (eg. AI) will be a plus

jobTitle: Manager, Strategy & Policy, National Space Agency of Singapore
agencyDescription: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) seeks to transform Singapore into a leading global city of talent, enterprise and innovation. Our mission is to promote economic growth and create good jobs to enable Singaporeans to improve their lives. In MTI, you can expect an exciting, challenging and rewarding career!
jobDescription: We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Manager (Strategy & Policy) to lead Singapore's space policy development and international engagement. This is a unique opportunity to shape Singapore's position in the global space economy and contribute to the development of international space governance frameworks.
jobResponsibilities:
As Manager (Strategy & Policy), you will spearhead critical initiatives that position Singapore as a responsible and innovative space nation. You will develop the National Space Strategy 1.0, establishing Singapore's comprehensive roadmap for space development across government, industry, and research sectors. This foundational strategy will guide Singapore's space ambitions and coordinate efforts across multiple agencies and stakeholders.

You will lead the development of national space legislation, crafting the legal framework that will govern Singapore's space activities whilst ensuring compliance with international obligations and supporting commercial space development. This includes analysing existing regulatory gaps, consulting with industry stakeholders, and designing legislation that balances innovation with responsible space governance.

Your role extends to developing Singapore's international policy positions on space matters, requiring deep analysis of emerging space technologies, geopolitical considerations, and economic opportunities. You will formulate policy recommendations that advance Singapore's national interests whilst contributing to global space governance.

On the international stage, you will represent Singapore in multilateral forums, particularly within the United Nations system, advocating for Singapore's positions whilst helping to shape international space law and norms. This includes participating in negotiations, building coalitions with like-minded nations, and contributing to the development of guidelines for responsible space activities.
jobRequirements:
•	The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in policy development, international relations, or space governance. You should have a strong understanding of international law, multilateral diplomacy, and the space sector's technical and commercial aspects. Experience in government policy work, international organisations, or space-related industries would be highly valued.
•	You possess excellent analytical and strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to synthesise complex technical, legal, and political considerations into coherent policy recommendations. Strong communication and negotiation skills are essential, as you will engage with diverse stakeholders from government agencies, industry, academia, and international partners.
•	Familiarity with space technology, international space law, or UN processes would be advantageous.

Learner. Creator. Leader

jobDescription: This is a customer facing position with the Temasek SkillsFuture Academy.
jobResponsibilities:
The Customer Engagement Executive will be expected to perform the following responsibilities when appointed:

• Serve as the first point of contact for all enquiries, ensuring timely acknowledgement and coordinating internally with the Programme Management / Business Development teams to follow-up within 3 working days.

• Assist customers/students with product and service-related queries, issues, and requests via multiple channels (emails, calls, walk-ins)

• Conduct lead follow-up on programme/course enquiries, including tracking responses and closing the loop with customers.

• Resolve concerns and complaints effectively, aiming for first-contact resolution.

• Support operations at the TSA One-Stop Centre to ensure a customer-ready environment.

• Provide administrative and logistics support for events (e.g., Graduation Ceremony, new Course Orientation, Partners Appreciation Event, SkillsFuture Festival), and ad-hoc duties as required.
jobRequirements:
• Qualification in any discipline with at least 2 years of experience in customer facing / engagement positions.
• Service quality mind-set with good communication skills.
• Meticulous and systematic.
• A team player with high initiative, resourceful and savvy with digital technology.
• Good time management, ability to multi-task and prioritise work.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

You will develop and deliver engaging lectures that inspire and shape the future of our students. In addition to your teaching responsibilities, you will serve as a mentor and guide, supporting students in their academic and personal growth. You will also undertake industry or consultancy projects to stay current with professional trends and evolving industry changes. Building and maintaining strong connections with industry and educational institutions is crucial. You will have opportunities for regular industry attachments or experiences to continuously update your skills, knowledge, and professional practices.

You will specialise in delivering education in either automation technologies and smart systems, or mechanical systems maintenance and operations, preparing students for modern manufacturing demands.
jobRequirements:
We are seeking highly skilled engineering professionals who are keen to mentor and guide the next generation of technical experts in ITE as Lecturers in Mechanical Engineering.

• Hands-on experience: Minimum 3 years in either:

  • Industrial automation, robotics systems, or smart manufacturing environments, OR

  • Mechanical systems maintenance, industrial piping and valve operations, or machinery maintenance (examples include industrial facilities, power plants, water treatment facilities, building services, or similar environments)

• Technical Expertise: Proficient in at least two of the following:

  • PLC programming and system integration

  • Industrial robotics setup, programming and maintenance

  • Automation system troubleshooting and smart manufacturing technologies

  • Mechanical systems maintenance and testing procedures

  • Industrial piping and valve systems installation and repair

  • Machinery maintenance including transmission systems and industrial pumps

• Industry Knowledge: Up-to-date with at least one of the following:

  • Digital manufacturing and Industry 4.0 concepts

  • IoT integration and predictive maintenance technologies

  • Condition monitoring systems and cybersecurity principles for industrial systems

  • Sustainability practices in automation and manufacturing operations

• Educational Background: Trained in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related engineering disciplines with practical experience in chosen specialisation area.

• Professional Attributes: Passion and commitment to engineering and teaching career, with strong communication skills and ability to mentor students.

• Additional Advantage: Knowledge of using AI in engineering environments, professional robotics certifications, or experience in training technical personnel.

Those with good and relevant experience can look forward to Senior Lecturer or equivalent positions, with career development opportunities to leadership positions in the Colleges or Headquarters.

jobTitle: Statistical Specialist (Data Analytics and Methodology), Data Collection, MRSD
agencyDescription:
Championing Human Potential for a Thriving Singapore
Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
The position is located in the Manpower Research and Statistics Department (MRSD), Singapore. The department produces a wide range of national labour market statistics to facilitate informed decision-making within the government and the community-at-large.

The main role of the position is to collect, analyse and interpret data using innovative tools, methods and approaches to optimise survey operations and facilitate policy making and development.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Leveraging on a variety of data sources (i.e survey data, administrative data), including big data to generate actionable insights.
•	Apply statistical techniques and data mining methods to identify patterns and trends, employment patterns, and labour market dynamics.
•	Designing user-friendly data visualization dashboards, presentation slides, charts and tables.
•	Undertake both qualitative and quantitative research and analysis, including predictive modelling, time-series forecasting. Commission research, draft terms of reference for research consultants and monitor and coordinate their work. 
•	Draft and/or provide technical input into the development, peer review and editing of occupational/industry classification system reviews, working papers, reports, publications and other knowledge products and contribute to their dissemination. 
•	Keeping up to date with advancements and developments in machine learning so as to leverage new tools and techniques. 
•	Provide evidence-based technical content for social media, digital and other knowledge-sharing tools and platforms, with a view to reaching broad and diverse audiences.
•	Developing and implementing policies related to data governance policies, procedures and standards, including identifying and resolving data quality issues.
•	Perform other relevant duties as assigned.
jobRequirements:
•	Tertiary qualifications with a preferred field of study in Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science or other relevant field.
•	Experience in research and quantitative analysis. Candidates with coding and programming experience (e.g. Python, R) will be considered favourably.
•	Good knowledge and understanding of theories, trends and approaches in the area(s) of machine learning/deep learning, natural language processing, large language modelling and econometrics modelling.
•	Good research and analytical skills.  
•	Good communication, presentation and writing skills. 
•	Ability to maintain effective and collaborative working relationships with key stakeholders.

jobDescription:
By 2030, almost a million Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, and there will be an increased demand for aged care services including Senior Care Centres (SCCs) and Active Ageing Centres (AACs). To reduce social isolation and delay cognitive and physical frailty among seniors, MOH has: (i) expanded the number of AACs to support well seniors with improved the range of services and programs offered at the AACs, and (ii)  improved the capacity and utilisation of SCC services to serve a subsegment of seniors who need supervision and assistance in activities of daily living (ADL) when their caregivers are at work.

However, ground implementation of AACs and SCCs may be varied. Some AACs have managed to attract many seniors to their centres and created a lively environment for seniors, while other AACs may not be as successful in outreaching to seniors. Different SCCs may have varying services which may not fully address the emerging needs of seniors (e.g. dementia care, custodial care, community rehabilitation).  

The Centre-Based Care & Social Support (CCSS) team (under the Ageing Planning Office in the Ministry of Health) is at the forefront of overseeing the overall strategy, policy, resourcing and governance for AAC and SCC services. The end goal is to enable seniors to remain well and socially engaged in the community and ensure service providers are uplifted to play such roles to support our seniors.
jobResponsibilities:
You will play a role in designing and implementing policies for AAC / SCC.  This includes working with MOH departments and partners such as the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to design policy levers (e.g., care models, sector structure, and capacity planning) to meet seniors/caregiver needs in the community. You will also review resourcing models (e.g. budget, manpower, infrastructure and site allocation), develop and implement governance structures supporting the provision of AAC and SCC services, and evaluate cost-effectiveness of new service models and make recommendations. Working closely with AIC as the lead implementation partner, you will co-develop strategies that translate policy intent into outcomes on the ground. 

This will also require a strong ability to collaborate closely with and work through stakeholders to implement these strategies. Public sector experience in service design, managing budgetary/procurement processes or large-scale infrastructural projects will be beneficial. 
 
You will be working in a fast paced and highly volatile environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. You can expect meaningful work that will improve the lived experience of seniors, while growing professionally through developing your strategy, planning and stakeholder engagement skills.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

The Paramedic Specialist (Work-Study Diploma in Paramedicine) programme by SCDF offers an excellent option for individuals navigating the post-ITE graduation phase, providing a blend of academic pursuit and practical work experience, thus offering the benefits of both realms. It enables them to advance their studies without financial worries and receive a monthly salary. 
 
Those holding NITEC or Higher NITEC qualifications and eager to join the Lifesaving Force upon graduation may find enrolling in a WSDip - Paramedicine program appealing. This pathway allows them to simultaneously work, earn a salary, and pursue a diploma. 
 
Upon joining SCDF, graduates can look forward to securing stable full-time employment with an enticing remuneration package. Candidate can stand to earn between $2,940 - $4,370, supplemented by additional monthly frontline allowances that goes up to $750.

Newly recruited trainees will receive a sign-on bonus of $30,000. This sum will be disbursed in two tranches: $12,000 upon signing the contract and $18,000 upon confirmation. 
 
As valued members of SCDF, employees stand to benefit from a range of perks and privileges, including: 
•	Competitive salary range, inclusive of frontline / shift allowance
•	Obtain a Work-Study Diploma in Paramedicine with ITE

•	Performance bonus
•	14 to 18 days’ vacation leave 
•	Medical and Dental Subsidies

jobTitle: SCDF Fire and Rescue Specialist (Work Study Diploma)
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.
jobDescription:
The Work-Study Diploma (“WSDip”) programme by SCDF offers an excellent option for individuals navigating the post-ITE graduation phase, providing a blend of academic pursuit and practical work experience, thus offering the benefits of both realms. It enables them to advance their studies without financial worries and receive a monthly salary. 
 
Those holding NITEC or Higher NITEC qualifications and eager to join the Lifesaving Force upon graduation may find enrolling in a WSDip program appealing. This pathway allows them to simultaneously work, earn a salary, and pursue a diploma. 
 
Upon joining SCDF, officers can look forward to securing stable full-time employment with an enticing remuneration package. They can also stand to earn between $2,940 - $4,370, inclusive of monthly frontline allowances.    

As a successful applicant, you will receive a $30,000 sign-on bonus (subject to eligibility) upon emplacement. This sum will be disbursed in two tranches: $12,000 upon signing the contract and $18,000 upon confirmation. 

You will also stand to receive benefits from a range of perks and privileges, including:
•	Competitive salary range, inclusive of frontline / shift allowance
•	Annual increments 
•	Performance bonuses 
•	14 to 18 days’ vacation leave (inclusive of other leave types) 
•	Medical and Dental Subsidies 
•	Employee welfare benefits 
•	Learning and Development subsidy
•	Strategic Payment Scheme
•	Invest Retirement Package
•	Group insurance 
•	Obtain a Fire Safety Manager Certification 
•	Obtain an Emergency Medical Technician Certification 
•	Obtain Class 3, 4 and/or 5 Driving Licenses 

Upon completing the WSDip, trainees will continue to progress in the SCDF with more exciting career opportunities, as they are deployed to specialised roles with higher rank(s).
jobResponsibilities:
Trainees under the course will join SCDF and become Fire and Rescue Specialists tasked with safeguarding lives and property in various emergency situations. As part of their duties, they will utilise their training to respond to fires, medical emergencies, and other rescue missions. Responsibilities include deploying firefighting techniques, conducting rescue operations, and providing medical assistance to those in need. 
 
The hands-on training will comprise 80% of the course, allowing trainees to gain practical experience in real-world scenarios. The remaining 20% will consist of off-the-job training on campus, providing theoretical knowledge and enhancing skill development. Joining SCDF offers not only the opportunity to serve the community but also the chance to make a significant impact by safeguarding lives and property during emergencies. 
 
As a WSDip Programme trainee, you can expect a comprehensive career pathway that includes the Fire and Rescue Section Commander course and Emergency Medical Technical training. After completing the relevant training, trainees will undergo the 2.5-year WSDip Programme while being stationed at a Fire Station. Frontline officers are eligible for allowances of up to $300
jobRequirements:
The WSDip program is a workplace training initiative available for individual who are ITE graduates. 
 
•	NITEC Certification with a minimum GPA score of 2.0; or any Higher NITEC Certification. 
•	Applicants with NS obligations must be medically classified as PES B1 or above
•	Minimum pass standard for IPPT; 
•	For Pre-enlistees, there will be a 5-year Minimum Term of Engagement (MTE) bond in lieu of the National Service’s obligation.  

For more information, please visit the following links  
SCDF Fire and Rescue Specialist (WSDip)
https://www.scdf.gov.sg/home/join-us/uniformed-positions/scdfwsdip

Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
MOM’s Work Pass Division (WPD) is modernising its Work Permit (WP) eServices (known as WINS-WP) to deliver reliable, adaptive, and user-friendly eServices that streamlines WP transactions for our customers. The WINS-WP Policy & Planning Office (WPPO) drives this modernisation effort through formulating a transformation roadmap, conducting thorough business process reviews (BPRs), and driving change management.

As a member of the WPPO team, you will play a key role in shaping and transforming the service delivery of Singapore’s Work Permit policies. Working at the intersection of policy, operations and systems, you will lead complex business process reviews and ground-up policy reviews to support the development of the WINS-WP system. You will also conduct engagements and prepare communications materials to ensure that users are well-equipped to navigate the changes. This role is critical in ensuring that WP workflows are robust, future-ready and user-centric, while remaining aligned with policy intent and operational realities.

The roles offers:
•	Meaningful work that contributes directly to national workforce and manpower outcomes
•	Opportunities to work on large-scale policy and digital transformation initiatives
•	Exposure to cross-divisional and cross-agency collaboration
•	A professional environment that values learning, initiative and teamwork
jobResponsibilities:
•	Chart out the WINS-WP transformation journey by contributing to transformation roadmaps, defining user journeys, and shaping success metrics from a business and policy perspective.
•	Conduct complex Work Permit Business Process Reviews (BPRs), re-examining end-to-end workflows, challenging legacy practices, and designing streamlined “to-be” processes.
•	Work closely with MOM policy divisions and operational teams to carry out ground-up policy reviews, translating policy intent into workable operational and system designs.
•	Engage internal and external stakeholders, including system and technology teams and other government agencies, to assess impacts, manage trade-offs, and adjust to changes arising from process and policy changes.
jobRequirements:
•	At least 2 years of working experience is preferred
•	Experience in policy, strategic planning, business process improvement, or operational transformation portfolios, or familiarity with work pass processes and foreign worker policies will be advantageous
•	Strategic thinker with the ability to challenge the status quo while balancing policy objectives, operational feasibility and user experience
•	Good interpersonal and communication skills, and ability to work across agencies and diverse stakeholders to reach mutually beneficial outcomes
•	Strong time management skills, including the ability to adapt, manage multiple projects simultaneously and work under pressure to meet tight timelines

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

Additionally, strong planning, coordination, and people management skills are important for executing training plans and managing courses effectively while optimising training resources. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment is key to success in this role.

You will operate at the intersection of policy, legislation, operations, and system design to translate policy intent into implementable, system-ready solutions. jobDescription: The role is responsible for developing and operationalising AI solutions to support critical energy sector operations and regulatory functions. jobTitle: SCDF Fire and Rescue Officer (Direct-Entry Lieutenant)
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

The team is charged with transforming the way HTX delivers AI-infused software, leveraging the latest technologies to enable agile software development, zero-trust security, continuous DevSecOps, and artificial intelligence.

As Head, MLOps, you will lead a team of engineers in designing, developing, and maintaining secure end-to-end DevSecOps solutions and processes. This is a hands-on technical leadership role sitting at the intersection of systems engineering, applied ML, and enterprise governance — pivotal in ensuring the security, scalability, and operational efficiency of software development and engineering workflows across HTX.

You will lead the design, architecture, and delivery of HTX's enterprise-scale AI platform, spanning the inference stack that serves in-house and open-source LLMs, and the agentic AI platform that enables officers across Home Team Departments to build, govern, and automate their own workflows. 

Through platform engineering, you will enhance developer experience and productivity while safeguarding organisational assets.

You will own the architectural direction of the AI platform, influence senior leadership on AI strategy, and build the team and partnerships needed to deliver at scale across on-prem, intranet, and air-gapped environments.
jobResponsibilities:
AI Platform Architecture & Delivery: Define and evolve the reference architecture for an enterprise agentic AI platform covering agent harnesses, sandboxing strategy, MCP connector gateways, durable execution, skills libraries, approval workflows, and structured audit trails. Shift the organisation from bespoke per-workflow builds to a platform where officers can describe what they need in natural language and have governed, versioned, repeatable workflows generated and executed. 

Inference Infrastructure: Own the roadmap and production operation of the LLM inference stack, covering vLLM/SGLang/TGI-class serving, GPU utilisation, quantisation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimisation, and related throughput and latency work. Ensure the stack runs reliably across on-prem GPU clusters and air-gapped environments. 

Senior Leadership Engagement: Shape and communicate the AI platform strategy to chief executives and senior leadership across the Home Team. This includes building the business case, securing funding, and translating rapidly evolving technical trends (agentic harnesses, MCP adoption, managed agent services) into decisions the organisation can act on. 

Team Building & Mentorship: Grow the engineering team through hiring, onboarding, and structured internship programmes. Define reading lists, career paths, and technical standards. Mentor engineers across inference, platform, and agentic workflow areas.

● 8+ years of experience in ML platform, MLOps, or large-scale systems engineering roles, with demonstrated technical leadership delivering production AI/ML platforms 
● Strong hands-on experience with LLM inference optimisation (vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM), including speculative decoding, quantisation, and KV-cache strategies 
● Working knowledge of modern agent harnesses(Opencode, Hermes) and durable orchestration patterns, MCP and MCP gateways, and evaluation frameworks for agentic systems 
● Understanding of sandboxing strategies across the isolation spectrum 
● Strong expertise in container orchestration (Kubernetes, Helm), observability (Prometheus, Grafana), and MLOps tooling (MLflow or equivalents) 
● Proficiency in Go, Python, Javascript 
● Classical ML and data science fluency, with the judgement to know when a problem is better solved with causal inference, experimentation, or optimisation rather than a GenAI approach 
● Experience building production ML systems with measurable business impact 
● Enterprise architecture sensibility, with comfort designing for security-conscious, potentially air-gapped environments, and familiarity with identity services, document management, policy databases, and integration patterns across legacy enterprise systems 
● Demonstrated ability to shape strategy with executives, build compelling narratives and pitches, and move funding and resource decisions forward 
● Prior experience in government, defence, financial services, or other regulated environments 
● Experience leading the shift from bespoke application delivery to platform-based operating models 
● Platform thinking with a bias toward building the one platform that enables many workflows, rather than N bespoke applications 
● Strong written and visual communication skills, capable of engaging both engineering teams and senior executives 
● Collaborative approach working with data scientists, ML engineers, platform teams, and operational stakeholders across the Home Team 
● Comfort with the operating-model shift implied by platforms, moving from engineers as builders to engineers as platform providers, and officers as workflow authors 
● Proactive mindset focused on reliability, automation, governance, and sustainable delivery

jobDescription:
[What the role is]

You are the technical engine of our data exploration efforts. In the fast-paced world of tourism, new data opportunities emerge constantly, but their true value is often locked away. Your mission is to be the key that unlocks it.

This role is the technical counterpart to our Data Partnership Managers, forming a dynamic duo to accelerate our data pilots. While the Partnership Manager defines the business problem/opportunity and secures the data, you will deep-dive into the data - to wrangle the data, test hypotheses, and build compelling proof-of-concept dashboards and analyses. You are the "technical expert" in our "tech sales" model.

Success in this position means rapidly transforming raw, messy data from new data pilots and data partnerships into tangible, high-impact prototypes that showcase the possibilities and maximum potential we can achieve with our data. You will deliver the evidence and initial insights that determine which data pilots graduate to become scaled, industry-wide data products.

This contract role sits within the Data Exploration and Partnerships (DXP) department. We are looking for a data practitioner who is passionate in data exploration, experimentation, and moving quickly to create tangible impact.
jobResponsibilities:
[What you will be working on]

Technical Design & Feasibility Assessment:

  • Partner with Data Partnership Managers in later-stage discussions with potential data partners to finalise the scope and specifications of data exchange.

  • Act as the technical expert, assessing the quality, structure, and feasibility of using STB’s and our partner's data.

  • Help translate business problems into specific, testable analytical questions.

Hands-on Data Analysis & Prototyping:

  • Take the lead on the entire technical pilot process: data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation of new and diverse datasets.

  • Perform advanced exploratory data analysis (EDA) using Python to uncover hidden patterns, correlations, and insights that go beyond basic reporting.

  • Apply statistical methods to test hypotheses with rigour and build simple predictive models where applicable.

  • Lead technical discovery and experimentation, defining your own hypotheses and analytical approaches to uncover the most valuable insights.

  • Design and build compelling, interactive proof-of-concept dashboards (using tools like AWS QuickSight) that answer business questions clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Insight Generation & Storytelling:

  • Synthesize complex analytical findings into clear, concise insights and recommendations.

  • Collaborate with the Data Partnership Manager to present pilot findings back to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating the value of the data collaboration.

  • Where possible and relevant, stretch the data pilots to include predictive and prescriptive insight.

Knowledge Transfer & Scaling Preparation:

  • Meticulously document the data sources, cleaning logic, analytical methodologies, and code for successful pilots.

  • Create a "recipe book" for each successful pilot that enables a smooth handover to the Data & AI Product Manager for evaluation and potential productisation onto our core Data and Analytics platform, STAN.
jobRequirements:
[What we are looking for]

Technical and Analytics skills:

  • Trained in a quantitative field such as Data Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or Economics.

  • At least 3 years of demonstrable, hands-on experience in exploratory data analysis, data ingestion, transformation (cleaning, aggregation), and data modeling using large, real-world datasets.

  • Strong proficiency in statistical programming (e.g., Python) and database scripting (SQL) is essential.

  • Proven ability to develop compelling data visualizations and dashboards. Experience with tools like AWS QuickSight is highly advantageous.

  • Solid applied statistical knowledge (e.g., regression, classification, significance testing).

  • A portfolio of projects (e.g., via GitHub, a personal website, or a slide deck) showcasing your hands-on data analysis and coding work is required.

Work Approach:

  • Collaborative Partner: A strong team player who sees yourself as the technical counterpart to our business-facing managers. You are comfortable owning your technical workstream end-to-end while working closely with others to achieve a shared goal.

  • Comfortable with Ambiguity: A self-starter who thrives in an environment where priorities evolve and the path isn't always clear. You can take a vague business problem and messy data, and proactively find a path forward without waiting for instructions.

  • Accountable & Driven: Balance creativity and exploration with discipline and follow-through. You take ownership of your projects, manage your timelines effectively, and are responsible for communicating progress and challenges clearly.

  • The Pragmatic Storyteller: Strong analytical skills with a good eye for detail, but you also know how to translate complex technical findings into clear, concise language that a business audience can understand and act upon.

  • A Continuous Learner: Humble and curious, open to feedback, new techniques, and better ways of working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Research Analysts work closely with economists, data analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate evidence-based insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Conducting policy-relevant research and analysis
Analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, foreign and local manpower policies, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and forecasting
Contribute to ED’s monitoring of labour market developments, workforce trends and economic indicators to support timely policy assessments and decision-making.

•	Undertaking ex-ante and ex-post policy analysis
Assess the likely impact of proposed policies before implementation, and evaluate the actual impact of policies and programmes after implementation.

•	Applying quantitative and empirical methods
Use econometric, statistical, data analytics and modelling techniques to derive insights from administrative data, surveys and other datasets.

•	Building domain expertise in labour economics
Develop specialist knowledge of labour economics, public policy, empirical methods, data sources, analytical frameworks and relevant academic literature.

•	Collaborating across Government and with external researchers
Work with researchers, economists, policymakers and operational teams within and outside MOM to support policy thinking and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex research findings into clear, policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using research to improve public policy.

You should have:
•	A degree, Master’s or PhD in Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Public Policy, or another quantitative discipline.
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to conduct rigorous research and draw policy-relevant conclusions.
•	Strong quantitative skills, including experience in econometrics, statistical analysis, forecasting, policy modelling, simulations and/or impact evaluation.
•	Proficiency in statistical or programming software such as Stata, R or Python.
•	A strong interest in empirical research and public policy.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly and logically.
•	The ability to work collaboratively with researchers, policymakers and stakeholders across different domains.
•	A willingness to learn new methods, data sources and policy areas.

Candidates with experience in labour economics, applied microeconomics, programme evaluation, causal inference, data science and/or machine learning will have an advantage.

jobTitle: Data Policy, M/SM/AD, Govt Data Division, SNDG
agency: Ministry of Digital Development and Information
agencyDescription: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) drives Singapore’s digital development in four key domains — the economy, government, security, and society. MDDI oversees the development of the infocomm technology, cybersecurity, and media sectors; the Government’s digitalisation initiatives; and the national library, national archives, and public libraries. The Ministry is also responsible for effective public communications, and the Government’s information and public communication policies.
jobDescription:
The Smart Nation Group (SNG), under the Ministry of Digital Development and Information drives key Smart Nation and digital government projects, uplifts the standards of Government ICT and services, builds long-term capabilities for the public sector, and promotes adoption and participation in digital and smart innovations. We are pulling together a whole-of-nation effort, and we will actively engage the public, the industry and fellow agencies to build a Smart Nation together.

The Government Data Division (GDD) within SNG plays a central policymaking role in advancing the management and use of Government data as a national strategic asset. It is responsible for (a) developing and implementing whole-of-Government policies that guide data management, sharing and use across the public sector; (b) identifying and driving new initiatives to improve the exchange of data between Government agencies, and sharing of Government data with commercial partners and the public; and (c) strengthening data governance by developing policies on the responsible use of data, as well as (d) driving the development of capabilities, institutionalising structures and standardising tools.
jobResponsibilities:
We want a change maker who has experience in policymaking, and is collaborative in stakeholder management. Experience in data management, governance or related domains will also be helpful.

You must be ready to roll up your sleeves and rally different teams across Government agencies to achieve SNG's vision of a public sector that is 'data driven to the core'. This includes enabling Government agencies to use data to create solutions that benefit citizens and businesses, while ensuring the responsible use of data.

You will be part of a team at the forefront of transforming Government data and driving the next bound of the whole-of-Government data ecosystem, through policy formulation and development of key systems and structures. Your work will involve one or more of the following areas:

Policy Development and Implementation. Formulate and implement key data policies across whole-of-Government, that cover data governance, data sharing policies, data classification frameworks, treatment and protection of personal data, as well as the accompanying legislative frameworks.

Ecosystem Development. Design and implement the next bound of the Government data ecosystem, to supercharge data sharing and usage across whole-of-Government to enable agencies' use cases in policy, operations and service delivery, while ensuring good data governance. This entails the following work:

a. Conceptualising a whole value chain perspective of the data ecosystem, including how the pieces should come together to best facilitate the sharing and usage of data underpinned by proper governance frameworks.

b. Developing the system-level roles and responsibilities that agencies need to play, as part of the broader data value chain perspective.

c. Capability building for effective implementation (e.g. establish centres of excellence to drive though leadership, establish funding principles and resource allocation).

d. Integrating the Policy-Tech "handshake" with Government Technology Agency colleagues to ensure the ecosystem architecture and data products support policy objectives.

Stakeholder Engagement. Work closely with agencies to understand their use cases and governance context, and drive implementation. Provide advice on policies and measures, including arbitrating between competing needs where necessary.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape policy and drive change implementation across the public sector, with significant impact on how Government agencies access and use data effectively and responsibly for policy analysis, service delivery and operations.

The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

jobDescription:
The Research Team under the Child Development division plays a cross-cutting role to develop and drive ECDA’s research strategy, by coordinating research initiatives, partnerships, and knowledge translation activities that support evidence-based policy development and practice improvements across Singapore's early childhood sector. 

As an Assistant Director in the Research Team, you will lead a team to work closely with MSF and ECDA Divisions, other government departments, relevant research agencies/institutes and preschools to inform evidence based early childhood policies, programmes and practices. This role supports ECDA’s efforts to push for quality preschools through a sustained focus on research to build up knowledge, establish strategic partnerships with the research community and more effectively translate research to policy and practice.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be responsible for developing and implementing ECDA’s research strategy, which includes
the following: 

•	Develop research priorities and build knowledge base on early childhood-related research – to establish ECDA’s research priorities and lines of inquiry, synthesize local and international research to identify policy-relevant insights and practice implications. Build and maintain a repository of research relevant to ECDA’s needs. 
•	Strategic engagement of research community and experts – to engage and forge partnerships with research entities/Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to conduct research or provide expert opinions on ECDA’s research priorities. This can include managing panels of experts to provide guidance and insights.
•	Translate research to inform policy and practices – translate research into resources and platforms that can inform policy (e.g. horizon scans) and practice in the Early Childhood sector (e.g. guides, frameworks). Develop a publications agenda to share and promote relevant research with preschools and educators to drive the accessibility of evidence-based practices.
•	Drive and implement research initiatives aligned with ECDA's strategic priorities and policy needs – to coordinate multi-phase research projects with internal and external stakeholders, manage research project timelines and deliverables and steer project to ensure alignment with ECDA’s needs. Research initiatives include, but are not limited, to the evaluation of innovative pilots and programmes, and implementing measures of holistic child outcomes
•	Provide secretariat support for inter-agency meetings relating to research. 
•	Undertake any other additional tasks and duties as assigned.

-	A relevant tertiary qualification e.g., social sciences, education, psychology, economics, sociology, public policy or field with strong research methodology components.

About the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore 
Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription: We are seeking a Cybersecurity Consultant to conduct horizon scanning and AI security assessments. The successful candidate will participate in assessing new security and threat developments in the AI landscape, conduct security assessment of AI, and participate in Whole-of-Government (WoG) forums to provide technical advice on AI security risks, mitigation strategies, and best practices. This role requires a good understanding of AI technologies, cybersecurity principles, and risk management methodologies. The Consultant will also collaborate with other government agencies and industry partners to develop coordinated approaches to AI security challenges, while staying at the forefront of global AI security trends and regulatory developments.
jobResponsibilities:
Responsibilities

•	Developing methodologies for assessing security risks of AI systems and designing robust security architectures for AI systems 
•	Conducting hands-on security testing and assessments of AI systems and components, identifying vulnerabilities and potential attack vectors
•	Developing technical guidance for the secure adoption of AI technologies, providing recommendations to de-risk AI adoption for government agencies, critical information infrastructures Owners and enterprises.
•	Collaborating with cross-functional teams, government agencies and industry partners through developing and implementing coordinated approaches to address AI security challenges.
jobRequirements:
Requirements
•	Relevant qualifications and experience in cybersecurity and AI security (e.g., ML, GenAI, Agentic AI).
•	Possession of a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
•	Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, OSCP, SANS) and knowledge in security testing methodologies 
•	Working knowledge of threat modelling and threat risk assessments to identify attack paths and exploitation opportunities across AI systems and technologies
•	Provide practical cybersecurity guidance and engineering capabilities to support stakeholders in securing critical systems and emerging technologies
•	Good knowledge and hands-on experience of AI technologies (e.g., ML, GenAI, Agentic AI), including neural networks, deep learning, and reinforcement learning.
•	Familiarity with relevant AI security frameworks and standards (e.g., MITRE ATLAS, OWASP).
•	Strong problem-solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills
•	Strong communication skills and ability to explain complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
•	Possess experience working in cross-functional and interdisciplinary teams.

If you share our passion to make a difference in the cybersecurity ecosystem, take up the challenge and apply now.

All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

jobResponsibilities:
The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst will be responsible for identifying, tracking, and analysing emerging cyber threats, with a focus on protecting critical IT/OT systems in the land transportation sector. This role goes beyond passive news consumption and emphasises active threat research, transforming global threat data into localised, actionable monitoring strategies and detection logic.

Key Responsibilities

  • Intelligence Programme Development: Lead the development and continuous improvement of the Threat Intelligence (TI) function, including the implementation of of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and CTI solution for intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination.
  • Threat Research & Actor Tracking : Conduct proactive research into the Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) of threat actors, with particular focus on the Asia‑Pacific region and Industrial Control Systems (ICS).
  • Monitoring List Management : Curate, validate, and maintain high‑fidelity monitoring lists, including Indicators of Compromise (IOCs), for ingestion into SIEM, EDR, and Network Traffic Analysis tools.
  • Detection Engineering Support : Translate research findings into technical detection artefacts, such as YARA, Sigma, or Snort rules, to strengthen proactive threat hunting and detection capabilities.
  • Incident Response Integration : Act as the Tier- 3 intelligence lead during critical incidents, providing real‑time threat context, infrastructure pivoting, and attribution support to the CERT team.
  • Vulnerability Intelligence : Monitor and prioritise newly disclosed CVEs based on the organisation’s technology stack, providing actionable, risk‑based assessments to patching and infrastructure teams.
  • TTP Mapping : Map observed adversary behaviours to the MITRE ATT&CK framework to identify visibility gaps and areas for improvement in existing security controls.
  • Stakeholder Reporting : Produce high‑quality intelligence report/ update (including Flash Alerts) for emerging or imminent threats and monthly strategic summaries for management and public transport operators.

Technical Skills & Competencies

  • OSINT & Investigation - Strong capability in conducting open‑source investigations across surface, deep, and dark web sources, including forums, code repositories, and social media, to identify leaked credentials or planned threat campaigns.
  • Automation - Proficiency in scripting to build custom scrapers, automate Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) workflows, and manage large‑scale intelligence datasets.
  • Log Analysis - Ability to correlate threat intelligence with internal telemetry (e.g. proxy, firewall, EDR logs) to validate malicious activity and identify early indicators of compromise.
  • Framework Knowledge - Strong understanding of MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis, and Cyber Kill Chain.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology or related field.
  • At least 8 years of experience in cybersecurity, with at least 4 years in Threat Intelligence, Advanced SOC Operations, or Incident Response roles.
  • Education - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.
  • Professional Certifications - GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI) or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
  • Desired Technical Certifications - Relevant technical certifications such as GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH), GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA) or GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM) would be advantageous.
  • Demonstrated track record in mentoring junior analysts and uplifting SOC/CERT capabilities.
  • Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to brief senior leadership and executive stakeholders on complex cyber risk matters.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a cross‑matrix environment, as well as independently and decisively in a fast‑paced, high‑impact operational setting.

jobDescription: We would like to invite interested applicants to apply for the position of a Senior / Researcher (Economics) in the Research and Strategy Management Division (RSM) at the Ministry of National Development (MND). As part of a dynamic and multi-disciplinary research team, you will contribute to wider policy and planning efforts to ensure that Singapore remains An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City.
jobResponsibilities:
You will undertake economic research, using theory and empirical methods to deliver timely and incisive analytical insights that inform MND’s housing policies, and land use planning and development efforts. The increasingly complex nature of research questions will also require you to work closely with dedicated researchers that straddle the social sciences and data science. To this end, your role will entail the following:

•	Conceptualise, design, and execute research that informs policy and planning. This will involve primary data gathering (e.g. stated preference surveys), secondary data analysis using various empirical methods (e.g. econometrics/ quasi-experiment methods for causal analysis, structural estimation, time series, and machine-learning algorithms), and developing and managing platforms, such as recurring surveys and dashboarding tools. 

•	Conduct think pieces that thoroughly examine housing-related topics to inform policy and planning. This will involve applying economic theories to real-world scenarios to explain market dynamics and policy mechanisms, challenge existing assumptions and offer new perspectives, as well as identify societal implications and propose feasible policies/ solutions. 

•	Synthesise and present research insights to Policy Divisions and Senior Management. This will involve making sense of diverse data points and sources and where necessary, draw upon economic and behavioural theories, as well as academic and policy research, to meet practical policy and planning needs.

•	Engage colleagues and stakeholders to support research and non-research work in MND and the Government. This will involve building relationships with other divisions and agencies, and academia, and meeting administrative and functional needs in RSM and MND, such as secretariat duties.
jobRequirements:

•	Experience and ability to utilise data analytics tools to prepare and analyse data (e.g. R or Python).
•	Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including translating and presenting research findings to address policy and planning needs.
•	Proactive, curious, resourceful, with good attention to detail; able to work independently and collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary team and manage diverse stakeholders.
