jobDescription: You will be responsible for driving service experience research, prototyping, and cross-MOM collaboration to support MOM's service delivery transformation. Working in the department’s Experience Design Unit (XD), you will plan and conduct user research and service journey mapping, build prototypes that are anchored on research insights, plan and execute experiments to test the effectiveness of potential solutions. Such solutions include both include digital and non-digital ones. You will be required to collaborate strongly with internal stakeholders, through regular engagements with our partners, planning and facilitating co-creation workshops to generate shared understanding and collaborative solutions across MOM divisions. The ideal candidate should be naturally curious about customer behaviour and mental models across MOM's service delivery channels and passionate about collaborating with internal stakeholders to drive customer-centric service transformation.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Plan and conduct comprehensive service experience research including discovery and sensemaking activities, using qualitative and quantitative methodologies to identify service gaps and opportunities for improvement.
•	Develop and maintain service journey maps across customer touchpoints, analyse customer feedback data from various sources, and translate research insights into evidence-based recommendations for service and digital experience improvements.
•	Lead prototype development by translating research findings into testable solutions including digital wireframes, service processes, and communication materials, then design and execute testing methodologies with target user groups to iterate and refine prototypes.
•	Drive cross-MOM collaboration by facilitating scoping and engagement meetings, designing and running co-creation workshops with stakeholders across divisions, and supporting dialogue to cultivate shared commitment to transformation outcomes.
•	Manage multiple cross-functional projects simultaneously to deliver transformational initiatives that advance MOM's service delivery goals.
jobRequirements:
•	Relevant experience in service design, user experience research, service journey mapping or blueprinting, prototyping, or digital transformation, preferably in customer experience and service delivery functions, with 2-5 years of experience in a similar capacity preferred.
•	Proficiency in user research methods, data analysis from multiple sources, and statistical methods to inform strategic decision-making
•	Some knowledge of /experience in cognitive science, psychology or information science to inform user-centred approaches
•	Strong project management skills with ability to partner with cross-functional teams and manage stakeholder relationships
•	Experience in prototyping (including using prototyping tools and programmes) usability testing, gathering user feedback, and iterating designs based on validation outcomes
•	Excellent communication skills to facilitate workshops, present findings persuasively, and influence collaboration across stakeholder groups
•	Strong empathy for MOM customers with ability to translate customer needs into actionable design recommendations
•	Problem-solving mindset with ability to work effectively amidst cross-cutting issues and drive iterative enhancement with a results-driven approach

jobDescription:
Victims of online harm often have no effective way to stop the harm, especially where perpetrators act anonymously online. The Online Safety Project Office has been newly set up to establish a regime that better protects victims by providing timely, effective and accessible means of relief.

SAR is the team within the Office responsible for reconsideration, appeals and other specialised casework. It supports victims in matters such as helping identify perpetrators of online harm, and helps ensure that Office’s decisions are robust, properly reviewed, and able to withstand scrutiny.
jobResponsibilities:
• Handling applications by victims for end-user identity information (EUI) of perpetrators of online harm
  • Handling applications for reconsideration of decisions
  • Assisting in matters relating to appeals against decisions
  • Establishing relevant standard operating procedures
  • Developing, maintaining, and managing a registry for EUI, reconsideration, and appeals
  • Working with different stakeholders to strengthen online safety
  • Managing knowledge management of the Office’s work
jobRequirements:
• Background in Law, Public Policy, Regulatory Affairs, or related field with strong understanding of legal frameworks
  • Able to operate at the frontier of a new regime, develop frameworks for untested situations and have the confidence to make principled decisions on matters without precedent.
  • Experience in case management, appeals administration, or regulatory compliance within digital safety or telecommunications sectors
  • Strong analytical skills with ability to interpret complex legal matters and provide sound policy recommendations
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills with experience working across internal and external parties on sensitive regulatory matters
  • Knowledge of online safety regulations, digital harm prevention, and the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act would be highly advantageous

jobResponsibilities:
The Active Mobility Group develops, promotes and regulates the use of active mobility (cycling, riding personal mobility devices, using personal mobility aids, and walking) as a key strategy in LTA’s Walk Cycle Ride vision. This includes overseeing the full value chain of activities from conceptualisation and planning to regulation and communications.

There are 5 main aspects of the Group’s work on Active Mobility:
i. Planning
ii. Infrastructure Design
iii. Promotion and Engagement
iv. Regulatory Policy
v. Device Sharing
vi. Active Mobility Device Import Control

We seek a dynamic individual with strong analytical and communication skills, and an interest in walking, cycling, transport and urban planning. You will be working on the planning of Active Mobility infrastructure (e.g. cycling path, bicycle parking, end-of-trip facilities) to encourage walking, cycling and using of personal mobility device as a green, healthy and enjoyable way to travel. You will work closely with other government agencies to develop the plans and provide planning advice for both ongoing and future developments, to ensure active mobility infrastructure is well integrated with the development and urban surroundings. In addition, you will design, plan and supervise data collection strategies and activities, analyse the data to inform planning, and interpret survey results. You will also have opportunities to organise and coordinate events to generate public mindshare and promote active mobility.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge preferably in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Economics, Geography, Engineering System Design, Transport Engineering, Transport Planning, Town/Urban Planning, or a related discipline.
• Those with relevant experience in urban and transport planning as well as strong analytical capabilities can be considered for a more senior position.
• Experience, knowledge or research on both local and overseas planning of Active Mobility infrastructure will be an advantage
• Experience in ArcGIS, Microstation / AutoCAD will be preferred
• Experience in land use planning, transport planning and transport modelling simulation techniques, and knowledge of pedestrian and cyclist demand modelling and simulation tools will be an advantage
• Excellent communication and writing skills

We value qualities such as professionalism, initiative, passion and quality service in all aspects of interaction with both internal and external customers which will make this role even more enjoyable.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

jobDescription:
About SAFCo

The Singapore Sustainable Aviation Fuel Company (SAFCo) is a mission-driven entity supporting Singapore’s national SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) policy. SAFCo manages SAF levy collection, procures SAF to meet regulated demand, and develops the voluntary SAF market. As a lean and agile startup, SAFCo is building foundational capabilities to ensure operational excellence, transparency, and credibility in the SAF ecosystem.

Role overview

This role reports to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of SAFCo. The Head of Technology / Enterprise Architect will lead SAFCo’s end-to-end technology, data, and cybersecurity capabilities. This role is critical to ensuring that SAFCo’s systems, data, and digital infrastructure are scalable, secure, auditable, and aligned with regulatory requirements, while enabling efficient operations and future growth.
jobResponsibilities:
Enterprise Architecture & System Design

  • Define and own SAFCo’s overall enterprise architecture across core systems (e.g. SEAMS/repository, ERP/finance, levy operaqtions, external integrations), ensuring clear system boundaries and data ownership.

  • Design and oversee end‑to‑end system integration across SAFCo’s ecosystem, including APIs, data flows, and synchronisation across multiple internal and external platforms.

  • Develop and maintain SAFCo’s technology roadmap, balancing immediate operational needs with long‑term scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency.

  • Translate policy, regulatory, and operational requirements into robust system architecture and design principles.

Systems Implementation & Integration

  • Lead implementation and configuration of SAFCo’s core systems (ERP, registry/SEAMS, reporting systems).

  • Oversee system integration across finance, levy operations, SAF transactions, and external counterparties.

  • Act as SAFCo’s technology lead, responsible for implementing and integrating ERP systems, SEAMS/repository, financial reporting tools, and procurement systems.

  • Manage integration of SEAMS/ with external SAF registries and ensure interoperability with SAFCo’s internal systems.

  • Drive digital transformation initiatives to strengthen SAFCo’s technology ecosystem and operational efficiency.

  • Establish testing, release management, and change control processes.

  • Ensure system delivery is fit-for-purpose and aligns with business needs.

Data Governance, Management & Analytics

  • Define SAFCo’s data architecture, including key data entities (e.g. SAF volumes, environmental attributes, levy, payments) and “single source of truth” principles.

  • Establish data governance frameworks covering data lineage, access controls, segregation of duties, and data quality assurance.

  • Ensure all critical data and reporting outputs are auditable, traceable, and compliant with regulatory and governance requirements.

  • Oversee development of reporting and analytics capabilities to support operational management, financial reporting, and stakeholder transparency.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish and oversee SAFCo’s cybersecurity framework, including access controls, encryption, monitoring, and vulnerability management.

  • Define cybersecurity risk posture and ensure appropriate controls are embedded across all systems and processes.

  • Ensure compliance with CAAS cybersecurity, data protection, and governance requirements, including audit readiness.

  • Develop and oversee incident response, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities for critical systems.

Vendor & Technology Governance

  • Manage and oversee all technology vendors (ERP, registry, integration, cybersecurity providers), ensuring delivery against contractual, technical, and performance requirements.

  • Establish governance structures and stakeholder forums to ensure alignment across SAFCo, CAAS, and external partners.

  • Drive disciplined vendor management, including cost optimisation, performance monitoring, and risk management.

  • Ensure SAFCo retains ownership of architecture, data, and system logic, avoiding over‑reliance or lock‑in to any single vendor.

Strategic Leadership & Execution

  • Provide strategic direction on SAFCo’s digital, technology, and data capabilities, while remaining hands‑on in design and delivery.

  • Partner closely with internal stakeholders (Operations, Finance, Procurement, Sustainability) to ensure alignment between policy intent, operational processes, and system implementation.

  • Lead and build a lean, high‑performing technology capability (internal and/or external), with clear accountability and delivery outcomes.

  • Support Board and CAAS discussions with clear, structured, and fact‑based inputs on technology strategy, risks, investments, and trade‑offs.
jobRequirements:
Experience:

  • 15 – 20 years of experience in technology, systems, or digital roles, preferably in energy, aviation, trading, or other regulated industries.

  • Proven track record in delivering large‑scale system implementations (e.g. ERP, SAP, ETRM, or equivalent) and integrating complex business processes across multiple systems.

  • Experience in leading enterprise‑wide digital or technology strategy, including multi‑year roadmaps, system modernisation, and cloud / platform adoption.

  • Strong experience in vendor management, system integration, and governance across multi‑stakeholder environments.

Skills:

  • Strong enterprise architecture and system design capability, with ability to connect business processes, data, and systems end‑to‑end.

  • Deep understanding of system integration (APIs, data flows), data governance, cybersecurity, and technology risk management.

  • Ability to translate business and regulatory requirements into scalable and auditable system solutions.

  • Strong project execution capability, including Agile/DevOps delivery, testing, and change management

Why Join SAFCo?

  • Be part of a pioneering team shaping Singapore’s sustainable aviation future.

  • Grow your career in a dynamic, purpose-driven startup.

  • Work closely with leadership and contribute to high-impact initiatives.

SCP also manages our engagement with the Board of Directors and our parent ministry, MTI.

The CP team plays a pivotal role in translating long-term strategy into actionable short- to medium-term plans, ensuring organisation-wide alignment and enabling the delivery of STB’s strategic priorities. You will work very closely with the Strategic Planning team which will plan for the longer term.

Focus areas of the CP team include:

1. Corporate Planning: Lead the corporate planning cycle by setting direction, engaging with internal business units, and shaping short- to medium-term workplans.

jobDescription:
[What the role is]

STB takes a data-driven approach in tourism planning and marketing, and at the heart of it is Stan (Singapore Tourism Analytics Network, Stan), a tourism data analytics platform that allows both internal STB users and external tourism industry stakeholders to access tourism data and derive actionable insights about Singapore's tourism landscape and visitors.

As Data and AI Product Manager, you will play a pivotal role in building the data product roadmap for STB and its industry stakeholders to drive tourism growth. You'll be at the forefront of leveraging data and AI to transform Singapore's tourism industry, not just defining what needs to be built, but getting hands-on to prove it works before it scales. Success in this position means delivering data and AI-enabled products that measurably enhance tourism decision-making capabilities, with demonstrated user adoption, stakeholder satisfaction, and measurable business impact on Singapore's tourism sector.

This role sits within the newly established Data Exploration and Partnerships department, reporting directly to the Head of Department, and works closely with line units across Singapore Tourism Board, government agencies, and industry partners to drive data-driven decision-making and insights generation in tourism.
jobResponsibilities:
[What you will be working on]

As a Data and AI Product Manager, your key responsibilities include:

1. Data Products Roadmap Development, Planning and Execution:

a) Develop and execute the data product roadmap, defining data products required by STB and industry stakeholders, and aligned with STB's organisational goals.

b) Create and maintain comprehensive data products requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and test cases.

c) Develop mock and/or POC dashboards and datasets, to support requirements specifications and acceptance criteria.

d) Work with Stan product team to plan and implement the data products onto Stan.

e) Support testing and production verification as part of productisation process.

f) Lead product launches and go-to-market plans for major releases of data products.

g) Drive innovation in data products, constantly seeking ways to enhance value for stakeholders.

h) Proactively identify opportunities for new data products or features based on industry trends and stakeholder needs.

2. AI Roadmap, Use Cases and Proof-of-Concept Development

a) Ideate and develop the AI roadmap for STB's data platforms, identifying high-value AI use cases that enhance data accessibility and user productivity for internal and industry stakeholders.

b) Prioritise AI roadmap items using sound evaluation frameworks that weigh feasibility, impact, and implementation readiness.

c) Lead hands-on development of AI proof-of-concepts, starting with natural language query (NLQ) for conversational access to STB's datasets and analytics.

d) Design evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and test cases for AI features, ensuring reliability, accuracy, and appropriateness before productisation.

e) Identify and shape AI use cases in close collaboration with line units, translating domain needs into technically grounded AI applications.

f) Work closely with the product implementation team to ensure AI PoCs are documented and specified to a standard that enables direct handover for productisation.

g) Stay current on applied AI developments relevant to data platforms, analytics, and public sector use cases.

3. Requirements Gathering and Product Design:

a) Conduct deep dives into business scenarios, use cases, user journey mapping as part of data and AI product solution design.

b) Translate complex stakeholder needs into clear, actionable product requirements and specifications.

c) Collaborate with Data Partnerships and Stan product team to ensure product feasibility and technical alignment.

d) As part of data and AI product design and specifications, review the end-to-end processes involved in implementing and maintaining the data products, ensure processes are streamlined and efficient.

e) Leverage digital and automation tools where possible as part of the end-to-end process design i.e. WOG tools like FormSG and Plumber to automate data collection and simple data validation checks.

4. Data Governance and Quality Management for Industry-facing data domains:

a) Ensure adherence to data governance policies for data integrity, security, and compliance.

b) Support data quality management processes, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of data products as part of productisation process.

c) Apply appropriate guardrails and evaluation criteria to AI features to ensure outputs meet governance and quality standards.

5. Stakeholder Management and Communication:

a) Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across STB line units, government agencies, and industry partners, with varying levels of data and tech maturity.

b)Translate complex data and AI concepts into clear, structured communications for non-technical stakeholders, facilitating understanding and buy-in.

c) Drive alignment and clarity across stakeholders, ensuring well-defined problem statements, expectations, and outcomes.

d) Collaborate cross-functionally to ensure alignment between product development, business needs, and technical capabilities.

e) Facilitate structured discussions and decision-making, especially in ambiguous or exploratory problem spaces.

6. Analytics, Experimentation and Continuous Improvement:

a) Support data pilots in identifying and solving complex data-related problems, applying critical thinking and analytical skills.

b) Support data pilots in advanced analytics, data integration and data wrangling needs.

c) Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for data products implemented.

d) Analyze usage pattern, stakeholder feedback and performance metrics to inform continuous improvement.
jobRequirements:

The ideal candidate is formally trained in Business, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with at least 3–5 years of experience in data product management, data engineering, or related roles with a proven track record of delivering data-driven solutions.

jobDescription:
Project : Designing Self-Service & Automation Solutions for Innovation Data Lab Workflows

This internship project aims to modernise and streamline the operations of the Data Lab by reducing manual workload on duty officers and improving the overall researcher experience. The intern will explore, design, and prototype a suite of self-service and automation solutions across the researcher journey.
jobResponsibilities:
- Explore AI-powered chatbot solutions to handle routine queries, reducing the burden on duty officers, based on a set of researcher-facing FAQs. The intern will also develop an onboarding video accompanying acknowledgement form for new researchers to complete at their own pace. 
- Explore the use of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) or other automation tools to streamline end-of-session PC wipe downs. This includes developing a script to automatically clear browsing history, recent files, and application data across all relevant programmes.
- Develop an AI-assisted script to automatically scan and flag microdata in researcher input and output files, reducing the need for manual checks by officers.
- Prototype an AI-powered tool to assist officers in reviewing researcher submissions of project findings for publication/dissemination. The tool should be able to summarise papers and slides, validate analytical results against approved output files, and flag sections that cannot be automatically verified — allowing officers to focus their manual review efforts more efficiently.
jobRequirements:
- Knowledge or experience in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Accountancy, Actuarial Science or subjects with substantial quantitative content
- Knowledge of Python or similar scripting languages for automation and file-checking tasks. 
- Familiarity with AI and natural language processing (NLP) concepts would be advantageous, particularly for the chatbot and paper verification components. 
- Some experience with RPA tools (such as UiPath or Power Automate) would be helpful for the PC session management component. Basic understanding of data handling and file management is also expected.
- The intern should be comfortable reading and interpreting analytical outputs, such as statistical results in research papers, in order to support the paper and slides verification component.

Required Duration: Jul/Aug 2026 to Dec 2026/Jan 2027 [Min. 24 weeks]
Part Time Option Available (Min. 3 days a week)

jobDescription: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. jobResponsibilities:
As a Lead Engineer / Engineer in the AI Security & Safety team, you will be at the forefront of operationalizing secure AI for the Home Team. Reporting to the Head of AI Security & Safety, you will act as the technical builder and operator, responsible for engineering, integrating, and deploying AI security products (e.g., LLM guardrails, vulnerability scanners) into enterprise environments.

This role will also include applying tools for supporting the automation and execution of testing, evaluation, validation, and verification lifecycle for AI models. The scope of tests includes rigorous adversarial robustness testing and systematic benchmarking to provide critical assurance to various stakeholders that deployed AI systems remain safe, reliable, and resilient against evolving threats. You will bridge the gap between AI innovation and enterprise security engineering, ensuring AI applications are "Secure by Design".
jobRequirements:
•	AI Model Test, Evaluate, Validate, Verify: Design and conduct systematic tests to evaluate AI model safety, security, and performance. This includes researching and applying various security/safety test domains, industry benchmarks, and advanced evaluation methodologies (e.g., benchmark based evaluations, LLM-as-a-Judge, etc).
•	Adversarial Robustness Testing: Conduct targeted adversarial testing (e.g., prompt injection, data poisoning, model inversion) on in-house and commercial AI models to identify vulnerabilities and edge-case failures, directly contributing towards and supporting the CISO office's risk assessment processes.
•	Product Engineering & Integration: Design, develop, and integrate AI security tools (e.g., input/ output guardrails, real-time monitoring sidecars) into existing AI inference pipelines and API gateways.
•	Enterprise Deployment: Deploy and manage AI security solutions across both Cloud (e.g., Government Commercial Cloud - GCC) and On-Premise containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes), while pushing the frontier of complex trade-off between ensuring high availability, low latency, and security.
•	DevSecOps for AI: Automate TEVV workflows and integrate AI vulnerability scanners and benchmarking tools into the organization’s CI/CD pipelines to ensure continuous security testing.
•	Threat Mitigation: Work closely with application developers, data scientists, project managers, and cloud engineers to understand use cases translating into design and implementation of robust mitigating controls and secure configurations across the end-to-end AI lifecycle (pre-training, fine-tuning, RAG, and inference).

•	Experience: Minimum 2 to 5 years in Software Engineering, DevSecOps, AI/ Machine Learning Engineering, or Cybersecurity.
•	AI Testing & Evaluation: Good understanding of AI evaluation frameworks, benchmarking datasets, and methodologies for qualitatively and quantitatively measuring model performance and safety (e.g., LLM-as-a-Judge, automated test case generation).
•	Software Engineering: Strong programming skills in Python, Go, or similar languages, with experience building and consuming APIs securely.
•	Cloud & Containerization: Hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and deploying workloads in both Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCC) and On-Premise environments.
•	AI/ML Knowledge: Familiarity with the AI development lifecycle, ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow), and LLM inference engines (e.g., vLLM, HuggingFace).
•	Cybersecurity Expertise: Knowledge of AI-specific threat frameworks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS) and traditional application security principles.
•	Certifications (Preferred): Relevant certifications in Cloud, DevSecOps, AI/ Machine Learning, or Cybersecurity.
•	Attributes:
o	Ability to multi-task and deliver high-quality engineering work under tight deadlines.
o	Meticulous in planning, test design, documentation, and system architecture.
o	A strong team player with excellent interpersonal and communication skills to engage cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., application developers, data scientists, governance teams).
o	Demonstrates resiliency, drive, and a continuous learning mindset to keep pace with the rapidly evolving AI threat landscape.

All new appointees are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure overtime, based on performance.

jobDescription:
The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and advances Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena.

Climate change is one of the defining issues of our time. It is a complex global challenge that calls for concerted international action and collaboration between governments, industry and individuals. As a low-lying city state, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change and has a strong interest in shaping effective global climate action. 

The Green Economy and Sustainability (GES) team sits within MTI’s International Trade Division, which is charged with formulating Singapore’s foreign economic policy and advancing Singapore’s economic interests in the internationally. The GES team leads Singapore’s international economic engagement on green trade issues. We also work closely with agencies, such as MSE, MOF, NEA and PMO(NCCS), to formulate and coordinate strategies to chart the path forward for Singapore’s transition to a low-carbon economy.
jobResponsibilities:
As a TIER officer in the International Trade (GES) Division in the Ministry of Trade and Industry, you will be part of a high-performing team operating at the forefront of international economic diplomacy and climate policy, shaping the rules and frameworks that will define the global green economy. You will work on one or more of the following work streams: 

a.	Negotiation of Article 6.2 bilateral/plurilateral agreements. Develop and implement strategies and policies to strengthen bilateral cooperation with like-minded countries on carbon credits aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. Officer will negotiate binding bilateral and plurilateral agreements with foreign governments, drive technical cooperation initiatives, and build robust project development pipelines — directly contributing to Singapore's ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

b.	Global carbon market rules and standards setting. Monitor and analyse evolving global carbon market developments and develop strategies to actively shape the international rules and standards that govern high-integrity carbon markets, positioning Singapore as a credible and influential voice in this space.

c.	Green trade policy development. Synthesise geopolitical, trade, and climate trends to craft Singapore's green trade policy agenda, safeguarding the country's long-term economic competitiveness through the low-carbon transition. The officer’s work will directly inform how Singapore positions itself in an increasingly climate-conscious global trading environment.

d.	Green trade instruments negotiation. Negotiate international instruments across multilateral, plurilateral, and bilateral fronts to advance Singapore's green trade interests. Officer will work with Ministries across the government to tackle complex, cross-cutting issues spanning environmental goods, services and investments, trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), environmental attribute certificates (EACs), and sectoral areas such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green buildings.


e.	Multilateral negotiations. Represent Singapore at the highest levels of international climate diplomacy, including at the UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP). You will advocate for Singapore's green economy and low-carbon interests, building coalitions and influencing outcomes that have real-world consequences for global climate action.

As the climate space is fast evolving, an officer may be deployed across different workstreams, based on the officer’s development and MTI’s organisational needs.
jobRequirements:
•	Experience in cross-cultural negotiations and international relations, particularly in the public sector; and/or 
•	Good knowledge in carbon credits/markets and Paris Agreement; and/or 
•	Good knowledge of green trade related issues including trade-related climate measures, environmental attributes certifications and sectoral issues that sits at the intersection of trade and climate.
•	Relevant experience in climate change/sustainability areas in the private sector, and/or non-government organisations – experience in carbon markets or other environmental goods/commodities is an advantage. Prior experience working on climate change/sustainability areas in the public sector will be perceived favourably

ASEAN – Where Proximity, Policies, Partners, and People Intersect

Position Overview: Trade Negotiator and Economic Policy Officer

Proximity: As we prepare for the future economy, the ASEAN region offers exciting growth opportunities. To enable our businesses and jobholders to seize these opportunities, MTI’s ASEAN Division advances Singapore’s economic interests and deepens regional economic integration at the ASEAN platform. Specifically, we seek to boost flows of goods, services, investments, data, people and ideas to strengthen the broader regional economic ecosystem.

Policies: Our team negotiates/reviews regional Agreements at the ASEAN platform to lower tariffs, address non-tariff barriers, improve trade facilitation, grow services flows, enhance the digital ecosystem, and address sustainability challenges amongst others, to improve the ease of doing business and harness the potential of emerging opportunities. Beyond Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), we also develop new initiatives and forms of cooperation to expand economic space through engagement, capacity building, and collaboration.

Partners: We nurture and work with partners to drive and champion deepening economic integration through the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC), a key trading partner and investment destination for Singapore. Beyond the 10 ASEAN Member States, the AEC provides opportunities for Singapore-based businesses to take advantage of ASEAN’s Agreements and initiatives with various external partners to facilitate their exports, investments and business activities. ASEAN’s suite of partners includes Australia, Canada, China, the European Union, India, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, and the United States, amongst others. To ensure businesses can benefit, we also engage stakeholders such as business councils and research institutions to increase awareness and understanding. 

People: Our team invests in building human capital. We have a unique opportunity to represent Singapore at Free Trade Agreement negotiations, analyse key developments and their potential implications, and take ownership for driving meaningful outcomes. Trade officers in MTI’s ASEAN Division develop technical competencies in either the domain of goods or the domain of digital economy, services, and investment. They gain experience in negotiations, public policy writing, and strategy development, including developing ideas to advance integration under the AEC and how Singapore should engage ASEAN on the economic track amidst a challenging global economic environment. jobDescription:
The Strategic Planning (SP) team is looking for a passionate officer to be part of a dynamic team to chart the way forward for the tourism sector. You will be part of a team that will identify opportunities, risks, and formulate mid- to long-term strategies to define the next phase of tourism growth as part of our Tourism 2040 (T2040) roadmap.

You will be an economic analyst working within STB Strategic Planning team, with a focus on developing economic impact analysis, projection and forecasting models and scenario planning. These include for instance, modelling the impact of international developments to Singapore’s tourism sector, forecasting our near to long term tourism performance, and analysing key trends, drivers and contributors.

SP also develops, reviews and tracks organisational performance to ensure alignment with STB's strategic outcomes and importantly, works with senior management to define STB's and the tourism industry’s aspirations and goals.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Work with Government agencies (MTI, MND/URA) and STB’s Analytics and Insights (A&I) team to analyse our past tourism performance and conduct both near and long-term projections of our tourism performance. Review and recommend planning assumptions for various scenarios to ensure the robustness of the projection methodologies.

2. Work with MTI and STB’s Analytics and Intelligence (A&I) to conduct economic impact analysis of specific policy changes on the tourism sector. The officer must be able to recommend the appropriate economic modelling/ frameworks, propose assumptions and review different methodologies.

3. Strengthen our analysis of drivers and contributors towards meeting our Tourism 2040 outcomes (TR, IVA and Productivity). This would include leading the analysis of Singapore’s competitiveness, vis-a-vis competitors.

4. Work with STB’s line units to set targets for key tourism performance metrics with the view of meeting our Tourism 2040 ambitions and ensure that these targets ultimately ladder up to the overall targets for the tourism sector.

5. In addition, officer will be part of the team to manage the following key workplans:

a) Prepare quarterly updates on key performance indicators, industry outlook, etc to MTI.

b) Work with MTI to manage key reporting platforms and updates for MTI senior management, as well as discussions on STB’s KPIs and priorities.

6. Beyond the immediate horizon, the officer will also need to think longer term to identify trends, blind spots, competition/ threats and/or new opportunities, which could potentially impact the future of Singapore tourism. This will involve working on “Futures Planning”, which will have the potential to significantly impact the outcomes of T2040.

[Key Relationships]

Within STB, you will be able to engage across all business teams and develop a keen understanding of the tourism landscape and its operating environment. You will also work closely with MTI and other government agencies, where you would be able to learn more about the work of other economic agencies and how their work is integrated to further Singapore's economic development.

jobDescription: The Senior / Geospatial Manager is a key member of the Geospatial Services team, driving geospatial capability building across Singapore. The team delivers geospatial solutions, analytics, data fusion and conversion services, and training programmes with the objective of deepening geospatial capabilities within Singapore's public and government sectors. jobResponsibilities:
As a Senior Geospatial Product Manager, you will lead the delivery of geospatial solutions and oversee the ongoing management of the ArcGIS Enterprise ecosystem. You will balance technical platform oversight with the structured management of complex, multi-stakeholder projects, while maintaining a strategic view of how the platform should evolve to meet the needs of the public sector. We are looking for a highly organised, process-driven professional who can drive high-impact geospatial solutions to government agencies and identify future opportunities — including the integration of AI and machine learning — to unlock deeper analytical value.

Key Responsibilities

Project & Product Delivery: Own the full project lifecycle with rigour — from initial requirements gathering and scoping through to final deployment — ensuring all geospatial solutions are fit for purpose, delivered on time, and within scope.

Platform Oversight & Administration: Oversee the technical management of the solutions on ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, including platform administration, user access control, content management, and configuration, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for government users.

Technical Consultation & Solutioning: Engage with senior stakeholders across the Healthcare, Social, Education, and Government sectors to translate organisational needs into structured geospatial workplans and clearly defined technical requirements, including identifying opportunities where AI can augment geospatial analysis and decision-making.

Solution Configuration: Drive the development and configuration of geospatial applications, applying your technical depth to solve spatial problems for agencies across the public sector.

Capability & Training: Lead the design and delivery of geospatial programmes and technical workshops, effectively upskilling both technical and non-technical audiences in modern GIS workflows and emerging AI-augmented geospatial capabilities.

Strategic Communication: Champion geospatial technology as a persuasive advocate, translating technical complexity into clear, value-driven business cases for senior management and decision-makers.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate is a technically grounded professional with 8 to 10 years of relevant experience, with a proven track record of bridging technical development and executive-level project and product management. A forward-looking awareness of how AI and machine learning are reshaping the geospatial landscape is strongly desired.

Technical Requirements & Expertise

ArcGIS Platform Knowledge: Advanced, hands-on experience with ArcGIS Enterprise Portal administration and configuration is mandatory. You should be deeply familiar with the ESRI suite, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated extension tools, as well as the ArcGIS API for Python for workflow automation.

Development & Automation: Proficiency in Python and JavaScript is required to drive automation and support geospatial solution development. Familiarity with R is an advantage.

Geospatial Analytics: A solid technical understanding of geospatial concepts, data fusion techniques, and advanced spatial analytical methods.

AI & Machine Learning Awareness: A working understanding of how AI and machine learning techniques can be applied in a geospatial context is highly desirable. This includes familiarity with spatial predictive modelling, automated feature extraction from imagery, or the use of Python-based AI/ML libraries. Hands-on experience in this area is a strong advantage, though candidates with a clear aptitude and willingness to develop these skills will also be considered.

Open Source: Experience with QGIS is considered a bonus.

Project Management & Leadership

Process-Driven Management: Strong organisational skills with demonstrated experience managing full project lifecycles and vendor relationships. A formal project management certification (such as PMP, etc) is highly advantageous.

Business Analysis: Strong skills in requirements gathering, solution scoping, and stakeholder alignment, ensuring that technical solutions are grounded in practical business needs.

Communication: Ability to produce compelling, high-quality presentation decks and articulate complex geospatial and AI concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders at all levels.

Collaborative Leadership: Proven ability to build and manage diverse, cross-functional working relationships across multiple government agencies and teams, driving delivery in a collaborative environment.

jobResponsibilities:
As a DevOps Consultant, you will play a key role in strengthening the architecture, automation and operational practices that support application development and deployment across cloud and on-premise environments. You will lead the implementation of CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, automated security checks and observability monitoring to improve deployment reliability, system resilience and operational readiness. Working closely with product, infrastructure, security and business teams, you will help ensure the Board’s digital services remain secure, reliable and future-ready, contributing to our broader mission of cyber resilience.

In this role, you will:
• Architect and manage cloud and on-premise infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code practices, including automated provisioning, configuration management and standardised deployment across environments.
• Design and enhance CI/CD pipelines to automate application build, testing, security scanning and deployment across the software delivery lifecycle.
• Drive DevSecOps adoption by embedding security controls, quality gates and release governance into delivery pipelines.
• Lead technical operations and release readiness, including change management, incident/problem management, capacity planning, configuration management and disaster recovery.
• Partner product, infrastructure and security teams to address deployment challenges, technical and operational constraints.
• Strengthen monitoring and observability capabilities through metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards to support proactive system operations.
• Engage stakeholders and senior management on DevOps roadmaps, infrastructure strategy, operational risks and implementation progress.
• Provide technical leadership and guidance on DevOps tooling, automation, cloud adoption, system resilience and operational excellence.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.
• Deep experience in solutioning and implementing backend systems and application infrastructure in an enterprise environment.
• Proven track record in managing the end-to-end software delivery lifecycle, from requirements gathering to production release.
• Extensive experience in developing and deploying backend systems on cloud platforms such as GCC, Azure or AWS, including hybrid cloud integration.
• Strong understanding of DevSecOps principles, Agile delivery practices and modern engineering ways of working, with experience managing DevSecOps toolchains.
• Expertise in CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, automated security checks and observability, using tools such as Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Terraform, SonarQube, AppScan, Kubernetes, Docker, Azure Monitor, Prometheus or Grafana.
• Deep experience in technical operations management, including production support, incident/problem management, root cause analysis, operational risk, resilience planning and disaster recovery.
• Proven ability to lead technical delivery teams and supervise DevOps consultants or engineers, including providing technical direction, mentoring, delivery oversight and driving team performance.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical matters for non-technical stakeholders and senior leadership.
• Analytical, self-driven and collaborative, with the ability to operate at an enterprise level, manage competing priorities and drive scalable, well-governed technology solutions.
• Ability to support emergency response and critical system updates outside office hours or on weekends when required.
 
The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on 2-year full time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into permanent position.

You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of fees setting and review, serving as the primary liaison with user groups to ensure fees are set optimally and reflect actual operational costs. Fees Management & Advisory

Analyse platform analytics to identify growth opportunities, audience insights, and content performance trends. Oversee content creation from ideation through production, ensuring alignment with platform-specific best practices and discovery mechanisms. Manage platform-specific initiatives including long and short-form video strategy, live content, community features, and content programmes.

Community Engagement Strategy & Development Design and implement comprehensive community engagement frameworks that foster authentic connections between STB and target audiences across VS social media presence. Develop community-building initiatives that encourage user-generated content, facilitate peer-to-peer recommendations, and create lasting emotional connections with Singapore as a destination. Establish metrics and measurement systems to track community health and engagement quality.

Emerging Platform Research & Strategy Continuously monitor emerging social platforms, closed community networks, and private social spaces to identify strategic opportunities for STB. Conduct platform assessments, audience analysis, and competitive research to determine viability and potential impact. Develop go-to-market strategies for promising platforms, including content approaches and community building tactics.

Technology Integration & Innovation Implementation Work with relevant teams to integrate new tools, platforms, and technologies that enhance community engagement and content creation capabilities. Stay current with AI developments, automation opportunities, and emerging social technologies including virtual production tools, automated content generation, and immersive storytelling technologies.

Innovation Project Leadership & Opportunity Identification Drive strategic innovation initiatives including AI-powered content creation, emerging technology integration, and experimental marketing approaches. Identify opportunities to innovate in areas such as virtual storytelling, automated content generation, immersive destination experiences, and next-generation audience engagement tools. Lead pilot programmes for cutting-edge marketing technologies and assess their potential for scalable implementation.

jobDescription:

SCP also manages our engagement with the Board of Directors and our parent ministry, MTI.

The CP team plays a pivotal role in translating long-term strategy into actionable short- to medium-term plans, ensuring organisation-wide alignment and enabling the delivery of STB’s strategic priorities. You will work very closely with the Strategic Planning team which will plan for the longer term.

Key areas of responsibility include:

1. Corporate Planning: Lead the corporate planning cycle by setting direction, engaging with internal business units, and shaping short- to medium-term workplans.

2. Performance Management: Drive target setting, monitor performance, and report on progress to ensure alignment with STB’s strategic outcomes. Collaborate with senior management to define both STB’s and the broader tourism industry’s aspirations and goals.

3. Ministry Engagement: Serve as STB’s primary deskhead for MTI, supporting ministry/WOG-level initiatives and facilitating coordination between STB and the ministry.

This role is ideal for you if you are keen to gain an overview of STB’s multi-faceted role in shepherding the growth of Singapore’s tourism sector, and to further develop core competencies such as corporate planning, analytical thinking, and stakeholder management.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of the Corporate Planning team, the officer will undertake, but not limited to, the following key responsibilities:

1. Lead the workstream on STB’s performance indicators and targets. The officer needs to be data-driven and regularly analyse STB’s performance through our corporate indicators, propose leading indicators, and set benchmarks based on STB’s strategies and priorities. Additionally, the officer will work with STB’s line units to seek alignment and monitor progress, organise timely, regular reviews of performance for senior management, develop and manage our annual reporting of targets and achievements to STB Board and MTI.

2. Work with relevant teams to set up the Management Dashboard on STB’s data analytics platform. The target users of the Management Dashboard are members of STB Management and line units. The officer must work closely with the technology teams to provide user needs on the desired visualisations and user experience.

3. Serve as STB’s deskhead for MTI, working with MTI to manage key reporting platforms and updates for MTI senior management, and discussions on STB’s KPIs and priorities. This includes maintaining oversight of ministry-level / whole-of-government requests and understanding the implications on STB’s planning and processes as a statutory board within the MTI-Family, as well as collating input and data across STB for ad-hoc initiatives.

4. Organise the annual corporate planning cycle for STB senior management and business units to formulate workplans in accordance with STB’s priorities. This involves the organisation of corporate planning discussions among management. The officer also needs to develop cogent and substantive guidance materials to help business units and market offices develop strong strategies for driving tourism performance.

5. In addition, officer will support industry engagement platforms such as the Tourism Industry Conference (TIC).

[Key Relationships]

Within STB, you will be able to engage across all business teams and develop a keen understanding of the tourism landscape and its operating environment. You will also work closely with MTI and other government agencies, where you would be able to learn more about the work of other economic agencies and how their work is integrated to further Singapore's economic development.

jobDescription:
The officer will play a key role in contributing to the success of the Singapore Grand Prix, a marquee annual event for Singapore that contributes significant economic and tourism benefits, and in raising the profile of destination Singapore. First held in 2008, the Singapore Grand Prix was the first night race in the FIA Formula One World Championship race calendar. It remains to be Asia’s only street circuit and night race.

STB is responsible for leading the Whole-of-Government effort to plan and execute this world class event in partnership with our race promoter Singapore GP Pte Ltd (SGP).
jobResponsibilities:
The officer will take on three key scope of work:

1. Circuit and Infrastructure. Plan and oversee the set-up of race-related infrastructure within the circuit in close partnership with Government agencies and race promoter SGP. This includes to:

  • Work closely with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to ensure the F1 track is compliant with FIA standards each year. With NS Square (the former Floating Platform) expected to be completed by 2027, the officer is also required to work closely with SGP to evaluate the current track design and incorporate NS Square in the circuit.

  • Work closely with the race promoter SGP to review the management of key Government assets (e.g., pit lane, race track lighting system and overpasses) to ensure these remain operationally ready each year. The officer will also work closely with LTA to facilitate the rental of the F1 track for events.

  • Represent the interests of STB and the Singapore Grand Prix as a project in national development projects which interface with the circuit such as NS Square.

2. Race Organising Committee (ROC). Facilitate good working relationships with stakeholders – race promoter SGP, national sporting association Motor Sport Singapore (MSS), and Sport Singapore, and recommend STB’s positions on key issues. The officer will also represent the Government’s position and interests in the ROC.

3. City Lighting (Aerial Filming). Facilitate F1's aerial filming requirements with race promoter SGP, key Government agencies such as the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and Singapore Police Force (SPF), and other stakeholders such as Swissotel etc.

Key relationships:

External: Race promoter SGP, Government agencies (especially SPF, LTA, and CAAS), and F1

Internal: Procurement, Finance, and Legal

Competency requirements:

  • Showing good business acumen, analytical thinking and judgement

  • Working effectively within STB to achieve results

  • Working effectively with stakeholders outside STB

  • Serving with heart, commitment and purpose

  • Being innovative and learning continuously

agencyDescription: The ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute is a regional research centre dedicated to the study of socio-political, security and economic trends and developments in Southeast Asia and its wider geostrategic and economic environment.
jobDescription:
The Wang Gungwu Visiting Fellows Programme honours Professor Wang Gungwu, former Chairman of the Board of Trustees at ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute (ISEAS) for his distinguished tenure of 17 years at the Institute.

The programme aims to build the next generation of scholars and policy makers exploring the nexus of big-power relations and its impact on Southeast Asia through policy relevant research on international politics and security, regional economics and digital technology, in the following priority areas of research:

1. Developments in US-China relations and their impact on Southeast Asia

2. Asia Pacific security issues (e.g. South China Sea, China-ASEAN relations)

3. Progress and prospects of global/regional economic cooperation initiatives (e.g. Belt and Road Initiative and Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership)

4. Rise of China and its impact on Southeast Asian communities

5. Use of digital media and technology by countries to further their interests and influence perceptions in Southeast Asian countries
jobResponsibilities:
Fellowships may be for a minimum of two (2) months and up to a period of six (6) months, subject to approval by ISEAS. Successful applicants are expected to be in residence at ISEAS for the duration of their fellowship.

Expected Outputs and Publication Opportunities

Wang Gungwu Visiting Fellows (WGWVF) are required to contribute to ISEAS Perspective and ISEAS Fulcrum publications in the areas of their research and speak at an in-house seminar on their research findings during their fellowship at ISEAS. As WGWVF, researchers will be part of a network of regional scholars and are welcome to contribute to ISEAS after their fellowship.

Stipend and Benefits

1. The Wang Gungwu Visiting Fellows Programme offers successful applicants a fixed monthly stipend (inclusive of a housing subsidy) for the duration of their fellowship at ISEAS and round-trip economy airfare between their home country and Singapore.

2. WGWVFs will be invited to a meeting with Professor Wang Gungwu during their fellowship, where possible.

3. Successful applicants will enjoy access to office space, computer equipment and IT services, ISEAS Library and other facilities at ISEAS, where appropriate.
jobRequirements:

agencyDescription:
"The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) was established on 2 February 1996, with the mission to develop Singapore as a premier global hub port and international maritime centre (IMC), and to advance and safeguard Singapore's strategic maritime interests.

MPA is the driving force behind Singapore's port and maritime development, taking on the roles of Port Authority, Port Regulator, Port Planner, IMC Champion, and National Maritime Representative.

MPA partners the industry and other agencies to enhance safety, security and environmental protection in our port waters, facilitate port operations and growth, expand the cluster of maritime ancillary services, and promote maritime R&D and manpower development."
jobDescription: The officer plays a key role towards the Whole-of-Government approach to detect and deter maritime security (MARSEC) threats in the Port of Singapore and Singapore Territorial Water (STW). This is particularly important as Singapore is strategically located at the convergence of key shipping routes around the world, with up to 70% of the world’s global maritime economy transiting through the Singapore Straits. Maritime Security is important to safeguard Singapore’s strategic maritime interest and maintains Singapore’s status as the premier hub port as well as the international maritime centre.
jobResponsibilities:
As a MPA representative, the officer will be seconded to Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC) full time and serve as a subject matter expert for shipping industry developments, commercial shipping practices, and national and international regulations governing the shipping industry. The officer will also be the key liaison between MPA departments and the seconded agency to ensure cross-agency initiatives are well communicated and executed. The officer will be required to support the conduct of exercises and workshops as well as training sessions/ visits/ seminars to enhance the Maritime organisation’s awareness and knowledge of the shipping industry.

• Representing MPA on maritime security issues with other government agencies at various committees, working groups, and taking turns to perform secretariat function for these working groups etc

• Part of the planning and execution team for the Whole-of-Government (WoG) maritime security operations for key coastal events, where the officer is required to be the MPA Liaison Officer and perform duties during these Maritime operations to ensure the security of major national events, which may fall on weekends and public holidays.

• Performing Duty Officer duties (12hrs duty both day and night shift at the Command Centre) on an average of 4 times per month to manage incidents and ensure smooth operations

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Data Analysts work closely with economists, research analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate data-driven insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Analyst in ED, you will help to shape manpower policies in Singapore through the application of data science, advanced analytics and clear policy communication.

You will use a range of data analytics techniques – including machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling, statistical analysis, data visualisation and other frontier data science approaches – to examine traditional and emerging issues relating to manpower policies and the labour market.

Your work will contribute to strengthening the evidence base for policymaking, uncovering new insights from complex datasets, and supporting better outcomes for workers, businesses and Singapore’s labour market.
Your responsibilities will include:

•	Applying advanced analytics to manpower policy issues
Use data science techniques to analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, skills mismatches, job transitions, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Developing new analytical approaches and datasets
Identify, process and analyse novel datasets, including structured and unstructured data, to generate new insights on labour market trends, policy issues and operational challenges.

•	Using frontier data science methods
Apply methods such as machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling and simulation techniques to support policy analysis and decision-making.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and policy monitoring
Develop indicators, dashboards and analytical tools to monitor labour market developments, workforce trends and emerging risks in a timely and policy-relevant manner.

•	Strengthening policy design and operational effectiveness
Work with policymakers and operational divisions to translate data insights into practical recommendations that improve policy design, programme implementation and operational outcomes.

•	Collaborating with economists and researchers
Work closely with economists, research analysts and external partners to combine data science techniques with economic theory, empirical research and policy domain knowledge.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, intuitive and policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using data science to improve public policy.

You should have:
•	A degree, Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Public Policy, or another quantitative discipline.
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to frame policy problems and translate them into data analytics projects.
•	Strong quantitative and technical skills, including experience in statistical analysis, machine learning, predictive modelling, text analytics, network analytics and/or data visualisation.
•	Proficiency in programming and data analytics tools such as Python, R, SQL, Stata or other relevant software.
•	Experience handling large, complex datasets, including structured and/or unstructured data.
•	A strong interest in public policy, labour market issues and applied data science.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly and logically to non-technical audiences.
•	The ability to work collaboratively with economists, researchers, policymakers, data specialists and operational teams.
•	A willingness to learn new methods, data sources and policy areas.

Candidates with experience in machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, causal inference, cloud-based analytics platforms, and/or dashboard development will have an advantage.

jobRequirements:

As a Lecturer in Industrial Automation, you will be responsible for delivering education in automation technologies, industrial control systems, and production digitalisation. Your expertise in programming industrial controllers (PLCs), designing Human Machine Interfaces (HMIs), and integrating smart sensors, vision systems, actuators, and motor drives will help students develop real-world automation solutions.

Additionally, you will teach industrial networking and IIoT (Industrial Internet of Things) technologies, including communication protocols such as OPC UA, enabling students to monitor machine performance and calculate Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE). Experience in implementing protection functions within Operational Technology (OT) environments will be highly valuable.

Beyond teaching, you will develop and assess assignments, mentor students, supervise final-year projects, and engage in industry collaborations to ensure students gain practical, industry-relevant experience.

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Develop and conduct lectures, tutorials, and hands-on workshops in industrial automation and control systems.

  • Teach PLC programming (IEC 61131-3), HMI development, and integration of smart sensors, cameras, actuators, and motor drives for automated systems.

  • Instruct students on connecting automation systems to Industrial IoT (IIoT) gateways using protocols like OPC UA for data collection and OEE calculations.

  • Provide practical training in industrial control networks, cybersecurity for OT environments, and digitalisation technologies.

  • Supervise and mentor students in final-year projects

  • Prepare and assess assignments, projects, quizzes, and tests, and maintain student records.

  • Support student learning through consultations and mentorship.

  • Train and prepare students for local and international competitions.

  • Involve in technology projects as a final year project supervisor, or as a member or principal investigator.

  • Identify and establish new collaboration opportunities with industry partners.

  • Manage course administration, including curriculum development and academic planning.

  • Organise and lead overseas study trips, immersion programs, and student exchange initiatives.
jobRequirements:
• A degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, or related disciplines.

  • At least 3 years of industry experience in industrial automation, PLC programming, and production digitalisation.

  • Experience in PLC IEC 61131-3, C/C++, or Python.

  • Knowledge of industrial networking, IIoT, RFID, PLC web servers, cybersecurity, and vision systems is highly desirable.

  • Passion for teaching, mentoring, and student development.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to develop engaging curriculum content and conduct hands-on training.

  • Commitment to staying updated with industry advancements and integrating new technologies into teaching.

jobDescription:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most pressing public health challenges of our time. As part of Singapore’s National Strategic Action Plan (NSAP) on AMR, this role sits at the heart of efforts to build a robust national AMR research agenda. You will work to deepen our understanding of AMR – its emergence, spread, drivers and risk factors – and translate research evidence into actional insights that inform policy across the pillars of the NSAP.
You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.

The Candidate will assist in building the national AMR research agenda through
(a) Regular monitoring the local research landscape to track research on antimicrobial resistance and appropriate antimicrobial use;
(b) Identifying priority research needs that support the development of local policies and practices to mitigate the threat of AMR;
(c) Exploring funding platforms and administering programmes to support such research.
jobResponsibilities:
Research and Policy

  • Map and monitor the local AMR research landscape on a regular basis to track progression in AMR research and developments.
  • Identify priority research needs that support the development of local policies and practices to mitigate AMR, in partnership with relevant stakeholders.
  • Explore funding platforms and opportunities, and assist with the implementation and administration of programmes that support AMR research.
  • Engage and partner local and international scientific community to advance the agenda for AMR research.
  • Research priority AMR issues as they arise on an ad-hoc basis, and communicate findings and information clearly to stakeholders.

Secretariat and Administrative Duties

  • Facilitate and support the work of committees, including providing administrative support for meetings, taking minutes and preparing meeting-related materials.
  • Monitor, collect, collate and report progress of work plan implementation.
  • Undertake administrative tasks as needed to support division’s operations, including but not limited to procurement, finance, records management.

Please note that secretariat and administrative duties form a meaningful part of this role alongside the research and policy work.

  • Produce clear recommendation reports for the product and leadership team.

Platform & Cross-Channel Testing

Data Analysis & Insights

jobResponsibilities:
You will play a key role in safeguarding the cybersecurity of vehicles on Singapore's roads. Analyse technical evidence, assess the scope and severity of incidents, and determine whether manufacturers have fulfilled their obligations under applicable regulations. Technical testing may be conducted on a case-by-case basis to support findings.

Familiarity with the following will be advantageous:

  • Automotive cybersecurity standards, including ISO/SAE 21434, ISO 27001, and UN Regulations No. 155 & 156.

  • Embedded security concepts such as HSM, Secure Boot, and SecOC, along with vehicle communication protocols (e.g., CAN, LIN, Automotive Ethernet) and their security implications.

• Work with system owners to define Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)

You will lead and steward the Ministry’s Records Management (RM) and Parliamentary Questions (PQ) management frameworks to ensure proper governance and achieve the desired policy outcomes.

You will be responsible for shaping and implementing MOH-wide RM and PQ policies, frameworks, processes and standards. This involves translating Whole-of-Government requirements and MOH’s strategic intent into clear, practical and implementable policies and practices. 

You will provide functional leadership to align MOH divisions on the policy interpretation and application of RM and PQ requirements.

You will steward the PQ management framework and guidelines to ensure clear standards, timelines and expectations for Divisions. 

You will provide policy interpretation to Divisions on RM and PQ matters and drive consistent application of standards across the organisation.

You will collaborate with internal stakeholders, partners and vendors to ensure that RM and PQ systems are effective and aligned with policy requirements. You will also identify opportunities to streamline processes and enhance these systems through continuous improvements across both portfolios.

At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. Develop World-Class Infrastructure

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
