jobDescription:
We are looking for a Marketing Automation and Lifecycle Specialist to join JTC's marketing team. With at least 7 to 9 years of hands-on experience, you will lead how JTC engages its stakeholders through data-driven, targeted, and purposeful communications.
 
In this role, you will be the in-house owner of Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced, responsible for how JTC reaches and nurtures its stakeholders (businesses, industrialists, partners, and the broader public) across the full lifecycle of their relationship with us. This is not a commercial marketing role. JTC is a public agency, and our marketing exists to advance our mission of developing industrial infrastructure and supporting Singapore's economic growth. 
 
The role is weighted 75% towards marketing automation and lifecycle marketing, with the remaining 25% covering performance marketing oversight: setting strategy and KPIs, managing our external media agency, and owning the analytics that connect campaign activity to real outcomes. If you are someone who has built and run sophisticated lifecycle marketing programmes before, and who is equally comfortable reading performance data and steering agency execution as you are building automation workflows from the ground up, we want to hear from you.
jobResponsibilities:
Marketing Automation & Lifecycle Marketing (75%)
•	Own and manage JTC's Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced system 
•	Design and run end-to-end lifecycle programmes that nurture stakeholder relationships across awareness, onboarding, engagement, and retention.
•	Develop audience segmentation and personalisation strategies using Salesforce CRM data to deliver relevant, timely communications.
•	Build and maintain automated workflows, triggered communications, and drip programmes across email and other owned channels.
•	Ensure data integrity across Salesforce CRM and Marketing Cloud, including managing integrations, data extensions, and sync configurations.
•	Work with IT, Business Insights and CRM teams to optimise platform capabilities and explore new features within SFMC Advanced.
•	Set and enforce best practices for marketing automation, including governance, documentation, and compliance with data privacy regulations.
Performance Marketing & Analytics (25%)
•	Set the strategy, KPIs, and success metrics for JTC's performance marketing activity, anchored in mission-driven stakeholder outcomes rather than commercial conversion.
•	Brief, manage, and review external media agencies running paid search, paid social, display, and programmatic campaigns on JTC's behalf.
•	Build and maintain analytics dashboards and reporting frameworks that track campaign performance, audience behaviour, and channel effectiveness across owned and paid activity.
•	Surface actionable insights from campaign and lifecycle data to inform future strategy.
•	Lead A/B and multivariate testing across automation workflows and, where relevant, paid campaigns.
jobRequirements:
•	Background in Marketing, Communications, Business, Data Analytics, or a related discipline.
•	Minimum 7 to 9 years of experience, with the majority spent in marketing automation and lifecycle marketing roles.
•	Deep, hands-on expertise in Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced or equivalent, including building customer segments, emails, user journeys and campaigns. 
•	Strong working knowledge of Salesforce CRM, including lead management, campaign tracking, and data integration.
•	Working understanding of performance marketing across paid search (Google Ads), paid social (Meta, LinkedIn), and programmatic. You do not need to have run these campaigns hands-on, but you should be able to brief an agency, interrogate their numbers, and recognise good work from poor.
•	Proficiency in Google Analytics 4, Marketing Cloud Intelligence, or equivalent BI platforms.
•	Strong analytical mindset with the ability to translate data into clear insights and recommendations for non-technical audiences.
•	Comfortable defining and working towards mission-driven KPIs in a public sector context, where stakeholder impact and organisational objectives take precedence over commercial metrics.
•	Excellent project management skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously.
•	Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
•	Experience in a public sector, B2B, or complex stakeholder environment is an advantage.

jobResponsibilities:
The organisation is looking for a hands-on Cyber Engineer to join the cybersecurity team, with a primary focus on Akamai Web Application Firewall (WAF) operations. The candidate will be responsible for the day-to-day operational health of the Akamai environment, supporting the expansion of coverage to additional internal systems, and helping the organisation mature its security posture through newly enabled capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

Day-to-Day Akamai Operations

The candidate will serve as the technical lead for Akamai services, working closely with various internal stakeholders and contractors to ensure the smooth delivery of Akamai services and timely follow-up on security incidents and alerts.

The candidate will also provide onboarding support for new systems being brought onto Akamai, and offer consultancy to project teams on Akamai-related matters.

Security Capability Rollout and Evaluation

The candidate will support the rollout and evaluation of new Akamai security features, including antimalware scanning, AI Firewall, and API Security. This involves hands-on tuning of policies and rules, conducting impact assessments, and working with stakeholders to balance security effectiveness with operational continuity.

Reporting and Stakeholder Coordination The candidate will prepare regular operational reports and security metrics for internal stakeholders and management, and serve as the coordination point between project teams and Akamai’s vendor.

Documentation

The candidate will maintain and improve operational documentation, including runbooks, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and configuration guides, to ensure operational knowledge is well-captured and accessible to the broader team.

Requirements

The ideal candidate should have at least 2–4 years of hands-on experience in cybersecurity operations or web application security, with direct experience working with Akamai products being strongly preferred. Candidates with equivalent experience on comparable WAF or CDN platforms such as Cloudflare, Imperva, or F5, and a demonstrated ability to ramp up on Akamai, will also be considered.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, or related technical discipline

• Possess working knowledge of web application security concepts, including the OWASP Top 10, common attack patterns such as SQLi, XSS, and CSRF, and how WAF rules are structured to detect and mitigate them. Familiarity with API security principles and how API gateways and WAFs interact is an advantage, particularly given the scope of the API Security capability work.

•Experience with log analysis and data extraction, and proficiency in at least one scripting language such as Python or Bash for automation and data processing tasks would be an asset.

jobTitle: [LTA-HR] ASSISTANT / DEPUTY MANAGER, HUMAN RESOURCE (WORKFORCE PLANNING)
agencyDescription:
The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is a statutory board under Ministry of Transport that spearheads land transport developments in Singapore. We are seeking dynamic, energetic, highly motivated, passionate and qualified professionals to join us.

Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.
jobDescription: [LTA-HR] ASSISTANT / DEPUTY MANAGER, HUMAN RESOURCE (WORKFORCE PLANNING)

agencyDescription:

Our people set us apart as we champion the development of a future-ready built environment for Singapore. Impactful: Champion an inclusive and sustainable built environment for people of all ages, abilities and needs.

Transformational: Lead the transformation of the built environment sector to deliver a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment.

jobDescription:
[What the role for]
The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) champions the development of a future ready built environment for Singapore. Besides regulating building safety, we lead and transform the built environment sector in delivering a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment. We are looking for resourceful, energetic and self-motivated individuals who are inspired to play an active role to make a difference to Singapore’s built environment.
jobResponsibilities:
[What you will be working on]

The Built Environment Technology Alliance (BETA) is a group under the Communications and Engagement cluster of the Building and Construction Authority (BCA). As the sector lead for Singapore’s Built Environment (BE) sector, BCA champions the development and delivery of a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment.

BETA’s work is primarily industry-facing, with an emphasis on generating commercial value and tangible outcomes from research and innovation activities. Simply put, BETA’s mission can be summarised as ‘Building Bridges, Accelerating Innovation’.


As an executive/senior manager in the BETA team, you will play a role in facilitating the research, innovation and technology adoption efforts of leading firms within Singapore’s BE sector. You will be managing and supporting a portfolio of accounts that includes but is not limited to developers, builders, consultants, and facilities management (FM) companies. Through the role, you will gain strong familiarity with the BE Innovation and Technology (I&T) ecosystem, including a diverse range of solution providers across various domains such as sustainability, productivity and digitalisation.

Relationship Management and Project Development

  • Serve as the main contact point to key accounts on Research and Innovation (R&I) matters and oversee end-to-end process of project development and execution as well as related activities

  • Work with growing enterprises in understanding their business needs, formulate R&I strategies (e.g. technology scanning and roadmapping) and assist to put in place an I&T framework so that appropriate execution approaches can be developed that will hone an agile and sustained competitive advantage for BE firms in Singapore and overseas

  • Cultivate strategic relationships and build trust with key executives of the BE I&T ecosystem (including C-suites in private and public sectors as well as academia) to undertake industry development, invest in R&I and deploy I&T

  • Work in close partnership with various stakeholders to define R&I project plans and budgets, develop timelines, establish and monitor project risks and facilitate the project teams in achieving deliverables and objectives

  • Research and develop deep understanding of Singapore and the global R&I ecosystem in BE as well as emerging technology and business trends, so as to be able to appreciate potential opportunities and implications to the relevance and transformation of the BE sector

Strategic Communications and Industry Awareness

  • Initiate and/or support publicity and awareness initiatives such as tech events and showcases, industry roundtables etc.

  • Curate I&T content and work with corporate communications team to present them in an effective and engaging manner to key stakeholders

Policy and Programme Implementation

  • Work with key agencies in the I&T eco-system (e.g. the National Research Foundation, Ministry of National Development, Enterprise Singapore, JTC Corporation and Infocomm Media Development Authority) to refine policy and implement initiatives that facilitate industry development and R&I activities in the BE sector, whilst ensuring proper governance

  • Evaluate and refine proposals, facilitate networking and strengthen partnerships within the BE I&T ecosystem, including via the Built Environment Accelerate-to-Market Programme (BEAMP)

  • Familiarity/experience with the built environment sector and/or business development/consulting/research and innovation fields are useful but not mandatory (i.e. fresh graduates are welcomed too)

  • Should be a results-oriented thinker, with proven conceptual and analytical skills

  • Able to work independently with excellent communication skills to engage a range of stakeholders in various settings

Interested applicants, please apply online.

jobTitle: Manager/Senior Manager (Systems Governance & Operations Policy), SIR/CCPO
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
Within the Strategy, International & Research (SIR) Directorate, the Systems Governance & Operations Policy (SGP) Branch under the CaseCentral Product Office (CCPO) is responsible for establishing robust governance frameworks, operational policies, and ICT system enablers that underpin MSF's frontline social service delivery.

CaseCentral is a case management platform, which aims to empower caseworkers from the social service sector to deliver holistic, coordinated, and efficient support – driving better client and family outcomes. This role plays a critical part in ensuring the system is well-governed, operationally ready, and continuously improved to meet evolving service delivery needs.

You will support ops policy development and governance to change management, stakeholder engagement, inter-agency coordination, and product operations. Working at the intersection of policy, operations, and technology, you will partner closely with internal teams, social service agencies, and ICT stakeholders. You may also be required to supervise and guide contract, temporary, or junior staff, providing day-to-day direction and quality assurance, as well as contribute to the team's capability building through knowledge sharing, coaching peers, and supporting a learning culture.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Governance and Ops Policy Framework Development
•	Co-develop or support the review of ops policies, governance frameworks, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure CaseCentral operates within MSF's and Whole-of-Government (WOG) Information Management (IM) and data governance standards.
•	Translate policy intent into clear, implementable operational workflows and process documentation.
•	Proactively identify governance gaps and propose solutions to strengthen accountability and compliance across the system lifecycle.

2. System Change Governance and Prioritisation
•	Manage the end-to-end intake, assessment, and prioritisation of system enhancement requests from business owners and operational stakeholders.
•	Facilitate structured stakeholder discussions to surface needs, resolve competing priorities, and build alignment across divisions and agencies.
•	Ensure policy and operational decisions are systematically documented to support traceability, auditability and governance oversight.

3. Operationalisation and Implementation Readiness
•	Develop and refine onboarding frameworks, rollout playbooks, and SOPs to prepare agencies and users for system transitions.
•	Support data migration planning and system transition and handover activities, coordinating across technical, operational, and business teams.
•	Conduct pre-go-live risk assessments and develop mitigation plans to ensure smooth operational launches with minimal service disruption.

4. Change Management and Stakeholder Engagement 
•	Design and execute change management (CM) strategies that address people, process, and technology dimensions for CaseCentral rollouts and enhancements.
•	Build, sustain and coordinate Change Champion networks across agencies to embed ownership, drive adoption, and enable peer-to-peer support.
•	Plan, coordinate and support communications, briefings, training, and engagement sessions tailored to diverse stakeholder groups.
•	Gather systematic user feedback through surveys, focus groups, and operational reviews; synthesise insights to inform product roadmap and system improvements.

5. Cross-Agency Coordination and Data Sharing
•	Develop, operationalise and maintain the consent framework to facilitate data sharing between MSF and partner agencies.
•	Advise on data governance considerations, including data standards and flows, to support interface and integration planning across CaseCentral and partner systems.

6. System Operations and Product Operations Management
•	Oversee or manage issue triage, escalation workflows, and resolution tracking to ensure timely and effective response to operational incidents.
•	Support system performance monitoring and service review processes, working with ICT partners to maintain service levels.
•	Identify recurring operational pain points and recommend systemic improvements to enhance system reliability and user experience.

7. Documentation and Knowledge Management 
•	Develop and maintain comprehensive SOPs, user guides, process maps, and governance documentation to support consistent system operations.
•	Establish and maintain knowledge transfer frameworks to ensure institutional knowledge is preserved and accessible across teams.

8. Project and Implementation Coordination
•	Contribute to project planning, milestone tracking, and delivery coordination across workstreams involving CaseCentral and related systems.
•	Manage project risks and issues, ensuring compliance with MSF and whole-of-government project governance frameworks.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong systems thinking with the ability to connect policy intent, operational realities, and technology enablers.
•	Analytical and structured, with a disciplined approach to problem framing, documentation, and decision-making.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement skills — able to communicate with clarity and influence across diverse audiences, from frontline workers to senior management.
•	Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment with competing priorities.
•	Proactive self-starter with a high degree of initiative and ownership over assigned workstreams.

Qualifications and Experience
•	Relevant qualifications in any discipline. Candidates with backgrounds in Public Policy, Social Sciences, Business, Information Systems, or related fields are welcome.
•	At least 3–5 years of relevant experience in policy development, operations management, change management, or ICT governance — preferably in a public sector or social services context.
•	Experience working with case management systems, social service platforms, or government ICT projects is an advantage.
•	Familiarity with WOG governance frameworks, IM8, or data governance practices is a plus.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.

agencyDescription:
SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Education (MOE). It will drive and coordinate the implementation of the national SkillsFuture movement, promote a culture and holistic system of lifelong learning through the pursuit of skills mastery, and strengthen the ecosystem of quality education and training in Singapore.

SSG will strengthen the adult training infrastructure by taking on all existing functions of the Committee for Private Education (CPE) and guide the Institute for Adult Learning (IAL) to enhance the capabilities and professionalism of adult educators. SSG will play a key role in the quality assurance for private education institutions and adult training centres. Together with educational institutions and training partners, SSG will ensure that students and working adults have access to high quality, industry-relevant training throughout life. SSG will also bring together synergies in continuing education and training (CET) and pre-employment training (PET), so skills requirements will continue to meet the demands of different sectors of the economy.
jobDescription:
The Manager/Senior Manager, Course Approval, within the Quality Management Division, plays a critical role in ensuring the quality and compliance of courses accredited in the Training Grant System (TGS).

Reporting to the Team Lead, the incumbent is part of a team responsible for course accreditation, quality checks, system testing, and cross-divisional coordination. This role is integral to maintaining high standards in Continuing Education and Training (CET), supporting SkillsFuture Singapore's mission to enable individuals to learn for life, pursue skills mastery and develop fulfilling careers, for a future-ready Singapore.
jobResponsibilities:
• Course Accreditation and Quality Management
    • Carry out course accreditation/approval and related course quality management activities in the Training Grant System (TGS).
    • Conduct course quality checks by reviewing course materials against sound adult learning principles and relevant SSG and funding requirements.
    • Handle escalated enquiries and appeals from the public and training providers relating to courses, including conducting inquiries to ascertain non-compliances against SSG's Terms and Conditions for Registered Training Providers (RTPs) when necessary.

  • System Testing and Enhancements
    • Support system testing and implement enhancements to TGS when necessary to improve processes and functionality.

  • Planning and Coordination Support
    • Support planning-related work by coordinating within the Quality Management Division and with external divisions such as policy units and system teams to align planning efforts.

  • Project and Initiative Support
    • Support divisional and organisational projects, initiatives, and other assigned tasks, contributing to continuous improvement and innovation within the division.
jobRequirements:
• Possess the required competencies to execute the job duties proficiently.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant working experience, preferably in Continuing Education and Training (CET). Fresh graduates or candidates without the required qualifications but with relevant experience such as course quality management, courseware design and delivery are welcome to apply.
  • A good command of English for both oral and written communication.
  • Experience or an appreciation of adult education in Singapore is preferred. Candidates with WSQ Advanced Certificate in Learning and Performance (ACLP) or WSQ Advanced Certificate in Training and Assessment (ACTA) qualifications are preferred.
  • Possess good analytical skills to investigate, evaluate, and analyse public complaints, feedback, and whistleblowing cases.
  • Basic or intermediate proficiency in data handling.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure.

Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume. Please check out www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP.

jobDescription:

The Department’s work involves analysing weather radar and environmental satellite data, post-processing numerical weather predictions and developing data-driven models to improve weather nowcasts and forecasts. To fulfil its mission, the Department also participates in stakeholder engagement and research collaboration activities.

We are looking for experienced individuals to develop and implement innovative weather solutions to support operational weather services, specialised stakeholder/user sectors and the public. The role requires deep meteorological expertise (in areas such as Numerical/AI Weather Prediction and specialised meteorological observing systems) as well as the ability to apply methods in related disciplines such as data science, geographic information systems and software development. You will work with users to translate their requirements for weather services into operational products and services. You will also have opportunities to participate in international conferences and seminars.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. The job scope includes:

  • Engaging stakeholder groups, e.g., in the field of aviation and marine services, as well as government agencies, to understand their specialised domain requirements and propose suitable meteorological solutions.
  • Analysing data from physics-based and AI/ML weather prediction models and meteorological observation systems and undertaking studies to improve the reliability of forecast products and services.
  • Designing and developing meteorological products for users, or for integration with their systems.
  • Directing the work of research performers.
  • Developing software applications to operationalise the generation and delivery of weather products and services.
  • Providing advice on meteorological data and applications to users.
jobRequirements:
The job might be for you if you possess:

  • Postgraduate qualification in Meteorology
  • Good understanding of numerical weather prediction and specialised meteorological observing systems
  • 3 years’ experience in developing weather forecast products and services
  • Experience in working with remote sensing data
  • Knowledge in statistical packages or machine learning/deep learning algorithms
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement
  • General proficiency in Information Technology
  • Working experience in scientific programming and application development
  • Good command of spoken and written English and excellent communication skills
  • Ability to work with others as well as independently

This is aimed at strengthening Singapore's public health capabilities built during the COVID-19 response to ensure a unified command and coordinated approach across all situations, from routine disease control to future outbreaks.

CDA safeguards the nation from communicable diseases through disease surveillance, outbreak investigations, vaccination programs, public education, and global health collaboration. Beyond domestic activities, the CDA aims to expand Singapore’s global outreach and foster collaboration with international partners.
jobDescription: As an officer in the Advanced Methods and Analytics Division, you will be part of a team that conducts infectious disease modelling to inform national policy development, surveillance and preparedness. This role requires not only relevant technical expertise but preferably a broad scientific knowledge of infectious diseases as well. You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
You will develop and deploy cutting-edge mathematical models on infectious disease related projects. Your work will transform complex data into clear, actionable insights that support evidence-based public health decision making and interventions. The core areas of work will include, but are not limited to:

  • Nowcasting and forecasting: Predicting infectious disease dynamics in real-time.
  • Scenario modelling: Simulating potential outcomes of different disease scenarios, public health strategies and interventions.
  • Program/Intervention evaluations: Performing impact and economic evaluations of public health programs and interventions.
  • Long-term projections: Deriving long-term disease burden and making future-looking predictions.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop and deploy infectious disease transmission-dynamic models to address key national communicable disease concerns.
  • Partner with stakeholders to design, develop and address project-related questions, identify knowledge gaps, and address key gaps through appropriate analysis.
  • Adapt and extend existing state-of-the-art models, or design and build new models where appropriate.
  • Parameterise models by analysis of appropriate data and literature review.
  • Synthesise evidence from literature, surveillance and other data sources to understand the natural history and epidemiology of infection, and the effectiveness of control measures.
  • Lead project from inception to completion, defining scope, timelines and deliverables, managing risks and ensuring outputs meet required standards of rigour and relevance.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for project-related communications, fostering clear and consistent engagement with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Provide mentorship and develop junior team members
jobRequirements:
• Post-graduate qualification in a quantitative discipline (e.g. mathematics, statistics, physics, computational biology or economics). A Ph.D. in infectious disease modelling is preferred.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in modelling infectious disease dynamics.
  • Strong skills in programming in PYTHON and/or R, or any other directly transferrable language e.g. C++.
  • Strong record of relevant, peer-reviewed publications is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify, frame, formulate and solve problems, make judgments based on analysis and interpretation of complex data or situations, as well as assess and devise appropriate responses.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with initiative and independence and as a team member in a multidisciplinary team.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate highly complex ideas, methods, and disseminate results clearly and succinctly to a wide audience of varying technical levels, including non-technical audience.

Attributes and aptitude:

  • Analytical thinking.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
  • Strategic thinking and planning abilities.
  • Collaborative mindset.
  • Accountability and ownership

The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding lead donors—including high-net-worth individuals, corporations, and foundations.
The incumbent will manage a portfolio of current and prospective donors and oversee all phases of the gift cycle including donor engagement, cultivation, solicitation, proposal development, and stewardship. The ideal candidate is an exceptional relationship-builder who is results-driven, creative, collaborative, organised, and strategic.
This role will also support the College’s leadership team in designing and implementing strategies to secure significant philanthropic gifts, while working closely with volunteers, senior leadership, faculty, and colleagues to advance the College’s priorities.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Strategic Leadership in Stewardship and Fundraising

Provide strategic oversight of the stewardship and fundraising programmes, approving frameworks and stewardship strategies developed by the College Philanthropy Unit, while ensuring stewardship and fundraising efforts are fully integrated across the donor lifecycle.

2. Donor Portfolio Management
Personally manage a portfolio of donors through full-cycle engagement, including face-to-face visits, tailored proposals, and personalised correspondence, serving as the senior institutional point of contact for the most significant donor relationships.

3. Prospect Development & Pipeline Building

Identify and cultivate gift prospects, develop sourcing strategies, and maintain a disciplined portfolio management approach with timely call reports and donor interaction records.

4. Donor Engagement & Stewardship Oversight

Hold accountability for overall stewardship programme performance, including setting key performance indicators, reviewing outcomes, and ensuring the team delivers events, impact reports, recognition initiatives, and communications to the required standard. Proactively develop and deliver meaningful engagement opportunities to maximise donor support—both financial and non-financial.

5. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Alignment

Collaborate with other units in the College, and senior leadership to support institutional fundraising objectives, and influence key stakeholders to participate actively in donor engagement and recognition.

6. Solicitation, Gift Documentation & Compliance

Solicit immediate and planned gifts, ensure accurate preparation of gift agreements, and hold ultimate accountability for compliance with gift agreements, donor intent, and relevant financial and legal standards.

7. Team Leadership & Programme Development

Supervise and develop the Managers of Stewardship and Fundraising, oversee the fundraising and stewardship budget, and drive continuous improvement and innovation in stewardship and fundraising practices.

8. Fundraising Performance & Accountability

Meet or exceed annual fundraising goals and activity metrics, maintaining a results-oriented approach across both personal portfolio management and broader team fundraising and stewardship activities.

jobTitle: Mgr/ Snr Mgr, Philanthropic Partnerships (Public Agencies and Community Groups)
agencyDescription: NCSS is the umbrella body for over 500 member social service agencies in Singapore. Its mission is to provide leadership and direction in enhancing the capabilities and capacity of our members, advocating for social service needs, and strengthening strategic partnerships, for an effective social service ecosystem. Community Chest and Social Service Institute (SSI) are part of NCSS. For more information visit www.ncss.gov.sg
jobDescription:
A little bit about who we are.

The Community Chest, formed since 1983, is the largest centralised fund-raising body for social services in Singapore to lighten social service organisations from the burden of fund-raising. The mandate of the Group was expanded in 2015 to include the role of Secretariat to the President’s Challenge, Office of the President of Singapore, and has gone beyond traditional fund-raising to engaging the community, public, family offices, foundations and the corporates in creating sustainable solutions to address social challenges and foster a more inclusive society.

The role as we see it.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced individual to join our Philanthropic Partnerships team, focusing on fundraising and partnership development with donors from Public Agencies, and Community Groups (such as Clans, Education, Healthcare and Religious Institutions).

In this role, you will be responsible for crafting and executing strategies to engage philanthropic donors, corporations, and partners to support the mission and programs of the Community Chest of Singapore. You will lead efforts to secure funding while building long-term partnerships that maximize resources and drive social impact.

You should take pride in your commitment to excellence, both individually and within a team, possess a keen attention to detail and thrive in a fast-paced, high-performance environment. We place a premium on your ability in managing demanding stakeholder relationships with professionalism and poise. You excel under pressure, adeptly resolve conflicts, and focus on building sustainable, long-term partnerships.

Areas you should be passionate about and excel in.

1. Strategy Development: Create and implement comprehensive strategies to engage philanthropic donors and partners, aligning efforts with the organization's mission and objectives. Identify and establish partnerships with philanthropic donors, corporations, government agencies, trade associations, and Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to leverage resources and maximize impact. Identify and cultivate new donor segments/revenue streams by leveraging the extensive suite of NCSS resources, including matching grants and government-backed initiatives.

2. Sector Development & Advocacy: Foster and maintain strong relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and other stakeholders to increase the giving of Time, Treasure and Talent. Lead sector-specific fundraising initiatives, including campaigns, events, and appeals, in close coordination with internal and external stakeholders.

4. Donor Management, Insights and Reporting: Develop and maintain systems for tracking and reporting on fundraising activities to ensure accountability and transparency. Utilize and refine donor data and insights to enhance donor experience and satisfaction. Ensure risk management / mitigation on systems and public facing platforms and touchpoints.

5. Strategic Communication: Craft compelling messages and materials that effectively convey the impact of philanthropic support and partnerships to donors, partners, and the broader community.

agencyDescription: The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) is Singapore's national land use planning authority. URA prepares long term strategic plans, as well as detailed local area plans, for physical development, and then co-ordinates and guides efforts to bring these plans to reality. Prudent land use planning has enabled Singapore to enjoy strong economic growth and social cohesion, and ensures that sufficient land is safeguarded to support continued economic progress and future development.
jobDescription:
About Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA)
The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) is Singapore’s land use planning and conservation authority. Our mission is to make Singapore a great city to live, work and play. We plan and facilitate the physical development of Singapore, in partnership with agencies and the community, to create a vibrant, sustainable and cosmopolitan city of distinction.

About URBEX and DPLab
Over the years, URA has spearheaded efforts to strengthen urban planning and design workflows through the application of urban science, geospatial and data analytics, modelling and simulation (M&S), and AI technologies. In 2022, URA was designated as the Whole-of-Government (WOG) Urban Planning & Design Technology Centre of Excellence (URBEX), to lead the planning and design sector in building up these strategic capabilities.  
The Design & Planning Lab (DPLab) is a multi-disciplinary team in URA which drives URBEX efforts. In recognition of our work, URA was conferred the 2024 Esri Special Achievement in Geographic Information System (GIS) Award for demonstrating vision, leadership and innovation in the use of GIS technology. URA was also awarded the Esri Singapore GeoInnovation Award in 2024 for being amongst Singapore’s most progressive organisations in the use of geospatial solutions to transform the future. Our flagship product, ePlanner (a web-based geospatial platform that brings digital planning tools to WOG) also won the Excellence Award at the Singapore Public Service’s Science, Technology and Engineering Conference 2024. 
In DPLab, you will work alongside talented individuals with expertise in wide-ranging domains including data policy, governance, strategy and engineering, product strategy, business analysis, software engineering, cloud engineering, urban design technologies, data science, AI/Machine Learning, and M&S.  You will also work closely with planners, architects, and policymakers to co-create digital solutions that contribute to enhancing the liveability, sustainability and resilience of our city-state.
jobResponsibilities:
•	In this role, you will formulate digital and AI transformation strategies for URA and its business groups. Working closely with stakeholders, you will map service journeys, surface business challenges, and translate these into technology solutions that deliver measurable outcomes. This includes identifying opportunities to apply AI and digital technologies across upstream and downstream planning processes — spanning strategic planning, physical planning, urban design, development and growth management, regulatory development control, and infrastructure planning and coordination.

•	You will partner with business groups to conduct end-to-end business analyses and facilitate service journey mapping exercises, identifying where the right technology — AI, automation, or process redesign — can strengthen planning outcomes, improve service delivery, and drive productivity gains. As a trusted partner, you will support business groups in their problem definition and solution scoping through to the implementation of fit-for-purpose digital products and the realisation of intended benefits. This includes assessing the technical feasibility of proposed solutions, estimating resource requirements, and identifying risks and challenges to inform prioritisation of development efforts. Throughout the product development process, you will work collaboratively with AI Engineers, Data Engineers, Software Developers, UX Designers, and Data Scientists to deliver the solutions.

•	Beyond AI solutions, you will develop and drive organisational transformation strategies that support the effective adoption of AI across URA and its business groups. This ensures that AI tools and capabilities are built up and meaningfully integrated into day-to-day business processes. In partnership with business groups, you will engage the URA community through targeted training and change management efforts, building AI literacy and competencies at both individual and organisational levels. Underpinning these, you will champion strong governance practices and ensure that AI is adopted in a secure and responsible manner.
jobRequirements:
•	The ideal candidate brings a strong analytical mindset, experience in business or systems analysis, and has a keen interest in cities and applying AI and digital solutions to make Singapore an even more liveable, sustainable and economically competitive city.

A postgraduate qualification or professional certification in business analysis, product strategy & management, or AI-related disciplines would be an advantage. Prior experience in digital transformation, change management, or technology implementation projects will be valued.

Project & Product Management

Experience with service journey mapping, agile methodologies, or human-centred design approaches, as well as understanding of urban planning processes, would be advantageous.

STB is responsible for leading the Whole-of-Government effort to plan and execute this world class event in partnership with our race promoter Singapore GP Pte Ltd (SGP).

1. Stakeholder management. As a street race, support and buy-in from multiple stakeholders is critical for the success of the race. The officer will work closely with diverse stakeholders, including Marina Bay stakeholders (e.g., hotels and malls), race promoter SGP and other Government agencies, to innovate ways to improve the race experience for businesses, public, and patrons. The officer will also lead the management of stakeholder-related queries in the lead up to and during the race week at the Joint Operations Command (JOC).

2. Circuit & Infrastructure (C&I) Subcommittee. The officer will:

  • Work closely with diverse stakeholders to plan and review the lighting of key trackside properties around the Marina Bay circuit (“city lighting”) to maximise the showcase of Singapore's cityscape on aerial broadcast, which translates into international media value and destination branding. The officer will have the opportunity to refresh the city lighting plans for the next few years.

  • Work closely with diverse stakeholders to manage critical assets (e.g., overpasses etc) to ensure these are ready for the race each year.

3. Security & Emergency Response (S&ER) and Traffic & Transport Subcommittees. The officer will be STB’s key representative and liaison for both Subcommittees respectively led by the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and the Land Transport Authority (LTA). The officer will:

  • Work closely with various Government agencies and race promoter SGP to set up and manage the Joint Operations Command (JOC) which serves as the nerve centre of operations and communications during the race weekend. The officer may be required to work closely with agencies and race promoter SGP to manage any security-related issues.

  • Represent STB in Subcommittee meetings, including to lead STB’s inputs where required.

  • Work closely with SPF and LTA on budget reimbursement.

4. This role will enable the officer to build effective relationship-building, problem solving, and budget management skills.

Key relationships:

1. External: Marina Bay stakeholders, race promoter SGP and Government agencies (especially SPF and LTA)

2. Internal: Procurement, Finance, and Legal

  • Showing good business acumen, analytical thinking and judgement

  • Being innovative and learning continuously

agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).

The Internal Security Department (ISD) confronts and addresses threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability. agencyDescription: Singapore Customs is a government agency under the Ministry of Finance. Re-constituted on 1 April 2003, Singapore Customs is the lead agency on trade facilitation and revenue enforcement matters. It is also responsible for the implementation of customs and trade enforcement measures including those related to Free Trade Agreements and strategic goods.
jobDescription:
[A Trade Facilitator, A Trade Regulator and A Law Enforcer]
 
Singapore Customs advances Singapore’s economic development by protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. We protect revenue – that is invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community, making Singapore a better place today and for tomorrow. We make trade easy, fair and secure by maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub while ensuring the integrity of the trading system. As part of the OneCustoms team, you will have the opportunity to take on different roles during your career with us – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. You can look forward to seamless advancement opportunities with our integrated grade structure under the Customs Unified Scheme of Service (CUS).
jobResponsibilities:
In Singapore Customs, we work, play, learn and grow together as OneCustoms team. With regular job rotations under our Open Posting System that offer many opportunities for competency and skills development, you will get to experience our Customs core functions in trade facilitation, regulation and compliance as well as enforcement during the foundational phase. 
 
You lead and guide a team of officers who share a common objective of protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. 
· Trade Facilitator: You facilitate customs connectivity across borders for a seamless and resilient end-to-end international supply chain, and work closely with local and international partners to advance Singapore’s economy. 
· Trade Regulator: You safeguard Singapore’s reputation as a global trade hub by upholding the rules of trade and tariffs, and keeping a close watch on strategic goods and technologies to maintain an effective and robust regulatory regime. 
· Law Enforcer: You protect Singapore’s revenue by adopting a whole-of-government approach, and working closely with other enforcement agencies to enforce against revenue-related and trade offences. 
 
No matter what your role is or how you spend your time, the impact of your contributions count. 
 
[Sign-on Bonus] Eligible officers who are newly appointed to the Public Service and Singapore Customs will receive a sign-on bonus of $8,000 paid in two tranches. 
 
[Retention Bonus] You will receive attractive retention pay-outs in your 4th, 7th, and 10th in Customs scheme of service. 

[Starting Salary] · $4,020 - $5,036*
 
*Starting monthly salary may vary based on a holistic assessment of academic qualifications, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.
jobRequirements: You can be a part of the OneCustoms team to protect the revenue to be invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community and to contribute to maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub! The role is open to applicants from all disciplines who are keen on the opportunity to take on different roles in Customs through the regular job rotations under our Open Posting System – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. We have a structured career development roadmap to nurture you as a professional Customs officer. We put our traders, travellers and our people at the heart of everything we do. We serve with commitment and purpose yet being able to deliver decisively at the same time. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. jobDescription:
What the role is

You will be part of a team focused on building technical capabilities for high-level feasibility assessments and the research of infrastructure requirements for advanced nuclear energy systems. You will develop expertise in researching the technical requirements and physical constraints associated with emerging nuclear energy technologies, ensuring that all theoretical frameworks align with international guidelines (e.g., IAEA) and contribute to national land-use efficiency studies.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on:

1. Developing Technical Capabilities for Site Hazard Research

  • Methodology Development: Contribute to the development of technical frameworks for studying site suitability and resilience, including geological, geophysical, geotechnical, and seismological (GGGS) research.

  • Hazard Analysis Research: Assist in developing analytical models to study external natural and human-induced hazards to understand long-term infrastructure resilience.

  • Environmental Impact Studies: Conduct research into radiological, biodiversity, and environmental impact assessment methodologies to establish high-level safety and ecological benchmarks.

2. Developing capabilities for relevant IAEA Infrastructure Areas

  • Build and apply deep institutional expertise across the IAEA Milestones approach, specifically assessing siting and operational implications for:

  • Safety & Security: Nuclear Safety, Security, Safeguards, and Radiation Protection.

  • Lifecycle Management: Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Radioactive Waste Management.

  • Crisis Readiness: Comprehensive Emergency Planning and Preparedness.

3. Infrastructure & Urban Integration Planning

  • Systems Integration Research: Collaborate with relevant agencies to study the physical requirements for integrating advanced nuclear energy facilities into urban environments, including cooling water systems and grid connectivity.

  • Spatial Constraint Mapping: Develop models to understand land-use trade-offs for various technology classes.
jobRequirements:
Education:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in the following fields will be preferred.

  • Civil / Environmental Engineering or Geosciences; Urban Planning.

  • Geology or Geotechnical Engineering;

  • Environmental Science, Marine Biology, or Ecology.

  • Engineering or other related technical fields.

  • Supply chain management

Qualification in other related fields are welcome to apply.


Preferred Experience:

  • 8–10 years of relevant working experience in related technical roles.

  • Experience with the site assessment of large-scale infrastructure projects in Singapore.

  • Experience with Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) for major projects.

  • Prior exposure to safety-critical or high-security infrastructure projects.

  • Demonstrated or adjacent but relevant expertise in the following areas (Nuclear safeguards and security; Front-end / back-end fuel cycle and radioactive waste management; Emergency planning and radiation protection) would be a plus.

Competencies and Other Requirements

  • Site assessment for large-scale infrastructure projects.

  • Geotechnical Engineering, Civil and Structural Engineering Management.

  • Knowledge of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and risk modelling will be a plus.

  • Familiarity with the IAEA Safety Standards.

  • Technical writing for regulatory submissions.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesise technical, and policy considerations.

  • Openness to being stationed overseas for extended periods (3 months –2 years) for specialised training and attachments.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
What the role is

You will join the team responsible for the overarching governance and integration of the department activities. The team establishes the internal systems—such as integrated management, international benchmarking, and cost-modelling frameworks—to ensure all feasibility studies are high-quality, and compliant with international standards. You will focus on streamlining internal processes to ensure all institutional outputs meet rigorous technical and regulatory benchmarks.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on:

1. Establishing the Governance & Management Framework

  • Integrated Management System (IMS) Support: Contribute to the design of an internal IMS aligned with international standards (e.g., IAEA GSR Part 2). You will help synthesize safety, quality, and economic elements into a single management structure to support long-term institutional knowledge.

  • Process Governance: Assist in defining decision-making protocols and oversight mechanisms. You will help establish the framework for how technical information is reviewed and validated to ensure high levels of organizational rigour.

2. Financial & Strategic Planning

  • Economic Modelling: Conduct deep-dive analysis and strategic modelling for the financial governance of complex, large-scale infrastructure. This includes researching international cost-control frameworks and long-term funding structures to understand the economic viability of emerging nuclear energy technologies.

  • Program Alignment: Serve as a central coordinator to ensure that various technical branches are aligned with overarching organizational objectives, budgets, and timelines.

  • Risk Frameworks: Support the refinement of risk management frameworks, focusing on identifying systemic dependencies in the early stages of technology assessment.

3. Institutional Readiness & Standards Benchmarking

  • Regulatory Gap Analysis: Collaborate with diverse stakeholders to study international regulatory landscapes. You will help identify gaps in existing local frameworks and research enhancements required to align with global energy governance best practices.

  • International Standards Engagement: Engage with internal departments and research bodies to facilitate comprehensive reviews of emerging energy standards. You will help ensure that any theoretical deployment models are validated against international "Safety, Security, and Safeguards" (3S) benchmarks.

  • Knowledge Management: Build institutional expertise in international licensing and compliance processes, ensuring that the organisation remains an informed participant in global nuclear energy dialogues

Architecture Conservation & Urban Design

  • Minimum relevant 5-years experience in conservation redevelopment works, urban planning & design processes.

This will include conceptualisation & delivery of urban planning strategies, urban design guidelines and architectural scopes to coordinate and execute urban infrastructure, transportation systems, pedestrian & cycling corridors, utility corridors & green infrastructure as part of an integrated streetscape and public realm. Part of the role involves coordination with planning & technical agencies to ensure that the planning intent is in line with the broader Greater Southern Waterfront plans, managing of stakeholder engagements, regulatory approvals, budget unlocking, experience-driven implementation, execution of tender processes & assisting in the project management for the infrastructure enablers required for the implementation the masterplan vision.
jobResponsibilities:
Key Responsibilities

Infrastructure Planning & Urban Design

  • Develop Urban Design strategies and Architectural scopes for urban infrastructure & transportation systems integrated with delightful, attractive & inclusive, climate-responsive public realm and streetscape as part of the Greater Sentosa Master Plan (GSMP).
  • Coordinate with planning & technical agencies on infrastructure planning works for GSMP with the broader GSW as well as national planning policies.
  • Develop comprehensive plans for the implementation of car-lite strategy with phased execution plans to facilitate market acceptance and support urban mobility goals.
  • Develop & implement experience-driven urban mobility strategies with public cool nodes to turn transportation rides and green connectors into curated experiential journeys.
  • Plan, coordinate and execute key transportation systems, pedestrian & cycling corridors, utility corridors, green infrastructure and sustainable urban systems as part of an integrated sensitively designed streetscape and public realm with supporting amenities & open space as infrastructural enablers for the various phases of the GSMP, including rejuvenation of Sentosa and bringing in of the next game changer attraction for Pulau Brani.
  • Contribute to the development and evaluation of Urban Design & Architectural Guidelines to guide infrastructure integration with ongoing and future developments across the various character zones in the GSMP.

Integrative Design Development & Implementation

  • Establish, coordinate and implement development plans in tandem with infrastructure readiness taking into consideration strategic goals, appropriate development densities, attractive tourism strategies, sustainable transport, district & infrastructural enablers, sensitivity towards built & natural heritage, green & blue spaces, sustainability and climate resilience efforts, coastal protection strategies, placemaking strategies and phasing timelines.
  • Work with internal cross-functional teams, precinct & environmental architects & planners, conservation architects, infrastructure & transport engineers to ensure seamless integration of common infrastructure across the various character zones in the GSMP.
  • Coordinate and manage phasing timelines for common urban infrastructure supporting long time developments as well as short term activations and interim uses.
  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, obtaining necessary planning, technical agencies and statutory clearances, and driving execution strategies for urban infrastructural approvals.
  • Prepare & execute of tender packages and project management of consultancy and development contracts to implement the urban infrastructure in support of the master plan and ensure urban design consistency across the various phases.
  • Conduct research on emerging trends and challenges in urban infrastructure design policies for urban planning, urban design and infrastructure coordination for the GSMP and related projects

Requirements

  • Degree in Architecture, Urban Design, Urban Planning, or related field.
  • Minimum relevant 5-years experience in transport-related development works, urban planning & design processes.
  • Familiarity with sustainable urban development principles, climate-responsive design strategies and/or Singapore sustainability frameworks will be advantageous.
  • Registration with Singapore’s Board of Architects (BOA), or Singapore Institute of Planners (SIP) will be preferred.
  • Proficiency in software such as AutoCAD, BIM, rhino, sketch up Photoshop, and ArcGIS or other urban analytics / environmental planning tools.
  • Proactive and creative approach, with a passion for urban infrastructure development.
  • Strong understanding of Singapore's urban design framework and conversant with local building codes & regulations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with experience in stakeholder management and engagement in multi-disciplinary environments.
  • Strength in analytical & problem-solving abilities, project management & organisational skills.
  • Strong written & verbal communication abilities.
jobRequirements:
This is a 3-year contract with the possibility of renewal.

We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

jobTitle: Manager/Assistant Manager (Operations Management and Engagement Department)
agencyDescription:

jobDescription: The Hawker Centres Group (HCG) of NEA plays a lead role in managing and enhancing our hawker centres, so that they continue to be places where people from all walks of life can enjoy affordable food in a clean and hygienic environment. HCG also reviews and implements hawker-related policies that benefit both hawkers and the public.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Asst Mgr/ Manager (Operations Management and Engagement) in HCG, you will be carrying out the following duties:

1. Tenancy Management

  • End-to-end management of stall tenancies, from ensuring stalls are in tenantable condition, onboarding of new stallholders to processing applications of transfers, assignments, joint operators and termination as well as appeals for rental waivers, rebates and remissions etc.

  • Conducting tenancy inspections and enforcements to ensure compliance to relevant statutory and tenancy requirements.

  • Managing arrears such as stall visits, serving of Notice-To-Quits, executing Writ of Seizure & Sales/Writ of Possession etc.

  • Operationalising new policies and programs e.g. ensuring compliance of stallholders to Productive Hawker Centre initiative, management of Incubation Stall Program, Hawkers Development Program etc.

  • Encouraging digitalisation and other programs/initiatives such as supply chain contingency to support and sustain Hawker Trade and maintaining Hawker Culture in the inscription on UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity etc.

2. Feedback/Appeals Management & Stakeholders’ Engagement

  • Managing feedback providers professionally to ensure that their feedback are being addressed or resolved promptly in accordance to NEA’s service standard.

  • Regular engagement with stakeholders including stallholders, Merchants/Hawkers Association (MA/HA), Town Councils, other Agencies etc to implement initiatives and resolve operational issues related to Hawker Centres.

  • Planning and implementing activities and programmes in Hawker Centres, such as fire drills & safety training and spring cleaning, and liaise closely with relevant authorities and stakeholders.

3. Cleaning & Facilities Management

  • Ensuring high cleanliness and post-COVID hygiene standard, good maintenance and safe operation of the centres.

  • Managing the facilities in MSE-owned Hawker Centres through centre level checks, covering facilities maintenance (preventive and routine maintenance), cyclical repairs and redecorations, ad-hoc improvement works to enhance patrons’ experience, incident management, general and toilet cleaning, table-cleaning management, and pest control.

  • Conducting centre surveillance in HDB-owned Hawker Centres to flesh out areas of concerns to stakeholders such as Regional Offices, Town Councils and Hawkers Associations.

  • Appointed by Designated Person (DP) as the Environmental Control Coordinator (ECC) for each hawker centre / wet market, to develop the ES programme in accordance with the ES standards and monitor its implementation on-site.

4. Emergency Preparedness and Contingency Management/Workplace Safety and Health (WSH)

  • Implementation of safety measures and future proof markets/hawker centres to safeguard against extreme weather and/ or civil or national emergency.

  • Adhering and identifying potential WSH risks and working with stakeholders to mitigate the risks.

  • Facilitate Safety Walkabouts at markets/ hawker centres to drill the importance of safety into staff, stallholders and outsourced contractors.

5. Any other tasks as assigned.
jobRequirements:
The job might be for you if possess the following qualities:

  • Organised and able to multi-task

  • Strong stakeholder management skills with outgoing and pleasant personality.

  • Independent, resourceful, meticulous and able to multi-task.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications.

  • Team player with possession of leadership qualities.

  • Able to work after office hours and on weekends when required.

  • As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobTitle: Dty Principal Engineer/Snr Engineer/Exec Engineer (Nuclear Regulatory Ecosystem)
agencyDescription:
The National Environment Agency (NEA) is the leading public organisation responsible for ensuring a clean and sustainable environment for Singapore. Its key roles are to improve and sustain a clean environment, promote sustainability and resource efficiency, maintain high public health standards, provide timely and reliable meteorological information, and encourage a vibrant hawker culture. NEA works closely with its partners and the community to develop and spearhead environmental and public health initiatives and programmes. It is committed to motivating every individual to care for the environment as a way of life, in order to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore for present and future generations.

For more information, visit www.nea.gov.sg
jobDescription:
The Radiation Protection and Nuclear Science Group in the National Environment Agency (NEA) is the national authority for radiation protection in Singapore and serves to protect the public, radiation workers and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation. Its Nuclear Safety Division is responsible for developing capabilities, plans and ecosystems to support national nuclear safety & security assessment, radiological emergency response, and nuclear regulatory development efforts. The division is also responsible for ensuring that Singapore fulfils its obligations to international conventions and agreements with respect to the safe and peaceful use of nuclear material and technology.

Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. Singapore will also need to prepare for the possibility of nuclear power deployment by other countries in the region. These endeavours involve planning and strategizing the development of legal and regulatory infrastructure required for a potential nuclear power programme and building up capabilities in nuclear safety, emergency preparedness and response and radiation protection.

You will be a key member of the team that will play a pivotal role in developing a robust domestic nuclear research and technical support ecosystem to support Singapore’s efforts in studying the safety of nuclear energy.

This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey.
jobResponsibilities:
Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and requires a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore.

By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to nuclear safety, security, safeguards and radiation protection capability building efforts domestically and regionally.

You will be involved in:

  • Master planning the development of Singapore’s nuclear research and technical support ecosystems.
  • Developing and coordinating with academic, research, and industrial partners to build nuclear safety, security and safeguards and radiation protection capabilities nationally.
  • Implementing and administering nuclear research funding initiatives.
  • Initiating and participating in audit exercises to ensure compliance with Standard Operating Procedures for grant management.
jobRequirements:
The job might be for you if you possess:

  • Experience and /or qualifications in Engineering, Research Ecosystem Development and Project Management related fields.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant working experience.
  • Excellent analytical, coordination and communication (written and verbal) skills are critical for this position.
  • Able to communicate with internal and external stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.
  • Able to build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Able to work in a team and independently with minimal supervision.
  • Able to work efficiently and meet tight deadlines.
  • A committed team player who is highly meticulous, with a strong interest in shaping Singapore's nuclear regulatory landscape.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

Applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Integrated Outreach team, which aims to create a Health Living Environment (HLE) where we make healthy living as part of every day life in Singapore. We aim to do so by place making, activating communities and empowering community leaders to play a role in health promotion. This transformative project shifts HPB's role from traditional programme provider to community enabler, embedding health promotion into citizens' lived environments across entire neighbourhoods. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Manager/Senior Manager to spearhead community activation and drive sustainable behavioural change together with healthcare cluster (SingHealth, National University Hospital Systems, National Healthcare Group) and other community partners at the town level.
jobResponsibilities:
As a core member of the HLE initiative, you will be responsible for operationalising an innovative approach to community health that reaches the unreached and transforms neighbourhoods into health-promoting ecosystems. This role represents HPB's strategic pivot towards citizen-centric, place-based health interventions that integrate clinical care with lifestyle support anchored in local communities. You will develop skills in translating data insights into clear strategies and practical actions, data storytelling, stakeholder engagement and negotiation, project management, and cross-agency coordination.

Key Responsibilities

Regional Roll out and Coordination of HLE

  • Support the rollout of the HLE initiative within the assigned region(s), ensuring consistency with national direction while allowing for regional/local adaptations

  • Apply HLE standards (e.g. digital wayfinding standard, engagement playbook, and collaboration manual) during initiative rollout and guide grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in using these resources effectively

  • Utilise community health dashboards and local data insights to empower grassroots and community leaders in identifying priority health needs and co-creating targeted interventions that address specific neighbourhood health gaps

  • Coordinate and support HLE implementation, including meeting facilitation and general project management tasks

Stakeholder Partnership and Capability Building

  • Work with grassroot advisors/leaders, clusters, and community partners to co-create and coordinate neighbourhood-level activities and strengthen community-led health agendas, building community ownership and optimising community spaces into vibrant, health-promoting environments

  • Deliver training sessions and provide practical support to grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in applying the playbook, message house, menu of actions, wayfinding guides, and dashboards

  • Support the team in collaborating with key healthcare partners in their planning and implementation of regional health promotion activities

Programme Activation and Targeted Outreach

  • Coordinate community and regional health programmes, ensuring they are relevant to residents and responsive to their needs

  • Utilise data to prioritise high-need groups, working with GRAs to apply targeted outreach models, outreach quadrants, and activation toolkits in local contexts

  • Connect residents to healthy living assets and programmes by enlivening the lived environment and the Healthy 365 online-offline resident journey, through local mapping that guides them from discovery to sustained participation.

Monitoring, Feedback and Continuous Improvement

  • Track ground-level progress of HLE initiatives, consolidate feedback from residents, local stakeholders, and share insights with the project team and data teams to strengthen impact measurement

  • Collate, utilise and evaluate data from other sources where required, to create a comprehensive picture of the precinct's health profile and its target segments
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be a collaborative leader with a passion for community health promotion transformation and systems thinking. You should have experience in community engagement, partnership management, or public health programme implementation, with the ability to work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

While a degree in a specific field is not mandatory, candidates with backgrounds in business administration/management, public health/public policy/public administration, sociology/psychology, health sciences, communications/media, or related field often possess relevant skills. Trained in project or account management is an added advantage.

The candidate should also possess:

  • A driven and resilient nature; comfortable with challenges and able to work effectively under pressure, both independently and as part of a team

  • Strong collaborative and interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport with diverse stakeholders

  • Adaptability and the ability to work cohesively in fast-paced teams whilst navigating complex, ambiguous situations positively

  • Analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a result-oriented mindset

  • Comfort working effectively in matrix and highly dynamic team environments

  • Basic data analysis and evaluation capabilities

Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract.

  • Building organisation-wide capabilities to embed behavioural and implementation science approaches in projects

  • Working with cross-functional multidisciplinary teams to apply behavioural and implementation science approaches in the design, implementation and evaluation of strategic health promotion interventions to maximise real-world effectiveness and population impact

  • Establishing strategic partnerships with leading behavioural and implementation science institutions and international networks

  • Postgraduate degree or certifications in behavioural science strongly preferred
