agencyDescription: The People’s Association was set up in 1960, in a time of racial and communal strife, to foster racial harmony and social cohesion. Today, we continue to be driven by the same purpose - to build an inclusive, united and resilient Singapore.  We create spaces and opportunities for people of different backgrounds to participate and volunteer in their community. Through community participation, we connect people and deepen relationships to build communities of mutual care and trust.
jobDescription: The Operations Executive supports the administration and operations of PAssion Wave outlets, co-ordinating adventure, water sports and camp programmes while ensuring safety and quality standards are met. The role involves supervising staff, managing facility maintenance and finances, and engaging members in People's Association initiatives. The ability to perform safety operations, including powerboat handling and search and rescue, is essential.
jobResponsibilities:
The Operations Executive assists Managers in the administration and operations of PAssion Wave outlets, implementing outlet strategies aligned with senior management's direction and the People's Association's objectives. They plan and co-ordinate courses, activities and services, oversee maintenance of outlet facilities, and manage budgeting, accounting and cash management to uphold the People's Association's integrity.

The Operations Executive supervises Operations Assistants, works closely with volunteers and trainers to deliver adventure, water sports and camp programmes, and monitors trainer performance on safety and quality. They recommend potential trainers for official appointments and maintain a network with local organisations to stay current with industry developments.

Additionally, the Operations Executive mobilises members to participate in People's Association projects and national campaigns. They assist in emergency evacuation during crises and carry out safety operations including launching and driving powerboats for search and rescue, ensuring all activities are conducted safely.
jobRequirements: At least one year of working experience in adventure, water sports, or an outdoor environment is required, along with the ability to swim at least 50 metres unaided. Possession of a Powered Pleasure Craft Driving License, Lifesaving 1, 2 and 3 certifications, and knowledge in Risk Assessment and Management would be advantageous. Three or more years of experience in a relevant field is preferred, and good presentation skills along with prior customer service experience would further strengthen an application.

  • Strong collaborative and partnership building skills; confident to work with corporate partners and to build relationships with stakeholders.

  • Proven track record in executing mid to large scale programmes and initiatives and demonstrated competency in project management, and

  • Have a strong customer-oriented mindset and good business acumen.

  • Possess excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills to maintain strong partnerships and communicate effectively at all levels

  • Have good leadership and teamwork qualities to engage, motivate and work with team members

  • Possess strong verbal, written and presentation skills coupled with strong negotiation and influencing skills; Bilingual capability will be a strong advantage.

Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Research, Evaluation and Monitoring (REM) division, which drives the development of data-driven insights and analytics to inform health promotion strategies across HPB. The division focuses on translating cutting-edge research and emerging technologies into HPB programmes. By distilling learnings from diverse datasets, applied research, and innovative pilots, REM supports the translation of evidence into practice for delivery in national-scale platforms. The division also plays a key role in strengthening programme design, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that interventions are evidence-based, outcomes-driven, and relevant for real-world implementation.
jobResponsibilities:
As a member of the Analytics and Translation team in the Research, Evaluation and Monitoring division, you will work in a cross-functional, matrix team to contribute to high-impact projects in priority growth areas.

You will generate actionable insights through advanced analytics on diverse datasets (e.g. large longitudinal cohorts, sensors, and combined datasets), applying appropriate statistical and machine learning approaches to support risk prediction, population segmentation, and identification of behavioural patterns.

You will support the development and application of predictive models and segmentation approaches (e.g. clustering) to inform programme targeting, intervention design, and risk stratification, ensuring outputs are robust, interpretable, and relevant for real-world decision-making.

You will set up and support behavioural experiments and programme evaluations, including contributing to study design, data preparation, and analysis to distil research insights and evaluate suitability for translation into programme delivery.

You will develop compelling data-driven narratives for impactful storytelling to both internal and external stakeholders, translating technical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights that inform programme and policy decisions.

You will work with cross-functional teams and external partners to support collaborations and analytics projects, contributing to delivery of strategic outcomes and facilitating knowledge sharing and learning across teams.

You will support the development of data pipelines, feature engineering, and preparation of datasets to enable efficient and scalable analytics, including working with relevant data platforms where required.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate will be a dynamic and self-motivated individual with a strong interest in advancing health promotion through data, research, and analytics. The candidate should be comfortable working at the intersection of data science and real-world application, and is motivated by translating insights into impact at scale.

jobTitle: Engineer/ Senior Engineer (System Integration & Testing – NGPO iATM)
agencyDescription: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore's raison d'etre is to develop the air hub and aviation industry in Singapore, expanding Singapore's links to the rest of the world. We enable opportunities through aviation, making connections, opening doors and enabling choices in people's lives.
jobDescription:
The Next Generation Programme Office (NGPO) in CAAS is looking for a strong, driven, and dynamic engineer to be part of the Info-Centric Air Traffic Management (iATM) Workstream.

You will be part of the team overseeing the implementation of Next Generation iATM systems to inter alia manage flight plan filing and air traffic flow management. You will play a key role in multiple phases of the project cycle e.g. seeking approval, procurement, implementation, testing, maintenance, enhancement, etc.

Depending on the phase, you will be working with relevant stakeholders to define the architecture of the systems, gather system requirements, formulate technical specifications, engage in procurement process, implement, commission and maintain the system in accordance with Singapore Government and international standards (e.g. SG IM8, ICAO). You will also support in the implementation of cyber and data security measures of the system. You will contribute to the safety and efficient management of air traffic in Singapore.
jobResponsibilities:
Key responsibilities include:

  • Work with various external and internal stakeholders to gather project requirements and conduct the necessary market surveys.

  • Design the high-level system architecture and formulate technical specifications for the relevant project(s).

  • Design integration solutions between various systems, applications and databases using APIs, middleware and other technologies.

  • Identify and resolve integration issues, ensuring the stability and reliability of integrated systems.

  • Monitor the performance of integrated system as well as design testing plans for integration solution.

  • Work cooperatively with Project Managers to seek Approval from the relevant authorities for the procurement, design, specifications etc.

  • Work cooperatively with Project Managers to ensure timely delivery of the project based on approved project plan and budget that meets all identified operational needs and objectives.

  • Identify potential integration risks, assess its implications, and recommend mitigating measures to manage and minimise project delay and impact.

  • Review and ensure project documents (e.g. system design document, site acceptance test document, interface control document, etc.) are delivered on time and accurate to support the various project activities.

  • Manage and enhance cyber-security posture (e.g. cyber defenses, mitigation measures) of the system so as to meet CAAS’, national, international standards, and requirements.

  • Engage with the various external and internal stakeholders to ensure that the system is properly integrated and tested to support air traffic operations.

  • Provide regular project updates and highlight any potential issues and its resolutions to management team in a timely manner.
jobRequirements:
• Trained in Engineering (Computing), Information Technology, Computer Science or equivalent.
  • Experience in implementing large-scale ICT system-of-system for the entire life cycle is preferred.
  • Knowledge of cloud system architecture design, system administration, networking, cybersecurity and air traffic management domain is preferred.
  • Professional certification such as Solution Architect and/or SysOps Administrator (from Cloud Service Providers), Project Management Professional (PMP), Agile Project Management, Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) etc. would be advantageous.
  • Self-motivated with good ownership and able to work independently with initiatives and accountability, a good team player with well-rounded skillset, and can-do attitude who is able to work with officers of all levels.
  • Good communication, written, interpersonal, analytical, presentation and negotiation skills with positive attitude and a keen sense of details.
  • Able to travel overseas occasionally.

Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal

jobTitle: Senior/ Investigation Officer, Investigation Department, FMMD
agencyDescription:
Championing Human Potential for a Thriving Singapore
Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
Foreign Manpower Management Division (FMMD)’s work is to maintain high compliance of the work pass framework and to protect migrant workers (MWs) and migrant domestic workers (MDWs)’ basic rights. This helps businesses get the foreign manpower they need to grow, and thereby provides employment opportunities for locals.

The Investigation Department supports the division’s missions, through ensuring compliance through investigation of breaches, as well as taking enforcement actions against offenders.  Enforcement actions against offenders can include prosecution in Court.
jobResponsibilities:
As an Investigation Officer (IO) in the Investigation Department (FMMD), you conduct investigation into offences under the following legislations:

1)	Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA);
2)	Employment Agencies Act (EAA);
3)	Foreign Employees Dormitories Act (FEDA); and
4)	Prevention of Human Trafficking Act (PHTA).

Through investigations, you play a key role in upholding in maintaining a high level of compliance to MOM’s work pass framework and protecting the basic interests of the migrant workers.  When assigned with a case, you shall identify the potential offences, plan and manage resources required to ensure investigations can be completed on time with the appropriate outcomes.  You are required to conduct interviews and take statements and steer the collection of evidence.  Thereafter, you shall make an assessment based on the evidence gathered, on an appropriate course of action to be taken against the parties investigated. You may have to plan and conduct operations.
You will also be given opportunities to build expertise through cross divisional postings within MOM to grow yourself professionally in the enforcement job function.
jobRequirements:
You should have the following qualities:
• Mission-focused; driven; able to perform under stressful situations; 
• Good time management; able to multi-task effectively
• Meticulous; strives for excellence and quality
• Good writing skills; able to put information together in a cogent manner;
• Analytical and has a curious mind
• Apply good judgement 
• Strong written and communication skills 

Note: Officers may be activated for ad-hoc night/weekend duties due to the nature of the work

It will be good if you have:
• Experience in enforcement and investigation
• A valid Class 3/3A driving license

jobTitle: Manager/Senior Manager, WOG CET Grants Management (RPD)
agencyDescription:
SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Education (MOE). It will drive and coordinate the implementation of the national SkillsFuture movement, promote a culture and holistic system of lifelong learning through the pursuit of skills mastery, and strengthen the ecosystem of quality education and training in Singapore.

SSG will strengthen the adult training infrastructure by taking on all existing functions of the Committee for Private Education (CPE) and guide the Institute for Adult Learning (IAL) to enhance the capabilities and professionalism of adult educators. SSG will play a key role in the quality assurance for private education institutions and adult training centres. Together with educational institutions and training partners, SSG will ensure that students and working adults have access to high quality, industry-relevant training throughout life. SSG will also bring together synergies in continuing education and training (CET) and pre-employment training (PET), so skills requirements will continue to meet the demands of different sectors of the economy.
jobDescription:

The Manager/Senior Manager is an individual contributor responsible for strengthening grants policies and governance within the organisation and at WOG level and engaging stakeholders to ensure compliance and enforceability. The role requires a proactive approach to risk assessment, regular stakeholder engagement, and reasoned judgment in evaluating deviation requests, while safeguarding SWDA’s interests and supporting overall objectives.
The Senior Manager level will be expected to handle work of greater complexity and manage additional projects.
jobResponsibilities:
The Manager/Senior Manager is an individual contributor role who reports to the Team Leader and is part of a team responsible for ensuring funded programmes are aligned with SSG’s funding policies and support SkillsFuture initiatives and SSG’s overall objectives.

The Senior Manager level will be expected to handle work of greater complexity and manage additional projects.

Regulatory Compliance:

  • Stay abreast of regulatory requirements for compliance with WOG’s and SWDA’s grants policies
  • Apply prevailing policies, laws, and regulations relevant to grants

Policy Strengthening:

  • Collaborate with SWDA divisions and other government agencies to strengthen grants policies and governance
  • Articulate policy goals in light of national interest and provide sound policy recommendations

Stakeholder Engagement:

  • Work with SWDA Divisions and other government agencies to monitor implementation and ensure alignment with policy intent

Risk Assessment:

  • Assess requests for deviation from WOG grants governance framework
  • Provide advice on governance, risk management strategies, and potential risk areas

• Manager: Up to 6 years of relevant work experience in grants policies, governance and risk management. Those with no relevant experience but have been involved in relevant projects, short stints in similar areas / functions or relevant course of study can apply
  • Senior Manager: At least 6 years of relevant work experience in grant policies, governance and risk management
  • Good project management and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Good understanding of funding policies and concepts are preferred, but not necessary
  • Familiarity with governance issues, risk management, and compliance matters are preferred, but not necessary
  • Good analytical and critical thinking skills
  • Detail-oriented, meticulous, and systematic
  • Independent and self-motivated, enjoys variety and new challenges, and able to work well in a team

agencyDescription:

jobDescription: SENIOR / EXECUTIVE / ENGINEER, ASSET ENGINEERING (POWER & SERVICES - MECHANICAL/ELECTRICAL)
jobResponsibilities:
You will work closely with the Rail Operators to develop and maintain good ground knowledge of Operation & Maintenance (O&M) issues so as to facilitate the return of the Rail Operators' O&M experience to LTA's design Divisions. - For Electrical Specialisation: Your scope of work will include review of the design of medium voltage power systems, railway traction power systems (3rd rail and overhead catenary systems), low voltage reticulation schemes.

- At least 3 years of experience in design or installation or operation and maintenance

- Knowledge of railway work environment and relevant safety requirements

- Good leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills

- Candidates without experience are also welcomed to apply

agencyDescription:
Master planner. Developer. Since its inception in 1968, JTC has played a strategic role in ensuring Singapore stays innovative, dynamic, and sensitive to global manufacturing trends.

A government agency under Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, JTC is paving the way forward for Singapore’s industrial landscape by championing clean, green and smart estates such as one-north, Seletar Aerospace Park, Jurong Innovation District, and Punggol Digital District. It is developing infrastructure, systems and initiatives that bridge cutting-edge technology and human skill to fuel growth.  

JTC is also bringing businesses and communities together through green spaces, cultivating an environment that is not only sustainable but nurtures ideas shaping the future.
jobDescription:
You will help the existing customer facing teams:
•	recover units in estates earmarked for redevelopment;  and 
•	follow-up on cases which require rectification of breaches within customers’ units.
jobResponsibilities:
You will manage customers whose units have existing breaches which need to be regularized. This includes engaging customers and other relevant stakeholders and finding solutions to address such breaches and monitor such cases until they are regularized or addressed.  

You will also be involved in other aspects such as: 
1. Developing alternative approaches to helping these customers address their breaches; and 
2. Revising current process in identifying and resolving breaches.
jobRequirements:
* Prior experience in facilities management or real estate. 
* Minimum 2 years of relevant work experience with keen interest in the Real Estate industry and engaging SMEs/micro-SMEs 
* Strong interpersonal and communication skill 
* Ability to work independently and in a team construct
* Positive attitude and resilient 
* Resourceful, problem solver and able to multi-task

jobDescription: Are you someone who relishes challenges and is constantly on the lookout for ways to enhance processes and financial controls? If so, we have just the job for you.
jobResponsibilities:
As a key member of our Payments Team, you will play a crucial role in managing financial resources, analysing data and undertaking initiatives that improve the efficiencies and controls of Finance procedures.

You will also get to:
• Ensure compliance with financial regulations and guidelines
• Conduct process reviews and implement process improvement initiatives
• Perform reporting using data analytics or data visualisation tools
jobRequirements:
You have:
• A background in Accountancy or other relevant professional qualification with working experience in Finance's payment operations
• Experience in SAP and in using data analytics tools

You are:
• Meticulous – You achieve thoroughness and accuracy when accomplishing tasks
• A team player – You have the ability to work both independently and collaboratively
• Adaptable – You are versatile and can respond flexibly to rapidly changing situations or requirements
• An excellent communicator – You communicate clearly and concisely with a range of stakeholders, both in writing and verbally

jobDescription:
GovTech supports various Government Agencies in carrying out ICT delivery services and appoints Agency Chief Information Security Officers (ACISO) to oversee information security management within these agencies. The ACISO is a leadership role that requires technical proficiency demonstrated in multiple cybersecurity domains. The role demands knowledge and/or practical experience in most of the domains below:

  • Cybersecurity Governance frameworks,
  • Security Operations including incident response,
  • Architecture design and threat risk assessment,
  • Security Testing.

The ACISO must possess technical understanding of both on-premises infrastructure security and cloud security architectures across major platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, and GCP), including their native security features, identity management systems, and security control implementations.

[What you will be working on]

Emplaced in public agencies and reporting to the agency’s Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Ministry Family CISO, you will collaborate with various stakeholders (GovTech HQ teams, Agency management, Agency project teams, and outsourced vendors) and will be responsible to:

  • Lead the agency-level cybersecurity function in supporting agency digital transformation initiatives whilst ensuring digital resilience of agency systems.
  • Formulate and implement agency cybersecurity strategies, policies and work plans, ensuring continuous alignment with Ministry Family's business strategic goals
  • Review and enhance risk management through threat-based risk assessments, risk mitigations, risk monitoring and reporting.
  • Provide consultation and endorse risk management and mitigation plans from agency’s project teams.
  • Govern and enhance the agency's security posture by maintaining visibility and oversight of ICT assets, security architectures, and cybersecurity operations code of practices.
  • Develop and maintain incident response plan and playbooks. This involves planning, designing and conduct of security incident response workshops and exercises (table-top exercises, simulation and drills) as well as lead the investigation and management of ICT security incidents.
  • Provide advisory and recommendations on appropriate cybersecurity technologies to be deployed that meets agency’s business requirements and aligned with WOG-wide advisories and practices.
  • Ensure secure by design ICT product development, and that security controls implementations comply with the defined security policies, standards and guidelines.
  • Develop and maintain effective cybersecurity awareness and training programmes


[What we are looking for]

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related Technology field
  • At least 8-10 years of management experience related to information security and solid grasp of ICT operations, security policies, business processes and the relationship between them.
  • Ability to work with multi-functional, multi-disciplined teams to formulate, institute real time awareness of security posture and baseline among end users.
  • Good interpersonal and partner/executive leadership skills.
  • Demonstrate knowledge and experience in security by design implementations, review of system architecture, devsecops practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and securing CI/CD pipelines 
  • Demonstrate understanding of cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), coupled with a strong understanding of core cloud services and modern cloud-native architectures (serverless, containers, microservices)
  • Identify on-premises and cloud-specific cybersecurity risks and threats, demonstrating skills to thoroughly assess their impact and likelihood. This assessment encompasses, but is not limited to, secure configurations, insider threats, vendor risks, data leakage, malwares including ransomware, account hijacking, and compliance risks.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies for on-premises and cloud-related cybersecurity and data security issues.
  • Display understanding of emerging threats and technologies, and the ability to translate risk into business impact
  • Strong understanding of compliance requirements and the ability to identify potential violations in on-premises or cloud environments.
  • Able to communicate cyber security topics effectively to senior stakeholders.
  • Minimally possess CISSP certification, preferably with other related certifications, e.g. CISM, CCSP, GCIH that demonstrates continuous learning and knowledge of industry best practices.
  • We believe in being Agile, Bold and Collaborative, and are looking for people who identify with these values.
  • Singaporeans only.

GovTech Data Practice


The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

Today, most organisations still struggle with data that is fragmented, inconsistent, and hard to use, alongside AI that is powerful but brittle without strong data foundations, and privacy policies that are difficult to operationalise. We are changing that at a national scale.

We are reimagining data engineering itself through AI for Data Engineering (AIDE), which introduces self-improving data pipelines that detect, fix, and optimise themselves, AI-assisted data modelling and quality management at scale, and semantic, context-aware data layers that make data instantly usable for AI. Underpinned by standardised, AI-native architectures, this ensures every agency can build strong foundations from day one.

At the same time, a Trusted Data Nation only works if data can be used without compromising privacy or security. We operationalise Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) into real capabilities, including federated computing to unlock insights without moving data, differential privacy and synthetic data to enable safe sharing, and trusted execution environments to compute on sensitive data securely. Alongside this, we build the golden paths for Singapore by creating reference architectures, reusable components, standard data platforms, and engineering playbooks that scale quality across government.

    a. Explore AI possibilities that can supercharge data engineering processes.

    and beyond Singapore.
    d. Build an AI-ready Singapore.

GovTech Data Practice

The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

A core focus of our work is advancing responsible data use. As data sharing and AI adoption accelerate, we develop both the frameworks and technologies needed to ensure sensitive data can be used safely; including in AI systems, where interactions with sensitive data are becoming more widespread and risks will scale further with more autonomous, agentic workflows.

A core focus of our work is to make responsible data use practical and scalable. This includes developing technical guardrails, privacy-preserving workflows, evaluation methods, and reusable standards that help agencies use data safely for analytics, AI, and digital services. Our work spans areas such as AI privacy, context-aware anonymisation, synthetic data generation, federated AI / computing, encrypted computation, differential privacy, and confidential computing. We bridge the gap between policy, research, and real-world deployment by experimenting with new approaches, validating them through agency pilots, and operationalising them into standards, implementation guides, and central government tools.

Frontier exploration and evaluation. Systematically scanning, experimenting with, and interpreting the latest AI developments across vision, video, audio, and document modalities. Agency engagement and transformation. Translating frontier AI capabilities into real outcomes for government agencies. jobTitle: Deputy Director, Government Incident Reporting Ops
jobDescription:
Role Purpose

The Deputy Director (DD), Government Incident Reporting Ops, leads a high-performing operational team responsible for centralizing, assessing, and managing the full spectrum of Whole-of-Government (WOG) incident reports across all Singapore Government agencies.

The scope of coverage is multi-disciplinary, encompassing cybersecurity/data incidents, physical security breaches, public-facing service disruptions, and general operational failures. The DD ensures swift severity assessment, accurate fact-gathering, and seamless leadership escalation, while driving a WOG continuous learning culture to prevent systemic recurrence.

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Domain Operational Leadership

  • Lead daily operations for the WOG Incident Reporting framework, ensuring all submissions across cyber, physical, and operational domains are triaged and validated accurately.
  • Demonstrate sharp acumen to make critical judgment calls on complex, multi-domain incidents, ensuring appropriate escalation and containment strategies are triggered according to SOPs.
  • Review and refine high-quality, high-stakes incident summaries and assessments for senior leadership presentation under tight timelines.

Process Optimization & Culture Building

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to streamline the reporting workflow, leveraging technology to make reporting frictionless and encourage timely submissions from all agencies.
  • Foster a "Just Culture" across the public service, prioritizing psychological safety so agencies report incidents transparently without fear of blame.

WOG Knowledge Management & Continuous Learning

  • Transform diverse incident data into actionable insights, identifying trends and cross-domain vulnerabilities.
  • Develop effective mechanisms (e.g., cross-agency sharing sessions, post-incident reviews, systemic playbooks) to ensure lessons are institutionalized WOG.

Talent Development

  • Mentor and develop team officers, uplifting their technical literacy across different incident domains and honing their analytical capabilities.

Requirements & Qualifications

Technical & Domain Knowledge (Critical)

  • Cross-Domain Literacy: Strong foundational knowledge across IT infrastructure, Cybersecurity operations, and Physical Security frameworks. Must be able to speak the language of both tech engineers and physical security teams.
  • Incident Triage Expertise: Familiarity with incident classification models, threat landscapes, and standard risk matrix frameworks across both digital and physical environments.

Professional Experience

  • Experience in Large-Scale Operations: At least 8 years of professional experience managing complex operations, incident response, crisis management, or operational risk.
  • Organizational Scale: Proven track record of navigating and operating effectively within large, complex organizations (e.g., Multi-National Corporations (MNCs), major financial institutions, critical infrastructure operators, or public sector agencies).
  • Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to manage diverse, high-level stakeholders and navigate matrixed organizational structures or multi-party ecosystems.
  • Public Sector Familiarity (Preferred but not mandatory): Prior experience within the Singapore Public Service, or a strong conceptual understanding of Whole-of-Government (WOG) governance structures and inter-agency dynamics, is highly advantageous. Private sector candidates with a strong adaptability to public sector governance are welcome to apply.
  • Process Improvement: Experience in operations design or process optimization (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, Agile) to simplify reporting workflows and drive efficiency.

Critical Skills & Competencies

  • Executive Communication: Exceptional command of written and spoken English. Ability to translate highly technical, ambiguous, or complex incidents (like a zero-day exploit or a complex supply-chain failure) into concise, plain-language briefs for senior management.
  • High-Stakes Diplomacy: Ability to manage sensitive conversations with senior agency leaders, challenging an agency’s self-assessment firmly but tactfully to ensure proper treatment.
  • Data Analytics & Pattern Recognition: Ability to look beyond individual incidents to identify systemic clusters or root causes across the government ecosystem.

Key Personal Attributes

  • Mental Agility & Resilience: Thrives in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment where variables change rapidly during concurrent crises.
  • Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Essential for building trust with stressed reportees during an ongoing incident.
  • Uncompromising Integrity: Absolute discretion in handling highly sensitive, restricted, or politically charged information.

GovTech builds the digital infrastructure behind Singapore's Smart Nation vision. The Data Programme is focused on one of the harder problems in that space: how analysts, engineers, and policymakers across government discover, access, and make sense of data that shapes real decisions.

As a Director / Deputy Director, Design Management, you'd be the most senior design voice in the programme — setting direction, defining what good looks like, and building interaction models that don't really have a playbook yet.

  • You think in systems and interaction paradigms, not just screens

  • You hold a strong point of view and know how to bring senior stakeholders along with it
  • You care as much about whether something gets used as whether it gets built

  • 12+ years of experience, with a track record at principal level — shaping platforms, ecosystems, or systems-scale products in multi-stakeholder environments
  • Deep experience with data-heavy products: search, APIs, dashboards, or developer tooling
  • Technical fluency — comfortable enough with APIs and data models to co-create with engineers, not just hand off to them

What you can expect

A genuinely novel problem and the seniority to shape how it gets solved — this is not an execution role- Work with real consequences: the data infrastructure you help define underpins how government operates and makes decisions

The Engineering Lead in a Product Development Office (PDO) is a modern technical leader - the "Head of Engineering" for a Ministry - someone who’s built, designed, or operated real systems, understands how technology decisions play out in practice, build capability, and can guide teams through the full journey from POC to scale.

[What you will be working on]

As Director/Deputy Director, you extend your leadership across multiple squads executing across multiple delivery threads (as manager of managers or across workstreams through tech leads) or a broader product (or infra) area, ensuring alignment, consistency, and impact across teams.

You oversee multiple squads (including internal staff and/or vendor teams) by setting a unified technical vision and enforcing multi-squad standards that drive measurable impact.

Your responsibilities include coaching EMs and Tech Leads, fostering cross-squad collaboration, and ensuring that your leadership structure remains lean and focused.

You are accountable for delivering consistent outcomes and high-quality solutions by balancing innovative initiatives with essential BAU improvements, making strategic decisions that always benefit the organisation's long-term objectives

Role and Responsibilities

  • Establish a unified architectural vision and technical standards that meets organisational requirements.

  • Set rigorous expectations for security, scalability, and advanced DevOps/SRE practices across squads.

  • Define and champion platform-wide architecture, tools, and practices that improve org-wide scalability, security, and velocity.

  • Ensure systems are sustainable, cost-effective, and adaptable to future needs.

  • Oversee design reviews and drive large-scale initiatives (e.g., major refactoring, system migrations) that yield quantifiable improvements.

  • Ensure that both innovative features and BAU work (tech debt reduction, bug fixes) contribute to efficiency gains and system reliability.

  • Oversee modernisation efforts or major platform migrations within your area of responsibility.

  • Balance innovation with operational excellence, reducing tech debt and delivery friction.

Ownership and Accountabilities

  • Own multi-squad outcomes by setting clear, measurable targets that support the organisation's long-term strategy.

  • Foster a culture of strong accountability where every deliverable meaningfully contributes to the organisation’s goals.

  • Drive engineering outcomes at scale — through delegation, system design, and strategic decisions.

  • Establish a culture of strong ownership where every decision balance organisational benefit, delivery needs, and long-term sustainability.

  • Coach and develop EMs and Tech Leads to enhance their leadership and technical capabilities.

  • Delegate responsibilities effectively, assigning leaders to high-impact opportunities.

  • Identify skill gaps to ensure the right expertise is in place for successful delivery, restructuring teams as needed.

  • Develop senior leaders to operate autonomously across teams.

  • Shape org structures in collaboration with your leads to align talent with opportunity and enable sustainable delivery.

  • Swiftly remove blockers and refine processes to enable sustained delivery and measurable impact across squads.

  • Make strategic decisions that yield sustainable, quantifiable benefits for the organisation.

  • Deliver high-impact outcomes across divisions by swiftly removing blockers and strengthening systems.

  • Exercise decision-making authority with transparency and empathy, ensuring choices reflect the organisation’s values and serve long-term outcomes.

Strategic Alignment

  • Clearly articulate how each squad’s work contributes to the organisation's long-term strategy.

  • Set strategic objectives that integrate immediate needs with multi-year goals.

  • Shape/Contribute to a multi-year engineering direction within your domain that aligns with programme or organisational goals.

  • Make strategic trade-offs visible and align investments with public-sector impact.

  • Drive data-driven decisions that avoid short-term fixes and yield scalable, transformative impact.

  • Communicate clearly and influence senior stakeholders across functions to align on priorities, trade-offs, and long-term investments.

  • Drive long-range plans for systems and people development, and rigourously measure the outcomes.

  • Champion security, interoperability, and scalability in decision-making.

Cultural and Organisational Influence

  • Serve as a strategic ambassador for the organisation's engineering standards, setting a vision for a lean, high-performing organizational culture.

  • Establish high expectations for transparency, accountability, and agility across divisions.

  • Build high-trust, inclusive engineering cultures at scale by modeling leadership values and aligning systems to sustain them.

  • Set and reinforce engineering standards, transparency, and accountability across your domain.

  • Partner with senior leaders to promote a high-trust, inclusive culture within and across your teams.

  • Support EMs in reinforcing leadership expectations and accountability norms.

  • Identify emerging skill gaps and work with senior stakeholders to evolve team structure for agility and clarity of ownership.

  • Contribute to strategic hiring initiatives to strengthen your area’s leadership pipeline and promote internal career mobility.

  • Coach EMs and Tech Leads to lead autonomously and uphold high delivery standards.

  • Drive strategic hiring aligned with future team direction and gaps.

  • Lead succession planning by identifying high-potential leaders and preparing them to take on greater scope.

  • Continuously reshape teams to improve agility, clarity of ownership, and cross-squad mobility.

  • Delegate effectively to EMs and Tech Leads, enabling them to take ownership of outcomes and scale their impact.

  • Share team-level learnings and operational improvements across relevant squads or programme areas.

  • Build a resilient, high-performing leadership team that delivers strategic outcomes reliably.

  • Influence organisational engineering culture and technical policy across functions.

  • Support transparent and fair performance management across your domain.

  • Partner with senior stakeholders across organisations to align priorities and secure resourcing or policy support.

[What we are looking for]

  • Experienced across the full product lifecycle — comfortable with problem framing, rapid experiments, POC/POV learning loops, and scaling systems into secure, reliable, maintainable services.

  • Technically credible — has coded, built, or designed production systems and can discuss implementation trade-offs with confidence.

  • Practical product-delivery mindset — knows when to optimise for speed, when to simplify, and when to invest in architecture, reliability, and interoperability as systems evolve.

  • Cross-practice collaborator — partners naturally with Product and Design to make good decisions together.

  • Clear communicator — can explain technical options and risks to Ministry CIOs, business owners, and engineers alike.

  • Outcome-oriented — focuses teams on the real-world impact of the work, ensuring decisions link to user value, organisational goals, and public good.

  • Ecosystem thinker — balances the needs of individual product teams with Ministry-wide alignment, reusability, and capability growth.

  • Secure and reliable by design — incorporates these principles early, not after delivery.

  • Curious and evolving — keeps up with modern practices like AI-assisted development and platform automation.

jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. [What you will be working on]

We are looking for an Engineering Lead to lead the software engineering capability for digital products and platforms that improve staff productivity, workflow efficiency and employee experience across the organisation. This role provides hands-on technical leadership for product teams, ensuring that solutions are well designed, securely built, reliably delivered and aligned with enterprise architecture, security and integration standards.

The Engineering Lead will manage and guide software engineers, establish sound engineering practices, and work closely with Product Managers, the Solution Architect, security, operations and business stakeholders to translate product needs into secure, scalable and maintainable digital solutions. The role is suited for an experienced engineering leader who can balance delivery pace, technical quality, team development and long-term sustainability.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The Engineering Lead is expected to guide technical decisions, review designs and code where needed, support complex troubleshooting, and ensure engineers are set up to deliver production-grade products effectively.

  • Lead and manage the software engineering team, including Senior Software Engineers and junior developers, across one or more digital products or platforms.
  • Provide hands-on technical leadership across frontend, backend, APIs, databases, integrations, automation and AI-enabled product capabilities.
  • Set engineering standards, ways of working and delivery expectations across code quality, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation, supportability and secure-by-design development.
  • Review and guide product-level technical designs, including application architecture, integration patterns, data flows, API design, operational support model and implementation approach.
  • Ensure technical designs are secure, scalable, maintainable and aligned with enterprise architecture, security, cloud and integration standards, working closely with the Solution Architect.
  • Partner Product Managers and business stakeholders to translate user needs and operational problems into practical technical options, delivery plans and product increments.
  • Guide engineers in evaluating build, configure, buy and integrate options, and recommend pragmatic approaches that balance user value, delivery speed, cost, risk, maintainability and long-term sustainability.
  • Oversee engineering delivery across product teams, ensuring that solutions are production-ready, reliable, supportable and delivered with appropriate technical discipline.
  • Identify engineering risks, technical debt, dependencies and blockers early, and escalate with clear options and recommendations.
  • Support troubleshooting of complex production issues, root cause analysis and implementation of durable fixes and improvements.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, support hiring and onboarding, and build capability in full-stack development, integration, automation, cloud, DevOps and AI-enabled product delivery.
  • Guide the practical use of AI-enabled services such as enterprise search, summarisation, recommendation, workflow assistance and intelligent automation, ensuring responsible use and sound engineering controls.
  • Work with vendors or delivery partners where applicable to maintain engineering quality, technical accountability and knowledge transfer.
  • Foster a healthy engineering culture that values ownership, quality, learning, collaboration and pragmatic delivery.

[What we are looking for]

  • Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong software engineering experience designing, building and operating production-grade applications and digital products.
  • Experience leading engineers, mentoring developers, setting engineering standards and improving team practices.
  • Strong full-stack engineering understanding, including frontend applications, backend services, APIs, databases, cloud platforms, CI/CD pipelines and application operations.
  • Experience with enterprise integrations, workflow automation, SaaS platforms, APIs, middleware or internal productivity tools.
  • Solid understanding of software architecture, application security, testing strategies, observability, reliability and supportability.
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound product-level technical design decisions and align solutions with enterprise architecture, security and integration standards.
  • Ability to work closely with Product Managers and business stakeholders to translate product needs into practical technical solutions and delivery plans.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, sound technical judgement and ability to navigate ambiguity in early-stage product development.
  • Clear communication skills, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs, risks and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience managing or guiding vendors, delivery partners or cross-functional engineering teams will be an advantage.
  • Practical familiarity with AI-enabled services, automation, enterprise search, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation or intelligent workflow features will be an advantage.
  • Experience in public sector, regulated environments, enterprise platforms or staff-facing digital products will be an advantage.

Developer Productivity and Service (DPS) is building a Central Product Marketplace, the single platform through which agencies subscribe, provision, and manage GovTech's central products. Console is the engine at its core, with a clear organisational mandate: every GovTech platform product should be fully subscribable, billable, and operable through it. This is a product with real momentum, a clear mandate, and a large pipeline of central products to bring on board fully.

What you'll own:

Console is the command centre for agencies: where they subscribe, get billed, provision access, and manage GovTech products. Right now, most central products are only partially integrated. Your job is to change that: making Console the complete operational home for agencies and the default go-to-market platform for product teams, rather than one of many portals they have to deal with.

You are expected to:

  • Own the Console product roadmap and drive central products through the full integration journey, from being listed, to subscribable, to billed, to fully operable, at scale.

  • Consolidate various Console surfaces into one, so agencies deal with one subscription surface.

  • Reduce the time it takes for an agency to go from starting onboarding to being ready to use a product. This is Console's most important outcome.

  • Make Console genuinely valuable to product teams, not just a mandate they comply with. Surface demand signals, reduce their GTM overhead, and make integration worth their while.

  • Work closely with the Product Portal and Developer Portal PMs so the agency journey holds together across the full funnel.

You do this by:

  • Shipping and iterating on onboarding, approvals, billing, and management plane workflows with your engineering and design team.

  • Running structured engagement with central product teams across GDP to unblock integrations and build a repeatable playbook for getting products fully live on Console.

  • Defining and tracking the metrics that reflect whether agencies and product teams are actually getting value, not just whether products are listed.

  • Partnering with TMO to align integration timelines with product teams' own priorities.

  • Building the instrumentation needed to trace agency journeys end-to-end, so the team can see where things stall and fix them.

You will ultimately be responsible for Console becoming the operational backbone of the Central Product Marketplace.

Who we're looking for:

We are seeking an independent individual with a strong grasp of product management fundamentals.

  • 6 to 12 years in product management. Years of experience are a rough guideline.

Role Summary
We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to build Ministry of Education (MOE)'s geospatial and spatial modelling capabilities to strengthen long-term infrastructure and space planning. The role focuses on developing models, tools, and a geospatial foundation that helps MOE anticipate future demand, optimise school locations, and make evidence-based planning decisions.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Build MOE’s Spatial Modelling Engine (Primary)
    • Develop spatial models that forecast future education demand based on housing growth, demographics, migration patterns, land-use plans, and accessibility.
    • Create multi-year scenarios to support decisions on new schools, mergers, campus shifts, capacity planning, and infrastructure renewal.
    • Integrate datasets and insights from other government agencies such as URA, SLA, LTA, DOS, HDB, and GovTech into MOE’s planning logic.
    • Translate planning and policy needs into clear modelling requirements.
  2. Establish MOE’s Geospatial Data & Platform Foundation (Secondary)
    • Build and maintain the authoritative geospatial data layers for MOE (school locations, travel-time layers, catchments, urban constraints, environmental layers).
    • Develop internal APIs, standards, and governance rules to ensure accurate, consistent, and accessible geospatial data.
    • Work with engineering and data teams to set up the geospatial platform that powers analytic tools and downstream products.
  3. Integrate Geospatial Capabilities into MOE Products (Secondary)
    • Embed mapping and location-intelligence features into existing MOE planning and operating tools such as School Cockpit+
    • Improve decision-making workflows using map-based interfaces and visual analytics.
    • Work with planners, policy officers, and product teams to ensure geospatial tools meet real operational needs.
What Success Looks Like
  • A working spatial-modelling engine that planners trust for long-term demand forecasting.
  • A central geospatial platform used across MOE for planning and operational decisions.
  • Planning teams have clear, data-backed insights to guide school infrastructure decisions.
  • Geospatial features are embedded meaningfully into key MOE products.
  • Strong cross-agency partnerships that improve data quality and modelling accuracy.
Candidate Profile
  • Experience developing geospatial products, planning tools, or modelling systems.
  • Familiarity with spatial data (GIS platforms such as ArcGIS, routing engines, geospatial APIs, 3D/2D mapping).
  • Able to work with complex demographics, land-use, and transport data.

You would also need to coordinate with multiple WOG product teams to bring a best of class delivery to IMDA.

This is a forward-deployed role: you will be a GovTech product leader embedded within Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), working day-to-day alongside agency stakeholders, policy owners, and design and engineering teams. The role blends deep, hands-on product ownership with leadership of a small and growing team of product managers. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, shape the direction of your area, and invest meaningfully in the people around you.

[What you will be working on]

Building the product function
You will establish how product is done on Digital Access — the operating model, the ceremonies, the discovery and delivery rhythm, and the standards for prioritisation and product craft. You will lead and grow a small team of product managers, set the bar for product thinking and execution, and create genuine opportunities for them to stretch. Just as importantly, you will partner with the existing business analysts and engineers as the team builds its product practice together — identifying those with product-management potential and coaching them toward it. You will contribute to raising hiring and assessment standards as the team scales.

Product strategy & execution
You will own the strategy and roadmap for your product area — translating complex business, regulatory, and technical inputs into a sequenced, measurable plan. You will set OKRs and success metrics, drive discovery, and make clear, well-documented prioritisation trade-offs. Drawing on user research, industry feedback, and platform data, you will validate or rule out ideas before development begins, and lead end-to-end execution to a high standard of quality, security, accessibility, and compliance. You will champion speed and simplicity within a large problem space while remaining clear-eyed about technical debt.

Agency partnership
Embedded within IMDA, you will help strengthen the product partnership between GovTech and IMDA. This means partnering with business and policy stakeholders to translate needs into well-framed product outcomes, and helping shape a sustainable operating model for how the two organisations collaborate on Digital Access. You will role-model the standards — prioritisation rigour, evidence-based decisions — that raise the bar for how the work is done.

Digital Access spans several government agencies, industry players, and vendor partners. You will build alignment through evidence, trust, and well-earned relationships — resolving complex dependencies, navigating competing requirements, and securing senior-management support for product strategy and investment. When stakeholder conflicts arise, you will be expected to facilitate solutioning toward strategic outcomes.

Job Summary

GovTech is looking for a Lead/Senior Product Manager to drive key strategic initiatives of AI Programme. Our mission is to transform the public sector from "digitally enabled" to "AI-augmented," building a suite of high-impact AI products and shared capabilities that empower government agencies to innovate at scale.

As a Lead/Senior PM, you will oversee a broad portfolio that bridges the gap between foundational AI capabilities and frontline user applications. You are responsible for ensuring that AI interventions are safe, performant, and seamlessly integrated into the daily workflows of public officers. You will lead the "AI Uplift," setting the standards for how the government builds, deploys, and trusts artificial intelligence.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Leadership & AI Vision

  • Develop and communicate a multi-year product strategy for a suite of products within AI Programme that aligns with national digital ambitions and agency-specific needs.
  • Ensure that modular AI capabilities (e.g. generative AI, agentic workflows) integrate into a cohesive ecosystem rather than fragmented tools.

2. Product Execution & Governance

  • Drive the end-to-end product lifecycle for the most complex initiatives within the programme, from initial discovery and "messy" problem-solving to large-scale deployment.
  • Balance the "Trust Deficit" in AI by making critical calls on model accuracy, hallucination management, and operational readiness for critical government tasks.
  • Prioritize high-value use cases that offer the greatest "uplift" in productivity or service delivery across the whole of government.

3. Agency Engagement & Discovery

  • Lead deep-dive discovery sessions with agency heads to identify "operational fragmentation" and visualize how AI can streamline disjointed systems.
  • Translate broad operational challenges into concrete technical requirements for engineering teams, ensuring solutions are operationally compliant and "effortless to use."

4. Mentorship & Product Excellence

  • Mentor Product Managers, fostering a culture of rapid experimentation, data-driven iteration, and user-centric design.
  • Establish "Best-in-Class" AI Product Management frameworks for GovTech, including success metrics focused on time-saved, friction reduction, and accuracy.

What You Will Bring

  • Strategic Depth: 10+ years of experience in Product Management, with a proven track record of leading large-scale technology platforms or AI-driven digital transformations.
  • Technical Fluency: A strong conceptual understanding of AI/ML (LLMs, Agentic workflows, RAG, and Computer Vision) and the ability to navigate architectural discussions with Lead Engineers.
  • Systems Thinking: The ability to see the "big picture"—understanding how a single AI capability can be leveraged across multiple government domains to create a multiplier effect.
  • Stakeholder Influence: Exceptional ability to align senior leadership, developers, and non-technical stakeholders around a shared product roadmap.

What we offer you:

GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.   

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs.

Job Summary

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.

You will own a dual-track roadmap:

  • For Developers: Building the "Safety Stack"—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
  • For Governance and Observability: Architecting the "Governance Layer"—observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard

  • Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
  • Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance "invisible" for developers.
  • Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).

2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails

  • Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
  • Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that "Safety-by-Design" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
  • Build real-time monitoring tools to detect "jailbreak" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.

3. Bridging Policy & Code

  • Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
  • Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.

4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability

  • Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.

What You Will Bring

  • Senior Product Leadership: Proven experience managing complex technical products, specifically those focused on Security, Governance, or AI/ML infrastructure.
  • AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
  • The "Translator" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
  • Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
  • Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an "accelerant" rather than a "roadblock."

[About the Team]

At MOE, our mission is to empower every learner to achieve their fullest potential and to build a future-ready nation through a dynamic and inclusive education system. We are dedicated to cultivating an environment that nurtures innovative teaching practices, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. Our mandate is to shape policies and drive initiatives that not only enhance the quality of education but also integrate digital advancements and global best practices—ensuring that our educators and students are well-prepared to navigate and excel in an ever-evolving world.

Joining MOE DXD’s Tf(x) team will place you at the forefront of transforming education through technology. As part of our innovative unit, you will create bespoke tools tailored specifically for educators, empowering them to streamline processes, enrich classroom experiences, and inspire the next generation of learners. In this role, your technical expertise will intersect with visionary educational goals. This is an opportunity to drive meaningful change in a dynamic environment where creativity, collaboration, and cutting-edge technology converge to shape the future of education.

Expect yourself to collaborate with experienced educators, product/ops managers, software engineers and designers to rapidly prototype innovative solutions that tackle key challenges in the education sector. You will be working in an environment that encourages continuous learning through hands-on guidance and mentorship. Be prepared to utilise a continuous integration engineering pipeline and an iterative design process to streamline both development and testing.

[What you will be working on]

You will work in Tf(x), a team of product/ops managers, software engineers and designers (formerly Transform): “We're a dynamic team, equally driven by our passion for making a positive impact and our dedication to our craft. Whether we're developing robust software or designing user-centric experiences, we ensure that everything we do is delivered at our best.”

Your job scope with our team is as follows:

  • Develop bespoke digital tools to help schools and teachers address their operational and administrative pain-points. You will join a team of software engineers, product managers and designers to establish a digital product team with the broad objective of building bespoke products for MOE officers and educators. This includes data analytics tools for analysing student results, profiling tools to identify at-risk students, and even an ops-readiness digital product to ready schools for emergencies such as COVID-19. Much of the work will be synthesised from hackathons, user discovery sessions, workshops and rapid prototyping.
  • Modernise the School Cockpit IT system and reorganise the engineering team structure. The School Cockpit is a critical system used by schools and educators for school administrative tasks and aggregating student information across Singapore. The vision is for MOE to re-conceptualise this long-standing system into a collection of applications with potential reuseability across the entire MOE ecosystem. Aside from engineering work, there will be an opportunity to work with MOE’s engineering partners in the private sector, and transform the way public-private engineering partnerships have traditionally worked in MOE.
  • Facilitate the transfer of central engineering knowledge from GovTech to MOE. You will be working with a product team who has previously built central products (e.g. SafeEntry, TraceTogether and OurSG Grants Portal) and Artificial Intelligence products that look into the extraction, synthesis and usage of data in government agencies. You will work with the team to actively transfer such intellectual property and know-how gradually into the MOE IT ecosystem, through strategic placement in apps.

[What we are looking for]

  • Demonstrate a solid understanding of responsive web application development and a willingness to enhance your skills.
  • Experience with continuous integration tools is a plus (added advantage). (Note: On-the-job training will be provided if needed.)
  • Possess working knowledge of at least one of the following—or show a willingness to learn:
    • JavaScript (added advantage: experience with React, TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS)
    • Go
    • Python
  • Exposure to any of the following areas is an added advantage, and our team is here to help you grow in these areas:
    • ML/AI/GenAI frameworks
    • Testing methodologies and troubleshooting techniques
    • Cloud application development/deployment fundamentals
    • Common IPC/RPC methods and patterns
    • OS/networking basics
  • Show curiosity in DevSecOps (added advantage).
  • Thrive in a collaborative, high-performing team environment.

jobTitle: Lead UX Designer, Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC)
jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

Who We Are

CCYC (Culture, Community and Youth Cluster) is part of GovTech’s Government Digital Transformation team. We partner with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — including the National Arts Council (NAC), People’s Association (PA), Sport Singapore (SportSG), and MUIS — to deliver digital products that strengthen social cohesion, cultural participation, and youth engagement.

Our product ecosystem spans community engagement platforms, cultural and arts enablement tools, youth development products, and sports and active lifestyle services — used by hundreds of thousands of Singaporeans.

[What you will be working on]

Lead Across the Ecosystem

Where a Senior Designer owns a product, you own the design layer across CCYC’s product portfolio. You see across product lines, identify gaps and inconsistencies, and make deliberate decisions about where to invest design effort for the greatest cross-cluster impact. You bring coherence to an ecosystem of products — without flattening the distinctive needs each one serves.

Mentor and Grow the Team

You actively invest in the development of the designers around you. You give feedback that is specific, actionable and grounded in the work. You create the conditions for others to do their best work — clearing blockers, sharing what you know without being asked, and treating every critique or check-in as an opportunity to build someone’s capability, not just improve a screen.

You notice when a designer is stuck, stretched or struggling, and you engage — not to take over, but to help them find their footing. You don’t measure your success by the quality of your own work alone. You measure it by the standard of the work the whole team produces.

Shape Design Strategy

You work at the intersection of design and product strategy. You contribute to roadmap discussions, bring design’s perspective to prioritisation, and articulate the value of good design in terms that resonate with product managers, engineers and senior leadership. You know when to advocate and when to adapt — and you rarely confuse the two.

You can hold a long view alongside the short one: thinking about where the ecosystem needs to go in 12 to 18 months, while staying close enough to the current work to course-correct in the next sprint.

Own ResearchOps

Research here is not a phase — it’s a discipline that needs infrastructure. You will design and steward the systems that make research sustainable and accessible: participant recruitment pipelines, consent and data governance practices, shared repositories, and frameworks that help the whole team synthesise and apply what they learn.

You ensure that insights don’t live in decks or individuals’ heads — they become institutional knowledge that informs product decisions across the cluster.

Build and Sustain DesignOps

You take responsibility for how design works — the processes, rituals, standards and tooling that determine whether the team can do good work at pace. This includes: maintaining design system governance, running effective critiques and design reviews, managing handoff quality with engineering, and establishing shared norms around file hygiene, documentation and version control.

You treat operations as a design problem: how do we structure the way we work so that quality is the default, not the exception?

Communicate with Clarity and Purpose

Every artefact you produce — a presentation, a brief, a feedback comment, a Slack message — is communication. You are deliberate about what you say, how you say it, and to whom. You match your communication to your audience and your objective. You don’t over-explain and you don’t under-specify.

You are especially clear when things are uncertain or complex. In moments of ambiguity, your communication creates alignment rather than adding noise.

[What we are looking for]

We are looking for a Lead UX Designer to take on both strategic and operational ownership of design across the CCYC product ecosystem. This is a step up from being a strong individual practitioner: you will shape how design is done here, not just what gets designed.

You bring deep craft, but you no longer keep it to yourself. You see the whole ecosystem and the people inside it — and you understand that the quality of the work is inseparable from the health of the team producing it. You make the people around you better, not by pushing them, but by showing them what good looks like and making it easier for them to get there.

You think clearly and communicate with intention. Whether you’re presenting a design direction to senior stakeholders, writing a research brief, or giving feedback in a crit, you say what matters and leave out what doesn’t. You can shift register — from a strategy conversation with leadership to a pairing session with a junior designer — without losing clarity in either.

This is a player-coach role. You will continue to do hands-on design work on complex, high-stakes parts of the product — but you will also be responsible for growing the practice, mentoring others, and owning how design operates at scale across the cluster.

  • Experience: 8+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio that spans product lifecycle ownership, ecosystem-level thinking, and measurable outcomes — not just polished screens.
  • People Development: Demonstrated experience mentoring or managing designers, with clear examples of how you’ve helped others grow their craft, confidence or career trajectory.
  • Strategic Range: Ability to think and operate at both the strategic and execution layer — you can set direction and get into the details when it matters.
  • ResearchOps: Hands-on experience establishing or significantly improving research operations: recruitment, repositories, governance, or synthesis practices at team or organisational scale.
  • DesignOps: Experience owning design operations: design systems governance, crit culture, handoff processes, tooling standards, or documentation frameworks.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You write clearly, present confidently, and can adapt your communication style to different audiences without losing your point.
  • Craft: Strong UX fundamentals — research, information architecture, interaction and visual design — applied with rigour and pragmatism in a live product environment.
