jobTitle: Principal / Lead Product Manager, TradeNet, DEP
jobDescription:
GovTech is Singapore's lead agency for digital government and the Smart Nation initiative. We build and deploy technology that meaningfully improves lives — for citizens, businesses, and the public sector.

Digital Economy Products (DEP) is a division within GovTech that operates with the pace and rigour of a modern product company. Our teams tackle high-stakes problems across Singapore's public sectors — Healthcare, Manpower, Trade and Finance, National Development, Sustainability, and more — and build digital products that serve millions.

Many of Singapore's most critical government systems were built decades ago — pioneering for their time, but now running on aging technology, tightly bound to vendor dependencies, and struggling to keep pace with evolving policy and industry demands. We are bringing these platforms in-house and rebuilding them from the ground up — rethinking not just the technology, but the operating models, user experiences, and regulatory workflows they underpin.

Two flagship programmes are currently underway:

TradeNet — Singapore's National Single Window for trade permit processing. Launched in the late 1980s, it processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export, and transshipment, contributing to approximately 10% of national tax revenues. Designated as critical IT infrastructure, TradeNet is being brought in-house to secure Singapore's technology sovereignty over one of its most consequential trade systems.

CoreNet X — Singapore's national digital platform for regulatory approval of building works. It unifies eight regulatory agencies into a single BIM-based submission and processing system, transforming how the built environment sector interacts with government.

Both programmes sit at the intersection of complex regulation, enterprise-scale technology, and high public-sector impact. As a Principal Product Manager at DEP, you will be at the centre of this transformation — working at the frontier of how government systems are redesigned, rebuilt, and reimagined for the future.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the product strategy for modernisation of your key system(s).
  • Translate complex business, technical, and policy insights into clear roadmaps that align teams and drive measurable outcomes.
  • Establish success metrics (OKRs, KPIs) and ensure alignment with the policy, business, and operational objectives.
  • Build strong stakeholder alignment through evidence, trust, and well-earned relationships — resolving complex dependencies and securing senior management support for product strategy and investments.
  • Develop deep system and domain expertise, serving as the subject-matter expert for your product(s) — bringing informed perspective to agency escalations, regulatory tradeoffs, and decisions that shape product approach across government and industry stakeholders.
  • Champion adoption of emerging technologies and industry best practices to improve team effectiveness and impact.
  • Lead and mentor a team of talented product managers, setting the bar for product thinking, execution rigour, and professional development of each team member.
  • Lead hiring of other product leaders for your team and outside, identify and coach future leaders
  • Lead end‑to‑end product execution of a major product —from ideation to launch to iteration—ensuring high standards of quality, security, accessibility, and compliance.
  • Collaborate with engineering, design, research, operations, and data teams to deliver cohesive, scalable user experiences.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of product management or equivalent experience with strong demonstrated impact in the consumer/enterprise/platform ecosystem.
  • Track record of delivering complex products at scale with measurable business impact.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, capable of inspiring teams and influencing senior leaders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills — ability to navigate complex, multi-agency environments and build alignment across government agencies, vendor partners, and industry players.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to leverage data to inform product decisions.
  • Proven experience hiring, managing, mentoring, and coaching a team of product managers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience modernising or re-platforming complex enterprise systems, B2B applications, or legacy platforms.
  • Domain expertise in trade/customs or building/construction industries.
  • Experience in process optimisation, regulatory technology, or government digital transformation.
  • Prior engineering experience working on complex web applications or enterprise systems.

[What you will be working on]

Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) is a key platform within Singapore Government Technology Stacks to allow government agencies to create high quality and reliable government services for citizens using commercial cloud services. GCC Engineering Team develops the required platform automations, processes, toolchain and policies/best practices to enable government agencies to develop, deploy and operate government services on the cloud in an agile yet secure manner.

If you are looking for opportunities to collaborate with leading industry experts and be surrounded by highly motivated peers, we welcome you to join GCC. These are newly created positions with many opportunities to make a difference!

  • Participate in an in-house engineering squad for engineering excellence in design, development and operational of the Singapore Government Commercial Cloud Platform

  • Opportunities to learn and implement large scale automation with cloud landing zone across multiple Cloud Service Providers in Government Context
  • Responsible to develop and maintain the platform used by multiple government agencies
  • Be the guiding subject matter of expert for Devops methodologies, contribute to Automation, Availability, Scalability and Resiliency to the team and the development communities within government
  • 8+ years of experience in Infrastructure and Platform as a Service using Cloud, Openshift, OpenStack, Vmware
  • Understand about large scale automated infrastructure and network deployment
  • Strong skills in platform network such as BGP, software defined network, firewalls, Anycast, DNS

  • Familiar with cloud services such as AWS, Azure and GCP
  • Appreciate or willing to learn large-scaled distributed systems and their challenges.
  • Familiar with code security and opensource tools in relevant domains
  • Passionate in automation
  • Good to have - practiced Terraform and Bash scripting too
  • Good to have – understand about Cloud Landing Zone such as Control Tower, Terraform Landing Zone, Microsoft Azure CAF
  • Good to have - practiced Site Reliability Engineering principle and familiar with application monitoring tools

[What we are looking for]

  • Strong understanding and appreciation of positive team culture. Care about growing and coaching staff.
  • Passion for automation for large scalable systems ensuring they are highly secured, resilient and highly available.
  • Have strong communication skills and belief in what you are doing.
  • Extremely strong team-player, primary focus is on leveraging your experiences to help the team succeed.
  • Strong contributor and hands-on in all your past experiences.

jobTitle: Principal / Lead Software Engineer (Cybersecurity Specialist) — TradeNet CII
jobDescription:
About GovTech

The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) transforms the delivery of Government digital services by taking an "outside-in" view, putting citizens and businesses at the heart of everything we do. We build the Smart Nation infrastructure and the platforms the public sector runs on, and we partner agencies to engineer trustworthy, resilient digital services at national scale.

What is this role?

TradeNet is Singapore's national single-window trade platform and a legislated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). Its availability and integrity underpin national trade continuity; disruption is an economic event, not a system outage.

We are seeking a Principal / Lead level Software Engineer (Cybersecurity Specialist) to be the technical design authority for the modernised TradeNet CII rebuild, focusing on architecture security and resilience.

This is an architect-and-build mandate, not an assurance or operations role. As a first-line engineering role, you will

  1. Design and embed security and resilience controls into the platform starting from the architecture and down to the implementation details.
  2. Decide what is inherited from the GovTech security tech stack versus built and owned by the product team.
  3. Design the defensive terrain jointly with the Singapore Customs Agency CISO (ACISO) so that the agency can defensibly discharge its CII regulatory accountability to Cyber Security Agency (CSA).

You will be measured on the delivery of TradeNet CII that is secure and resilient by design and construction — not on the volume of findings triaged or evidence produced after the fact.

Impact and outcomes

You will be successful when:

  • TradeNet's security architecture is conformant with CSA CCoP v2 and WOG IM8 by design, not by downstream remediation, and the conformance basis is clearly documented and defensible to CSA.
  • The Customs ACISO can stand behind a coherent, evidenced security and resilience architecture for the CII without reconstructing it from operational artefacts.
  • The platform has an engineered national trade-continuity posture — recoverability, degraded-mode operation, and containment of blast radius are designed properties, not aspirations.
  • The boundary between controls inherited from the GovTech security tech stack and controls owned by the TradeNet product is explicit, maintained, and used to scope CII audit and attestation.
  • Security control intent is expressed as code and continuously monitored, reducing reliance on point-in-time attestation.
  • There is a strong culture of security in the organization through your leadership, mentorship and coaching.

What you will be working on

Secure and resilient architecture (core mandate)

  • Own the reference security architecture for the TradeNet CII: trust boundaries, identity architecture, segmentation and trust-zone strategy, east-west controls, encryption and key management, and blast-radius containment for the CII boundary.
  • Embed secure-by-design controls by working inside product and engineering teams through the delivery lifecycle — at design, solutioning and implementation time, not as post-build validation.
  • Maintain a living threat model per system and trust boundary, referenced to MITRE ATT&CK and to relevant adversary classes (including supply-chain and nation-state), and use it to drive architecture and segmentation decisions — not merely to prioritise remediation.

Resilience and national trade continuity

  • Engineer the platform's recoverability and graceful degradation: degraded-mode operation, recovery objectives appropriate to a national single-window, and containment design that preserves trade continuity under attack.
  • Map and treat dependency and concentration risk across the TradeNet ecosystem (traders, brokers, ports, and partner agencies), including third-party and supply-chain integration risk.
  • Design for, and participate in, CSA-mandated cyber resilience exercising for the CII, feeding findings back into the architecture.

Defensive terrain (with the Customs ACISO)

  • Partner the Customs ACISO as the technical design authority enabling the agency to discharge CII accountability to CSA: design the Customs digital terrain and CII boundary with multi-layered defence, and translate regulatory obligation into architecture rather than into compliance tasks.
  • Co-develop the defensible architecture and resilience narrative the ACISO relies on for CSA engagement, audits, and CII regulatory submissions.

Platform leverage and control inheritance

  • Determine and document what the CII inherits from the GovTech security tech stack (e.g. GCC, central SOC/monitoring, ShipHats pipeline guardrails, IM8 baseline controls) versus what the TradeNet product team must build and own.
  • Maintain the shared-responsibility delineation as an architectural artefact that also scopes CII audit boundaries, so inherited controls are not re-attested.

Continuous assurance and secure delivery

  • Express security control intent as code: pipeline guardrails, policy-as-code, and continuous control monitoring designed into the platform so conformance is observable continuously rather than reconstructed for audits.
  • Champion secure SDLC and agile security practice within the delivery cadence, embedded in engineering teams rather than gating them.

Transitional / Day-2 scope (explicitly secondary)

The following are transitional and not the primary remit. Operational validation of the CLE's own designs sits with an independent assurance line to preserve control independence; the CLE provides engineering guidance, not self-validation:

  • Advisory and incident-response engineering support in coordination with SIRO, ACISO, and GCSOC.
  • Scoping and engineering guidance for external VAPT and vulnerability assessment, with closure validation performed independently.

What we are looking for

  • 10+ years in Cybersecurity as a Software Engineer and not just in the capacity of auditing, pen-testing, operational triage, etc….
  • We need someone that is hands on where the ideal candidate is someone that can design systems to be secure and can sit down to write code if they need to, someone that can coach our engineering teams on how to write better and more secure code, and someone that understands the cybersecurity tooling landscape to help us choose the right tools, we are not looking for a high level theorist / academic.
  • Demonstrated experience with designing security architecture into regulated / critical systems and platforms at the national or whole enterprise level, not just providing testing and assurance but actually designing and implementing.
  • Working command of Singapore regulatory frameworks for critical systems: CSA CCoP v2 for CII and WOG IM8 (Reform), with the ability to translate obligation into architecture and to delineate control inheritance for audit scoping.
  • Strong systems thinking: able to reason about a national platform as an interdependent whole — boundaries, failure modes, recoverability, and concentration risk — not as a checklist of controls.
  • Depth across cloud and platform security architecture (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS), identity, encryption and key management, segmentation and zero-trust patterns, and secure SDLC / policy-as-code.
  • Fluency with architectural and adversary frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, ISO 27001, CIS benchmarks) used to drive design decisions.
  • Ability to operate as a technical design authority alongside a CISO, clearly within the first line, and to produce architecture that withstands regulatory and audit scrutiny.
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting/automation language (e.g. Python, TypeScript, Shell/Bash, etc…) for policy-as-code and tooling.
  • Preferably proficient in both Kotlin/JVM stack and TypeScript.
  • Architecture-leaning certifications are advantageous (e.g. CISSP / CISSP-ISSAP, SABSA, cloud security architecture). Incident-response and offensive certifications are useful but not the primary signal for this role.
  • Subject to personnel security clearance / CII vetting appropriate to access to a national CII.
  • Subject to the nature of the role, onsite presence during fixed hours may be required.

How this role sits in our assurance model

This is a first-line engineering role. The Customs ACISO holds CII risk accountability; an independent assurance function validates and attests. The CLE provides the engineering and architectural substance both rely on, and does not validate or attest to the controls it designs. This separation is deliberate and protects the integrity of the CII assurance chain.

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is responsible for the Government Procurement (GP) policies, which govern how government agencies conduct their procurement. With evolving needs of our public officers and changing procurement landscape, MOF is embarking on the Whole of Government Procurement initiative.

GeBIZ X is the MOF product that would transform the procurement and business experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers.

Our team is made up of passionate individuals committed to solving challenges and driving meaningful change. We embrace diversity of thought, encourage experimentation, and foster a culture of continuous learning. As part of this team, you will lead design direction and collaborate with UX designers, finance officers, and solution providers — forward-thinking professionals equally invested in your growth and in transforming MOF’s corporate finance services.

We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Lead Designer to lead our product team. This individual will play a pivotal role in shaping the vision, strategy, and execution of GeBIZ X product portfolio. The Lead Designer will collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive product innovation, ensure market fit, and deliver exceptional value to our customers.

The Lead Designer leads strategic design initiatives while ensuring alignment with organizational goals. He/She coordinates and plans discovery research, including user interviews, workshops, surveys, usability testing, and gathering insights to understand user needs and pain points; evaluates the usability of new and existing products and makes constructive suggestions for change. Key responsibilities include translating discovery research into actionable insights, creating wireframes and prototypes in Figma, conducting user testing, iterating designs based on feedback, and collaborating closely with product manager, software engineer to deliver user-centric solutions within technical constraints.

Define and Drive Procurement Design Strategy, Roadmap, and Outcomes

  • Develop and own the design vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for end-to-end procurement systems, aligned with MOF's digitalisation priorities.

  • Establish, track, and deliver on design OKRs and success metrics that drive user adoption, operational impact, and continuous improvement.

  • Prioritise design initiatives that maximise value creation and usability for procurement stakeholders, from requisition through contract management and vendor relations.

Enhance Procurement Operations through Human-Centred Design and Systems Thinking

  • Strengthen procurement workflows by embedding user research and data-driven design decisions to support strategic sourcing, vendor evaluation, and contract lifecycle management.

  • Redesign procurement interfaces and experiences through systematic design standards that enable intuitive, multi-stakeholder collaboration across complex technology solutions (eg. SaaS/ Bespoke).

  • Implement design systems and methodologies that proactively identify user friction points and reduce operational risk through detection of usability barriers in procurement processes.

Coach and Develop the Procurement Design Practice

  • Mentor and develop designers and design researchers to build internal capabilities and foster a high-performance, user-focused design culture.

  • Promote cross-functional collaboration between design, product, and engineering teams whilst evangelising design-led problem-solving across the finance and digital teams.

  • Lead the development of design standards, frameworks, and measurement methodologies that demonstrate design impact beyond traditional product metrics in complex government procurement contexts.

Required qualifications, skills and mindset:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Industrial design, Interaction design, Human Computer Interaction (HCI), Visual Arts or similar; Master’s degree preferred.

  • Minimum of 8 years of experience in design across multiple industries, with demonstrated success in launching and scaling complex digital products.

  • Proven track record of leading end-to-end design initiatives from discovery through delivery, with measurable impact on user adoption and business outcomes.

  • Strategic design thinking with strong analytical and synthetic capabilities, including the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive design initiatives that align with organisational objectives.

  • Experience with agile methodologies and full product lifecycle management, particularly in complex enterprise software environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, translating user needs into strategic design decisions that balance business goals with user outcomes.

  • Expert-level proficiency in design methodology with exceptional attention to detail and deep understanding of how users engage with complex digital systems.

  • Advanced skills in design and research tools including Figma, Miro, and project management platforms such as Jira.

  • Strong foundation in design principles, typography, and accessibility standards (WCAG), with experience applying these in government or regulated environments.

  • Passion for public good is a strong plus.

Key Competencies :

  • Product Leadership: Ability to define strategy, own outcomes, and lead multi-year product execution.

  • Data-Driven Decision-Making: Able to translate data into actionable insights and financial intelligence.

  • User-Centric Thinking: Designs with users in mind, balancing operational workflows with intuitive UX.

  • Systems Thinking: Comfortable working across a complex organisation with diverse stakeholders and processes.

  • Coaching & Team Growth: Skilled in mentoring others and building high-performing product teams.

[What you will be working on]

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager, Deputy Director to join our team at the Ministry. This is a role for someone who operates at the intersection of deep product craft, strategic leadership, and organisational influence — someone who doesn't just build great products, but shapes how an entire department thinks about and delivers them.

As a Principal PM, you will own outcomes at Ministry HQ level, mentor the next generation of product leaders, and drive alignment across teams on strategy, execution, and culture. You will be expected to lead through influence as much as through authority, and to leave the organisation meaningfully better than you found it.

Your core responsibilities include:

Product Strategy and Execution
You will lead the development of product strategy grounded in user insights, market dynamics, and organisational goals. You are the person others turn to when facing complex, ambiguous problems — guiding junior product managers on how to perform rigorous analysis and translate findings into sound product decisions. You will be accountable for balancing short-term delivery speed against long-term technical debt, and for fostering a team culture defined by speed, simplicity, and agility.

Divisional Ownership
You will take full accountability for the success of the CIO Office division — contributing to the definition of goals and outcomes, and driving their achievement. This means identifying and removing systemic inefficiencies, advocating for the tools and processes teams need, and driving ownership and accountability across multiple teams. When challenges arise, you act decisively; when opportunities emerge, you move quickly to seize them.

Strategic Alignment
You will translate divisional goals into a coherent theory of success, working with teams to develop OKRs and long-term roadmaps. You proactively anticipate systemic risks and changes, and take initiative to lead workstreams that keep the ministry HQ moving in the right direction. You are comfortable operating across teams and functions, ensuring that effort is aligned and that progress is visible.

Culture and Organisational Influence
You will shape the culture of the division — championing open communication, continuous improvement, and genuine collaboration. You build and maintain strategic cross-functional partnerships, facilitate high-stakes discussions, and ensure that diverse perspectives are heard and acted upon. You are willing to make structural changes where needed to help teams operate more effectively.

People Leadership
You will align division goals with broader ministry HQ objectives, setting high standards while empowering the people around you. You coach people managers and senior leaders, conduct regular one-on-ones with direct and indirect reports, and lead recruitment efforts to bring in and develop top talent. You take an active interest in team health — gathering feedback, providing the right resources and infrastructure, and keeping teams motivated and engaged over the long term.

[What we are looking for]

  • You have a strong track record of product leadership in complex, fast-moving environments.

  • You are as comfortable shaping strategy in the boardroom as you are rolling up your sleeves to help a junior PM work through a difficult problem.

  • You lead with clarity and conviction, but remain genuinely open to other perspectives.

  • You understand that at this level, your most important output is not the products you ship directly, but the capability, culture, and direction you build around you.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you will work at the intersection of policy, operations, and technology, leading cross-functional teams to reimagine and rebuild mission-critical enforcement workflows into modern, scalable digital products.

What is Enforcement 2.0 (ENF2.0)

ENF2.0 is LTA’s next-generation enforcement transformation initiative.

It aims to:

  • Modernise legacy enforcement systems and workflows
  • Enable end-to-end digital enforcement journeys
  • Improve operational efficiency and decision-making for enforcement officers
  • Integrate data across systems to support smarter, more proactive enforcement
  • Build modular, scalable platforms that can evolve with policy and operational needs

This includes areas such as:

  • Case management for enforcement officers
  • Workflow automation and rule engines
  • Data-driven insights and analytics for enforcement actions

The programme adopts a product-led, agile, and discovery-first approach, moving away from traditional system delivery.

Strategic Leadership

What the role is

Product Managers make sure the right things get done. At a high level, this means establishing a clear vision for what a product should be and charting the path to get there. Day-to-day, it means handling all the different facets of a product — user needs, technical constraints, and design goals — and keeping them coordinated.

In the Data Programme, this role sits at the intersection of policy, engineering and data science. You will need to be technically credible enough to work closely with engineers and data scientists, while being user-focused enough to translate complex capabilities into products that agency users actually find useful and intuitive.

What You Will Do

Understand users deeply

You will conduct user studies to understand the needs and problems of agency users, analyse usage data to uncover patterns that inform product decisions, and research the landscape to understand existing and competing solutions. The goal is to know your users better than anyone else on the team.

Make good product decisions

You will work with designers to create intuitive user experiences, develop multiple proposals for how a product could take shape, and lead the team to a balanced, well-considered position on what the product should be. This includes creating interfaces and data narratives that make insights immediately accessible to users who may not have technical backgrounds.

Work closely with the engineering team

You will translate product strategy into technical, detailed, and actionable plans for both business and engineering teams. You will understand developers' needs and, where necessary, explore emerging tools and techniques that can meet them. Experience with modern software development practices — CI/CD, DevOps, microservices, TDD/BDD — will help you engage credibly and move work forward.

Drive product growth and adoption

You will drive user adoption through increased engagement, expanded features, and sustainable usage growth. This includes maintaining a network with key user agencies and central government product teams to identify collaboration opportunities, and participating in public-speaking engagements to raise awareness of the product.

Manage resources and planning

You will develop workplans with the product team, manage the product budget through expenditure monitoring and cashflow management, and secure funding where needed. This includes co-creating budget papers with the Product Owner and procuring necessary software, hardware, and ICT professional services.

Communicate across teams and stakeholders

You will explain technical considerations to non-technical audiences, identify and engage key stakeholders — including government agencies, industry partners, and the broader tech community — and coordinate efforts across functions including marketing, legal, and finance. You will also represent the product through presentations and written papers.

Keep things organised

You will run efficient meetings to keep stakeholders and team members updated, prioritise and track what needs to be done, and document key decisions and product information clearly.

Ensure compliance and governance

You will ensure the product meets security and performance requirements (SSAT, VAPT, Performance Testing) and adhere to compliance requirements and audits (IM, AGO, QMS, and others).

[What we are looking for]

We value your aptitude for getting things done and your commitment to continuous learning over formal certifications. That said, the following reflect the genuine hiring signals for this role.

You should have a degree or diploma in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related field, with at least five years of relevant experience. Candidates with more experience will be considered for senior roles.

Beyond the baseline, we are specifically looking for someone who:

  • Has hands-on experience in product management, ideally in a data, platform, or infrastructure context

  • Has worked directly with engineers, designers, and data scientists — and can engage credibly with all three

  • Has practical experience applying data science or machine learning to solve real problems, whether as a practitioner or as a PM working closely with data science teams

  • Has written code or worked in software development, and is comfortable reading technical documentation and participating in technical discussions

  • Is familiar with modern software development practices such as Agile, CI/CD, DevOps, microservices, and TDD/BDD

  • Has awareness of and experience with cloud service offerings

  • Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and can evaluate trade-offs clearly and communicate them well

  • Has good design sense and can distinguish between a product that works and one that users actually want to use

  • Communicates well — in writing, in presentations, and in stakeholder conversations — and can adapt their register for technical and non-technical audiences alike

  • Takes initiative and sees things through without needing to be managed closely

  • Wants to work for the public good, and understands what that means in practice

Prior public service experience is a plus. Relevant certifications such as CITPM, COMIT, PMP, or Certified Scrum Master are welcome but not required.

[About This Role]

We are looking for a Product Manager to work on the development and adoption of a centralised data discovery platform that serves as the single authoritative entry point for public officers across the whole of government to find, evaluate, and request access to government data.

Today, data discovery is fragmented across multiple platforms, each with its own go-to-market effort, onboarding process, and user experience. This creates confusion, duplication, and missed opportunities for data reuse. Your role is to change that — by building a product that becomes the definitive "first stop" for any public officer looking for government data, and by driving the ecosystem-level coordination needed to make that vision real.

This role that sits at the intersection of product, data governance, and cross-agency coordination. You will be responsible for both the strategic positioning of the platform and the day-to-day execution of product improvements — from search experience and catalogue coverage, to request workflows and integration with downstream delivery systems.

[What you will be working on]

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Establishing and Communicating a Clear Product Vision

  • Execute Own and articulate the product vision for a centralised data discovery platform, ensuring alignment across engineering, design, policy, and senior stakeholders

  • Contribute to Define and maintain a coherent product strategy that positions the platform as the single entry point for government data discovery, replacing fragmented multi-platform behaviour

  • Collaborate with programme leadership and agency partners to secure buy-in and drive adoption at scale across government

Driving Catalogue Growth and Coverage

  • ExecuteLead the strategy to expand the platform's central catalogue by working with agency data owners and platform teams to surface more government data in one place — without necessarily requiring agencies to migrate their underlying systems

  • Identify and resolve the technical, operational, and incentive barriers that prevent agency datasets from being discoverable centrally, and develop scalable approaches to address them

  • Work with agency data owners to improve metadata completeness and quality so that datasets are genuinely useful to discover, not just listed

Improving Search, Discovery, and Request Experience

  • Own the end-to-end user experience for data discovery, from search and browse to dataset evaluation, access request, and approval

  • Use search analytics and user research to identify where the discovery journey breaks down — and drive iterative, evidence-based improvements

  • Explore how emerging technologies, including AI, might fundamentally reimagine how users find and evaluate data relevant to their needs — going beyond conventional search to ask what a great discovery experience could look like

  • Ensure that data consumers can assess dataset fitness-for-purpose directly within the discovery experience, without needing to contact data owners separately

Streamlining the Request and Approval Workflow

  • Drive consolidation of the inter-agency data request process into a single, trackable workflow within the platform, reducing fragmentation and improving visibility for both requestors and approvers

  • Work with policy and governance teams to digitalise and simplify approval processes, reducing time from request creation to first data access

  • Enable data providers to manage their sharing obligations — including approvals, rejections, and monitoring — through a single console experience

Reducing Friction Between Discovery and Data Use

  • Investigate and address the gap between a user finding a dataset and being able to actually use it in their work — understanding where friction exists in how data is accessed, integrated, and consumed across different working environments

  • Define and validate approaches that reduce the effort required for users to go from discovery to productive use, without prescribing a fixed technical solution upfront

Driving Adoption and Go-to-Market

  • Develop and execute a go-to-market strategy that consolidates user mindshare around a single discovery platform, replacing fragmented awareness across competing products

  • Build and maintain relationships with key agency stakeholders — both data providers and data consumers — to drive onboarding, usage, and feedback loops

  • Use consolidated user activity data to generate insights that improve the product and demonstrate value to programme leadership and agency partners

Monitoring, Measuring, and Iterating

  • Define and track product metrics that reflect real discovery success (e.g. search success rate, time from request to first access, catalogue coverage) rather than vanity metrics

  • Run structured experiments and user studies to validate product decisions and prioritise the roadmap

  • Maintain a clear, well-reasoned product backlog and communicate trade-offs transparently to stakeholders

Compliance and Governance

  • Ensure the platform meets security, performance, and data governance requirements applicable to a whole-of-government system handling sensitive metadata and access workflows

  • Adhere to compliance requirements and audits (IM8, AGO, QMS, etc.)

[What we are looking for]

The customers for our products are normally agency users, which means that prior public service experience will help. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification.

We look for product managers with:

  • Product management experience, with a demonstrated track record of owning and shipping products used at scale by diverse user groups

  • Experience driving adoption of a platform or tool in a multi-stakeholder environment where you did not have direct authority over all users or contributors

  • Strong product sense — ability to translate ambiguous strategic goals into concrete, prioritised product decisions

  • Proven ability to work directly and effectively with engineers, designers, and data or platform specialists (at least 3 years in cross-functional product teams)

  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable using data to diagnose problems, validate hypotheses, and communicate product performance

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence senior decision-makers and drive alignment across organisations

  • Prior experience with data cataloguing, metadata management, search/discovery products, or developer/analyst-facing platforms

  • Experience working in or with government agencies, or in other large, federated organisations where adoption requires ecosystem coordination rather than top-down mandates

  • Familiarity with data governance concepts (e.g. data stewardship, data classification, access control workflows)

  • Experience designing or improving approval and workflow automation features

  • Exposure to AI-assisted product features, particularly in search or recommendation contexts

  • Specific government data policies, classification frameworks, and inter-agency data sharing processes

  • Technical details of the underlying data infrastructure and delivery mechanisms

  • The specific agency landscape, stakeholder map, and political dynamics of the programme

Requirements

  • Diploma/Degree in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related subject area, with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience. Candidates with more experience will be considered for more senior roles.

  • Prior working experience in product management, IT business analysis, or application solutioning design and testing

  • Experience in modern product development and management practices such as Agile, Design Thinking, and Product-Centric Development will be strongly preferred

  • Relevant certifications such as CITPM, COMIT, PMP, or Certified Scrum Master are advantageous

As a Product Operations Specialist deployed to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), you will drive success by enabling the team to better serve end users and stakeholders of our products. You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, and Customer Success, supporting the Appointment@MOM booking system and the Special Pass issuance and printing systems through various operational activities.

You will serve as the primary point of contact between vendors, the development team, and MOM stakeholders, ensuring that these systems remain reliable, compliant, and continuously improved. You may also play a key role in the modernisation or revamp of the Special Pass issuance and printing systems, contributing to efforts to improve and future-proof these critical services.

[What you will be working on]

System Maintenance & Operations

You will oversee the health and performance of the Appointment@MOM and Special Pass systems, coordinating with technical teams and vendors to resolve incidents, manage system updates, and ensure minimal disruption to operations. You will establish and maintain monitoring routines, track system issues, and drive timely resolution of bugs and service requests.

Drive Operational Excellence

You will implement automated workflows to reduce manual processes and improve team efficiency. You will establish and track metrics that measure both product and operational performance, providing the team with clear visibility into system health and service quality. You will also design and maintain internal knowledge bases to ensure consistent and well-documented support practices across the team.

Vendor, Procurement & Budget Management

You will manage relationships with third-party vendors supporting the systems under your charge. This includes overseeing vendor deliverables, tracking service level agreements (SLAs), conducting performance reviews, and escalating issues where vendors fall short of expectations. You will also support procurement and contract renewal processes, ensuring that vendor engagements remain compliant with government procurement policies and deliver value for money.

Alongside vendor management, you will be responsible for tracking and managing project and operational budgets. This includes monitoring expenditure against approved budgets, flagging variances, supporting budget planning and forecasting cycles, and ensuring that spending decisions are well-justified and aligned with project priorities. You will work closely with internal finance and procurement teams to ensure that all financial processes are followed correctly.

Stakeholder & Project Management

Acting as the bridge between MOM business owners, vendors, and the technical team, you will gather and document requirements, manage change requests, and ensure that enhancements are delivered on time and within scope. You will facilitate regular project meetings, maintain project trackers, and provide status updates to both internal and client stakeholders.

The position requires a deep understanding of both public sector financial management and the rapidly evolving technology landscape that underpins modern government operations. The candidate should possess analytical capabilities to evaluate complex technology proposals, assess emerging digital trends, and provide strategic financial guidance that enables the Ministry to leverage technology effectively whilst managing costs and risks prudently.

ICT Budget Analysis and Evaluation
Review and analyse ICT budget submissions from various divisions and departments within the Ministry, assessing technical requirements, cost justifications, and alignment with digital strategy. Evaluate the financial viability of proposed ICT projects, including hardware, software, cloud services, and digital infrastructure investments. Review cost-benefit analysis for major ICT initiatives and technology refresh cycles.

Technology Investment Assessment
Assess the strategic value and business case for ICT investments, ensuring alignment with the Ministry's digital roadmap and whole-of-government ICT policies. Review vendor quotations and pricing models used for ICT procurements, including software licensing, cloud subscriptions, and managed services. Evaluate the total cost of ownership for ICT assets and services over their lifecycle.

Establish and maintain cost standards and benchmarks for technology purchases across the Ministry. Research market prices for ICT services, hardware, and software to create reference guides. Regularly update these benchmarks by tracking industry pricing trends, including developing standard cost estimates for common technology purchases. Validate these cost standards by reviewing actual project costs after completion, adjusting the benchmarks as needed to ensure future budget planning reflects realistic market conditions.

Compliance and Risk Management
Ensure ICT budget proposals comply with government procurement regulations, cybersecurity requirements, and data governance policies. Ensure leverage of WOG or Ministry contracts and service agreements for ICT vendors and service providers for ICT procurements. Assess financial risks associated with technology investments, including vendor dependency and obsolescence risks.

Strategic Planning Support
Contribute to the development of the Ministry's ICT budget strategy and multi-year technology investment plans. Provide financial analysis to support ICT governance committees and technology steering groups. Collaborate with ICT teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into budget implications.

Stakeholder Collaboration
Work closely with the product teams, finance teams, and business units to understand technology needs and budget constraints. Liaise with central agencies such as GovTech and Ministry of Finance on ICT budget matters and policy compliance.

Job Qualifications

  • At least 5 years of experience in ICT operations, technology project management, or IT procurement within government or large organisations, with proven success in technology implementation and vendor management.

Your mission is to ensure every AI action is auditable and non-repudiable, protecting multi-agency data sources while maintaining the highest standards of public trust.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Security Architecture & Threat Modeling
  • System Design: Lead the design of security guardrails for AI agents to prevent them from taking unauthorized legal or financial actions.
  • Threat Modeling: Map out potential risks for autonomous AI, such as users trying to "hijack" the agent's intent or tricking it into accessing data it shouldn't.
  • Human-in-the-Loop: Design workflows that ensure high-stakes AI decisions (like grant recommendations) cannot proceed without explicit, authenticated human approval.
  1. Reliable Audit & Explainability
  • Audit Trails: Build a "Chain of Custody" for AI decisions by logging what the agent "thought," what specific data it retrieved, and which model version was used.
  • Reproducibility: Ensure that AI actions are documented well enough to be reconstructed and explained to auditors or stakeholders.
  • Data Governance: Ensure the AI only accesses integrated agency data on a strict "need-to-know" basis.
  1. Testing & Advanced Privacy (Preferred)
  • Security Testing: Conduct proactive testing to find vulnerabilities in how the AI processes instructions or uses external tools.
  • Advanced Privacy: Implement specialized privacy technologies to protect sensitive business information within our unified data hub.

Required Competencies & Experience

Working in close collaboration with the CIO, SCIO, Chief Data Office, Ministry Chief Information Security Officer, Engineering Lead and cross-functional product teams, you will serve as the central architect for MSF’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) journey.

This role is responsible for formulating MSF's overarching AI strategy, identifying high-impact opportunities for AI adoption, and establishing robust governance frameworks. You will ensure that AI technologies—including Generative AI, LLM, machine learning, and predictive analytics—are deployed responsibly, ethically, and securely to drive impactful early childhood education and social service outcomes while remaining fully aligned with Whole-of-Government (WOG) directives and MSF Strategic outcomes.

[Key Responsibilities]

1. AI Strategy, Roadmap & Adoption

  • Evolve and execute MSF AI Strategy: Continuously keep pulse with the changes in this space, calibrate and realign, and execution of the Ministry Family’s AI roadmap, identifying how traditional and upcoming AI models can optimise internal operations and transform citizen-facing services.

  • MSF, WOG & National AI Alignment: Ensure MSF’s AI initiatives are tightly aligned with MSF's Strategic Outcomes, Singapore’s National AI Strategy, the Digital Government Blueprint, and Smart Nation goals.

  • Use Case Prioritisation: Partner with policy and operational divisions to identify, evaluate, and prioritise high-value AI use cases, establishing clear metrics for success and business value.

  • Capability Building: Drive ministry family-wide AI literacy and capability-building programmes, fostering an AI-ready culture and preparing teams for human-AI collaboration.

2. AI Governance, Risk & Ethics

  • Establish AI Governance Frameworks: Develop, implement, and maintain MSF’s AI governance policies, ensuring alignment with WOG guidelines (such as IM8 AI standards) and international best practices for responsible AI.

  • Ethical AI & Bias Mitigation: Define standards for algorithmic fairness, transparency, accountability, and explainability. Establish guardrails to identify and mitigate biases in AI models, particularly those affecting vulnerable segments of society.

  • Compliance & Risk Management: Monitor regulatory shifts and WOG policies regarding AI safety, intellectual property, and data privacy. Conduct risk assessments on proposed AI systems before deployment.

3. Policy-Ops-Tech Integration & Collaboration

  • Cross-Functional Synergy: Act as the central node connecting tech execution teams (Data Engineers, AI Specialists) with policy and operational stakeholders to translate AI potential into scalable solutions.

  • Steering Committee Representation: Provide secretarial and strategic support for digital and AI governance steering committees. Work closely with central agencies (e.g., GovTech, SNDGO) to benchmark and accelerate MSF’s AI capabilities.

  • Play a foundational role in shaping how data, analytics, and predictive intelligence are embedded into everyday decision-making across Case Central.

  • Develop and deploy predictive and statistical models that surface early warning signals and proactive triggers (e.g. risk escalation, intervention needs).

  • Work closely with product managers and the wider team to define hypotheses, design experiments, and deeply understand user needs, pain points, and business goals.

  • Translate complex data into clear, strategic recommendations for product enhancements.

  • Continuously evaluate model performance, bias, and real-world impact on client outcomes.

  • Build and maintain intuitive dashboards for our product team, caseworkers, supervisors, and policymakers, tailored to their decision context.

  • Visualize data effectively to highlight trends, anomalies, and opportunities, enabling data-driven decisions across teams.

  • Define and uphold data schemas, definitions, and quality standards across incoming programmes and partners.

  • Act as a data steward for Case Central, ensuring consistency, lineage, and trustworthiness of data.

  • Help set the long-term data and analytics roadmap for our product team.

[What we are looking for]

Experience & Qualifications

  • A Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field.

  • At least 7+ years of experience in Data Science or Product Analytics roles within dynamic, outcome-driven organizations with a strong portfolio of projects demonstrating data-driven solutions.

  • Domain Knowledge: Strong understanding of AI concepts (e.g., LLMs, NLP, predictive modelling), data infrastructure, and the lifecycle of AI model development (MLOps). Familiarity with public sector data policies and platforms or IM8 is highly preferred.

  • You are proficient in SQL and Python for handling large datasets.

  • You have advanced knowledge in statistical methodologies and machine learning to uncover insights. You can also apply these techniques to large datasets.

  • Familiarity with database, data pipelines, analytics tooling, and model deployment.

  • Ability to build relationships with diverse stakeholders and cultivate strong partnerships.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to bridge technical and non-technical stakeholders and collaborate across various functions to ensure impact.

Key Competencies

  • Strategic & Ethical Thinking: Ability to balance aggressive technological innovation with rigorous ethical reasoning and risk management, keeping the citizen’s well-being at the centre.

  • Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to demystify complex AI concepts for non-technical senior leaders and build consensus across diverse ministry sectors.

  • Agile & Problem-Solving Mindset: Highly adaptable to the rapid pace of AI advancements, with a proven ability to navigate ambiguous regulatory landscapes.

About Ministry of Transport (MOT)

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Civil Aviation and Air Transport
  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is responsible for the Government Procurement (GP) policies, which govern how government agencies conduct their procurement. GeBIZ X is the MOF product that will transform the procurement and business experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers.

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking a Senior Enterprise Software Engineer who combines deep technical craftsmanship with leadership capabilities. You are someone who goes beyond writing high-quality code—you take full ownership of broad, ambiguously-scoped projects, drive architectural standards, and actively uplift the team's engineering capabilities.

In this role, you will balance technical delivery with transitional people management, guiding junior engineers, navigating stakeholder alignments, and ensuring our enterprise configurations are resilient, secure, and highly maintainable.

Our Team

We are a passionate, diverse team committed to driving meaningful public change. We value experimentation, continuous learning, and constructive debate. Here, you will lead technical design direction and collaborate closely with UX designers, finance officers, and solution providers who are equally invested in your growth and the transformation of MOF’s corporate finance services.

What You Will Be Working On

  1. Craft, Configuration & Architecture Delivery
  • Enterprise Development: Lead product development, system integration, and architecture design for large-scale applications used across WOG. Independently implement complex workflows, multi-object data models, and platform extensions.
  • Platform & Lifecycle Mastery: Demonstrate deep mastery of core architecture, extension models, and integration capabilities. Proactively reduce platform debt and resolve multi-module production bottlenecks.
  • Data Migration & Resilience: Safely manage complex data migrations and bulk changes within platform constraints, implementing strict pre-checks, reconciliation protocols, and backout plans.
  • Technical Sustainability: Deliver features balancing configurability, reliability, and performance. Document crucial architectural trade-offs using Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) under the "comply-or-explain" standard.

  • Enforce Engineering Standards: Lead configuration reviews and enforce naming conventions, patterns, and code reuse. Establish mandatory review checklists for high-impact changes (permissions, data models, integration touchpoints).
  • Security & Compliance: Review all configurations for security risks, ensuring strict alignment with government policy and compliance, and agency data classification requirements.
  1. Strategic Alignment & Team Leadership
  • Roadmap Translation: Partner with Product Managers, Engineering Managers, and UX Designers to translate business requirements into technical product roadmaps, actionable engineering tasks, and high-fidelity prototypes.
  • Transitional People Management: Actively mentor junior team members by breaking down complex problems and providing constructive feedback. Conduct regular check-ins with direct or indirect team members to support their day-to-day progress and unblock technical hurdles.
  • Drive Automation, Culture & Process Optimization: Champion an automation-first culture to elevate Developer Experience (DevX) and mitigate delivery risk. Introduce safe integration patterns, automated testing, and robust CI/CD pipelines to eliminate manual friction and enhance deployment safety. Continuously optimize engineering processes and team rituals, constructively challenging the status quo while facilitating cross-functional alignment when disagreements arise

Required Qualifications, Skills & Mindset

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Computer Science, Computer/Electronics Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.

  • Technical Stack Proficiency: Practical experience with modern front-end and back-end web technologies, such as Next.js, React.js, JavaScript, Node.js, and CSS. Experience with ETL / AWS for complex data migrations. Familiarity with developing alongside SaaS, Bespoke, and COTS (Commercial Off-The-Shelf) solutions. Procurement and/or ERP SaaS experience strongly preferred. (e.g. Ivalua)
  • Automation Expertise: Strong understanding of and proven track record in driving automation across the development lifecycle (e.g., test automation, deployment automation, infrastructure-as-code, or automated business/platform workflows) to maximize engineering efficiency and ensure system safety.
  • Government Tech Ecosystem: Direct experience with Government Commercial Cloud (GCC), SHIP-HATS, and the SG Tech Stack (SGTS) is highly advantageous.
  • Governance & Security: Solid understanding of public sector data protection regulations, privacy considerations, and compliance.
  • Leadership Mindset: Strong communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technology concepts to non-technical stakeholders. A desire to step into technical mentoring and transitional leadership while remaining a hands-on practitioner.
  • Public Good Focus: A genuine passion for utilizing technology to maximize public impact and improve the lives of public officers and citizens alike.

Please note that this will be a 2-year fixed term contract.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will take ownership of complex, cross-cutting technical work while actively raising the bar for those around you. You will be expected to operate with a high degree of independence — making sound architectural decisions, leading incident response, and delivering features that span multiple services or systems — while also investing meaningfully in the growth of junior software engineers and the health of the team.

This is a role for someone who is equally comfortable writing a technical design document, reviewing a colleague's code for AI-introduced antipatterns, and facilitating alignment between engineers and stakeholders on a tricky design trade-off.

Craft & Technical Execution

  • You will design and deliver moderately complex features that span multiple components or services, with genuine attention to modularity, scalability, and resiliency. This means evaluating solution options, sharing well-reasoned recommendations, and proactively addressing technical debt before it compounds.
  • On quality and DevOps, you will contribute to reusable test automation frameworks and help the team adopt better observability, CI/CD, and automation practices. You will ensure that features you own are properly monitored and that issues surface early rather than in production.
  • You will build deep knowledge of your team's product architecture, dependencies, and data flows, and use that knowledge to make independent technical decisions and author design documents with minimal guidance. You will also conduct architecture reviews for junior engineers' work, offering constructive and actionable feedback.
  • When incidents occur, you will lead triage and debugging within your domain, contribute root cause analyses, and drive concrete preventive actions through post-incident reviews.
  • Security, compliance, and performance are design constraints in your work, not afterthoughts. You will apply the organisation's recommended platforms and tools effectively, and escalate deviations appropriately.
  • You will also play a key role in how the team works with AI-assisted development — writing clear, unambiguous technical specifications that serve as effective context for both AI tools and junior engineers, identifying when AI-generated code introduces technical debt or security risks, and establishing team-level norms for reviewing AI-generated output before it merges.

Ownership & Delivery

  • You will take full end-to-end ownership of broad project scopes, navigating uncertainty and ensuring successful outcomes.
  • You are comfortable taking calculated risks and learning openly from both successes and failures.
  • You actively mentor junior team members — sharing knowledge, breaking down problems, and providing constructive feedback that raises overall team productivity.

Strategic Contribution

  • You will translate team goals into actionable plans, breaking down and prioritising work and contributing to project strategy.
  • You proactively identify opportunities, drive workstreams, and synthesise data into clear recommendations that connect to organisational impact.
  • At the project level, you anticipate risks and put mitigations in place before they become blockers.

Culture & Organisational Influence

  • You will coordinate cross-functional collaboration and help ensure projects are delivered effectively across team boundaries.
  • You navigate disagreements constructively, facilitating alignment among team members and stakeholders.
  • You challenge existing processes where improvement is warranted and drive change initiatives at the team or division level. You share learnings openly — both wins and failures — and make recommendations that help the team continuously improve.

People Management

  • This role includes a developmental people management component. With close guidance from your software engineering manager, you will support team coordination by communicating project goals and priorities clearly, and helping team members understand how their individual work connects to broader objectives.

Role Overview

MOE is strengthening its product-led approach to deliver impactful digital products and services across schools, educators, HQ officers, and parents.

As MOE expands its portfolio of digital products, the challenge is not only to build useful solutions, but to ensure that products are introduced thoughtfully, understood clearly, adopted effectively, and translated into sustained improvements in day-to-day workflows and service delivery.

As an Assistant Director / Senior Manager, Product Marketing, you will lead go-to-market, adoption, and value realisation efforts for one or more product domains, working with product, operations, policy, communications, and business teams to ensure that:

  • products are positioned clearly around user needs, policy intent, and operational outcomes,
  • go-to-market and rollout approaches are tailored for different user groups such as educators, HQ officers, and parents, and
  • product value is realised through sustained usage, reduced friction, and improved user experience at scale.

You will work at the intersection of product strategy, user needs, and operational delivery, translating product intent into clear narratives, coherent rollout approaches, and measurable adoption outcomes. The role requires strategic judgment, strong stakeholder management, and the ability to move from ambiguity to practical execution in a complex public-sector environment.

[What you will be working on]

You will lead go-to-market and adoption for one or more product domains (e.g. educator products, parent-facing products, or corporate systems), with responsibility for product positioning, rollout readiness, stakeholder alignment, user engagement approaches, and adoption performance. Depending on the product domain, your work may focus on educators, HQ officers, parents, or other MOE user groups.   • Advise product managers and stakeholders on adoption implications for product design, onboarding, sequencing, support, and roadmap decisions

2. Shape Product Positioning, Narratives and Rollout Messaging

  • Shape clear and consistent product narratives anchored on user value, policy intent, and organisational outcomes
  • Tailor positioning and messaging for different user groups (e.g. school leaders, teachers, HQ users, parents) while maintaining coherence across products
  • Translate complex product capabilities into simple, practical, and decision-useful content for users and stakeholders
  • Ensure alignment between product messaging, policy intent, rollout plans, and communications materials

3. Plan and Execute Product Launches

  • Lead end-to-end go-to-market and launch planning for product releases, ensuring clarity on objectives, target users, timing, and readiness
  • Orchestrate readiness across product, operations, training, support, and communications teams
  • Oversee the development of launch artefacts (e.g. user guides, briefing decks, demos, FAQs) to support adoption at scale
  • Drive engagement and rollout approaches that improve user readiness, confidence, and uptake

4. Drive Coordinated Engagement and Change Support

  • Design and refine scalable engagement and change support approaches for product rollouts across diverse MOE user groups
  • Partner with communications, operations, schools, and business teams to deliver coordinated outreach, onboarding, and adoption interventions
  • Support organisation-wide campaigns, showcases, and leadership engagements where product understanding, confidence, and momentum are important

5. Translate User Insights into Actionable Improvements

  • Synthesise user feedback from engagement sessions, analytics, support channels, and operational partners to identify meaningful adoption patterns
  • Translate user and organisational insights into actionable recommendations on onboarding, messaging, launch sequencing, or feature usability
  • Influence product and stakeholder decisions by bringing a clear view of user needs, friction points, and value realisation opportunities

6. Track and Improve Adoption Metrics

  • Define and track key adoption and value indicators (e.g. activation, repeat usage, workflow uptake) for assigned products
  • Assess product performance across user segments, identify where adoption is lagging, and recommend course corrections
  • Provide clear updates and insights to product teams and stakeholders, with a focus on decisions, actions, and outcomes

Working Model

  • Operate in a matrixed, cross-functional environment across product, operations, policy, communications, and business teams
  • Work closely with product managers and delivery teams to shape rollout strategies, readiness plans, and adoption interventions
  • Partner with policy, communications, support, and operational stakeholders to ensure alignment between product intent, user needs, and implementation realities
  • Depending on scope, may lead workstreams, coordinate across multiple teams, and help build shared practices for go-to-market and adoption across the division

Qualifications and Experience

  • Background in product management, product marketing, communications, change management, digital transformation, or a related field

  • Experience operating in complex environments where user needs, policy intent, service delivery, and implementation realities must be balanced

  • Experience working across cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders in a structured environment
  • Ability to use data, user insights, and operational context to guide decisions and interventions
  • Experience in the education sector, public sector, or other large service environments is an advantage

  • Clear communication and narrative framing – simplifies complexity and frames messages for educators, HQ officers, parents, and stakeholders

  • Execution and delivery discipline – converts strategy into practical rollout plans, interventions, and results

You will work closely with product managers, operations teams, policy officers, and engineering to translate complex regulatory requirements into usable, scalable digital experiences. This role requires balancing compliance constraints with user-centered design, operational efficiency, and long-term system coherence.

Your portfolio will include:

  • Licence management systems for work pass compliance
  • Migrant worker address management workflows
  • Enforcement operations and case management tool

Lead end-to-end design delivery across systems

  • Own product-level design from discovery through post-launch optimization, ensuring that enforcement systems are usable, coherent, and operationally effective while meeting policy and compliance requirements.

  • Conduct discovery using appropriate methods - user interviews, stakeholder workshops, operational shadowing, journey mapping, and data analysis to deeply understand enforcement workflows, pain points, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Map service ecosystems and end-to-end journeys across multiple systems and touchpoints, identifying systemic gaps, friction points, and opportunities to improve both user experience and operational efficiency.

  • Bridge business, operations, policy, and technology by facilitating alignment across cross-functional teams. Translate complex regulatory, operational, and technical constraints into clear design direction and actionable solutions.

  • Drive design direction by analyzing research findings, synthesizing insights, and defining design principles that guide product decisions while balancing user needs with regulatory and operational realities.

  • Rapidly prototype and iterate using modern tools and AI-assisted workflows (e.g., Figma, Claude for design assistance, AI prototyping tools) to accelerate concept validation, stakeholder feedback, and learning cycles.

  • Establish and maintain design standards for enforcement products, ensuring consistency, accessibility, and quality across all touchpoints while contributing to GovTech's broader design system.

  • Define and track success metrics for design solutions, measuring impact on user outcomes, operational efficiency, and policy objectives. Use data to drive continuous improvement.

Shape systems-level thinking and design excellence

  • Maintain strategic perspective at the programme level, ensuring individual product decisions align with broader enforcement division goals and contribute to MOM's service transformation vision.

  • Connect design work across multiple products and touchpoints, identifying opportunities for shared patterns, reusable components, and common capabilities that reduce duplication and increase efficiency.

  • Strengthen design quality through critique, review, and knowledge sharing, raising the overall standard of work and fostering a culture of design excellence across the enforcement portfolio.

Lead through collaboration and influence

  • Partner with cross-functional teams (product, engineering, operations, policy) to ensure design is deeply integrated into product strategy, planning, and delivery — not an afterthought.

  • Communicate design decisions, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to stakeholders at all levels, ensuring alignment between user needs, operational constraints, and regulatory objectives.

  • Influence without authority by building trust, demonstrating value, and articulating how design contributes to measurable outcomes - not just better-looking interfaces.

  • Mentor junior designers and share knowledge across the organization, strengthening design capability and fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.

Contribute to GovTech's design community

  • Drive efficiency and innovation by piloting new tools, methods, and AI-assisted workflows in your work, demonstrating how design can operate faster and smarter without sacrificing quality.

  • Actively participate in design community initiatives - sharing learnings, contributing to design standards, and supporting efforts that benefit all GovTech designers.

  • Support hiring and team-building efforts where relevant, helping build a strong, diverse, inclusive design practice.

What success looks like

Enforcement systems feel coherent and connected across critical journeys from licensing to address management to enforcement operations with measurable improvements in usability and operational efficiency.

Cross-functional teams trust design to frame problems, guide decisions, and deliver solutions that meet both user needs and regulatory requirements.

Design work accelerates through effective use of modern tools and AI-assisted workflows, enabling faster iteration, higher output, and greater strategic focus.

Enforcement division stakeholders recognize design as a strategic capability that contributes to measurable outcomes not just a service function

Experience and domain understanding:

  • 10+ years of experience in UX/UI design, product design, service design, or related fields
  • Proven experience leading design across complex, multi-stakeholder products or services
  • Experience in regulated, compliance-driven, or high-stakes environments (government, healthcare, financial services, legal/regulatory systems) strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated experience working on at least 2–3 different products, showing breadth and adaptability

You'll thrive here if you

  • Enjoy tackling complexity and ambiguity - breaking down messy regulatory and operational problems into clear, actionable design solutions.
  • See design as a means to measurable impact - cost reduction, productivity improvement, better policy outcomes not just better experiences.
  • Embrace efficiency and innovation - actively seeking ways to work smarter through modern tools, AI assistance, and streamlined methods.
  • Influence through clarity and credibility - earning trust by demonstrating value, not asserting authority.
  • Care about public service - motivated by the opportunity to improve critical government systems that affect thousands of employers, workers, and officers.

Product Strategy & Ownership

Delivery Accountability

Product Delivery & Execution

  • Work with cross-functional teams (engineering, design, data/QA, operations) to deliver iterative releases while maintaining service continuity for critical operations.

Process Transformation & Operational Efficiency

  • Experience managing delivery in partnership with engineering teams (planning, prioritisation, risk management, release management).
  • Exposure to budget and procurement processes (forecasting, utilisation tracking, licensing/professional services procurement, renewals) is an advantage.
  • Working knowledge of security, data protection and audit/compliance needs in enterprise environments is an advantage.
  • Outcome-oriented product thinking: frames problems clearly, defines success metrics, and prioritises work that delivers measurable impact.
  • Strong execution and delivery discipline: plans work, manages risks and dependencies, and drives issues to resolution.
  • Stakeholder management and communication: aligns teams, writes clearly, and can present options and trade-offs.
  • User-centric approach: uses research, feedback and data to improve usability and adoption.

About MOT

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Civil Aviation and Air Transport
  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).
