We are Digital Society Products (DSP). We build tech for public good. Anchored in the Ministry of Culture, Community & Youth (MCCY) serving a Whole-of-Government mandate, we create solutions that solve real citizen problems and modernise public services.

We turn policy goals into working software. With a strong heritage in GovTech, our team has a long history of shipping national-scale digital products.

Our portfolio includes:

  • CulturePass: Democratising access to arts and culture for all Singaporeans.
  • CrowdTaskSG: A crowdsourcing platform that empowers citizens to contribute to national policy and projects.
  • Wireless Alert Alarm System: A critical safety net deployed in seniors' homes to provide immediate aid.

Who We Are Looking For

We believe the most critical phase of product development happens before a single line of code is written.

We are looking for a Discovery Product Manager to lead this upstream work for high-impact government projects. You will partner with policy teams to navigate ambiguity, de-risk investments and define the "What" and "Why" of the next generation of public services.

This is a strategic role that requires strong collaboration, a deep understanding of user and stakeholder needs and the ability to navigate public sector constraints while pushing for innovation and modernisation.

Your goal is to ensure we solve the right problems in the right way. By leading multi-disciplinary teams through problem framing, opportunity mapping and service envisioning, you will translate user needs into co-created concepts that are aligned, actionable and future-ready.

Note: This role focuses purely on achieving clarity. Once a direction is validated and actionable, you will hand it over to implementation teams for delivery.

What you will be working on:

  • This is a strategic "0-to-0.5" role. You will lead a squad with Design, Engineering to validate hypotheses and define the future state of government services.
  • Orchestrate the Vision: Lead inception workshops and envisioning sessions with policy owners and C-suite stakeholders to crystallise vague problem statements into clear product opportunities.
  • De-Risk the Future: Conduct rigorous fit-gap analysis, market sizing and feasibility assessments. You will influence if a problem requires a digital solution, a policy change or a process redesign.
  • Shape the User Experience: Apply design thinking to translate user research into actionable service concepts, opportunity maps and prototypes. You will partner with Design and Engineering to co-create services that are visionary, viable and inclusive.
  • Bridge Policy & Tech: Act as the translator between high-level government policy goals and on-the-ground technical constraints, ensuring solutions are both visionary and viable.
  • Modernise Legacy: Tackle complex legacy systems by proposing future-ready, interoperable architectures that pave the way for digital transformation.
  • Stakeholder Management: Engage and align C-suite and senior government stakeholders on the product vision, strategy and delivery roadmap.
  • Deliver Clarity: Your final "product" in this role is clarity. You will synthesize insights into a validated product direction and roadmap, facilitating a seamless handover to delivery teams.

We are looking for:

  • A strategic thinker who thrives in ambiguity and can tell a compelling story.
  • Experience: 5+ years of product management experience, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact initiatives.
  • Discovery Expertise: Strong experience in shaping early product direction, MVP scoping or working on pre-delivery discovery (0-to-1 work).
  • Strategic Translation: Ability to translate user needs, policy requirements, and technical constraints into viable product strategies.
  • Design Thinking: Solid understanding of design thinking principles and how to apply user research insights to product and service design.
  • Stakeholder Management: Excellent communication skills with the ability to navigate bureaucracy and align senior leadership/C-suite.
  • Collaboration: Able to facilitate cross-agency collaboration and navigate ambiguity to drive alignment.
  • Technical Fluency: Familiarity with technology and system design principles and agile ways of working.

Bonus Points For

  • Familiarity with government processes, digital service standards, procurement frameworks or data governance.
  • Experience in public sector digital transformation or modernising large-scale legacy systems.

Why Join Us?

  • Shape the National Agenda: Work upstream where the biggest decisions are made. The directions you define will become the roadmap for national services used by millions.
  • Pure Product Thinking: Focus on the "Why" and "What" without getting bogged down in the daily grind of delivery and ticket management.
  • A World-Class Team: Join a discovery squad with Design, Engineering and Policy working as one team.
  • Tangible Impact: Continue the legacy of products like CulturePass and CrowdTaskSG, influencing how government services are imagined, not just implemented.

About the product

Singapore Customs is a regulatory agency under the Ministry of Finance, with the mission of protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy.

Customs eServices serves as Customs' Single Digital Touchpoint for 6,500 Singapore based Companies, offering trade facilitation services including Hand-Carried Export Scheme, Permit Clearance Enquiry Service, Permit Returns, and eGuarantee@Gov. eGuarantee@Gov which started as service meant for Customs, had scaled to support more than 220 school, agencies and financial institutions. jobTitle: Senior Software Engineer, AI Infrastructure & Operations (AI Practice)
jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

Within the AI Practice, the AI Infrastructure & Operations (AI Infra & Ops) team defines the reference architecture and best practices for running AI at scale. Rather than owning a single product, we work across multiple agencies and use cases — helping teams stand up production-grade AI infrastructure, establishing governance standards, and building reusable platform components that accelerate adoption government-wide.

As a Senior AI Infra & Ops Engineer, you will be a technical leader and trusted advisor — shaping architectural standards, uplifting engineering capability across agencies, and ensuring that AI workloads across government are production-ready, cost-efficient, and secure. You will operate at the intersection of deep technical expertise and stakeholder engagement, working with a diverse set of agency teams at varying levels of AI maturity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

[What you will be working on]

You will work across multiple agencies and projects simultaneously, combining hands-on engineering with advisory and enablement work. You will be responsible for:

You will bridge the gap between experimental data science and production-grade engineering, working across multiple agencies and use cases rather than a single product. You will be responsible for:

  • MLOps & Lifecycle Management: Design, build, and maintain automated CI/CD pipelines for ML models. Establish whole-of-government standards for model versioning, automated testing, canary deployments, and rollback strategies. Build reusable pipeline components and templates that agencies can adopt to move toward self-service model delivery.

  • Model Optimization & Quantization: Apply and benchmark advanced techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, distillation, speculative decoding) to optimize LLMs and other deep learning models for inference. Evaluate inference engines (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server) and publish recommendations balancing performance, cost, and resilience. Provide hands-on support to agency teams applying these to their workloads.

  • Infrastructure & Platform Architecture: Architect scalable, multi-tenant AI infrastructure (on-prem and cloud) to support training and inference workloads, with a focus on GPU orchestration (e.g., Kubernetes, Volcano, Run:ai, NVIDIA GPU Operator). Define reference architectures, capacity planning guidance, and FinOps practices that agencies can adopt.

  • Observability & Monitoring: Design and champion observability standards for AI systems — covering model health, data/concept drift, system latency, GPU telemetry, and cost attribution. Define SLO/SLI frameworks to ensure AI services are transparent, debuggable, and maintainable at scale.

  • Security & Governance: Collaborate with Responsible AI and cybersecurity stakeholders to embed security guardrails and compliance checks into standardized deployment pipelines, ensuring AI systems meet government security standards (e.g., IM8, CSA guidelines). Drive governance frameworks covering model lineage, reproducibility, and approval workflows.

  • Technical Consulting & Enablement: Act as a senior subject matter expert for government agencies, conducting architecture reviews, maturity assessments, and providing actionable roadmaps to scale AI from POC to production. Develop reusable playbooks, reference implementations, and training materials. Mentor engineers within the AI Practice and across partner agencies — the goal is to build self-sufficient teams.

[What we are looking for]

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Postgraduate study or research in distributed systems, ML systems, or high-performance computing is a plus.

  • Experience: At least 6–8 years of progressive experience in DevOps, MLOps, Cloud Infrastructure, or Platform Engineering, with a significant portion focused on AI/ML workloads in production environments. Experience in a consultancy, platform team, or CoE setting — where you've had to advise and enable multiple teams rather than just build for one — is highly valued.

  • Core Technical Skills:

    • Strong proficiency in Python and shell scripting; working knowledge of at least one systems language (Go, Rust, etc.) is a plus.

    • Deep, hands-on expertise with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) in production settings, including experience operating multi-tenant clusters.

    • Proven experience designing MLOps platforms and patterns using frameworks such as Kubeflow, MLflow, BentoML, or equivalent tooling.

    • Advanced Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) skills with Terraform or Ansible — including module design, state management, and CI/CD integration for infrastructure.

    • Experience with GitOps workflows (ArgoCD) and platform engineering patterns (internal developer platforms, self-service portals, golden paths).

  • Domain Expertise:

    • Strong understanding of GPU hardware and performance tuning for distributed training and inference.

    • Hands-on experience with LLM serving stacks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, KServe) and model optimization techniques (quantization, distillation, pruning).

    • Expertise in observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK/Loki) and ML-specific monitoring tools (Arize, Langfuse, etc.).

    • Solid understanding of networking fundamentals and service mesh architectures.

  • Consulting & Leadership Skills:

    • Demonstrated ability to engage with multiple stakeholder teams at varying levels of technical maturity and tailor advice accordingly. You can be equally effective whiteboarding with senior engineers and presenting infrastructure roadmaps to agency leadership.

    • Experience conducting architecture reviews, writing technical guidance documents, and developing reusable standards that others adopt.

    • Track record of mentoring engineers and building capability in others — the measure of success is teams that become self-sufficient, not teams that stay dependent on you.

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You can produce clear, concise technical documentation and present confidently to both technical and non-technical audiences.

    • A proactive, systems-thinking mindset — you anticipate failure modes across diverse environments and can triage the highest-impact recommendations when agency teams have limited bandwidth.

    • Passion for building public good through scalable, well-governed technology.

  • Preferred / Bonus:

    • Experience managing large-scale GPU clusters or cloud AI services in production.

    • Prior experience in a consulting, professional services, or internal platform/CoE role serving multiple product teams.

    • Contributions to open-source projects in the MLOps, Kubernetes, or AI infrastructure space.

    • Certifications in Cloud Architecture or Kubernetes .

    • Experience with cost optimization at scale — FinOps practices, spot/preemptible instance strategies, and resource right-sizing for GPU workloads.

    • Familiarity with emerging paradigms: multi-modal model serving, agentic AI infrastructure, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and edge inference.

CCYC (Culture, Community and Youth Cluster) is a part of GovTech's Government Digital Transformation team where we support the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — such as the National Arts Council (NAC), People’s Association (PA), Sport Singapore (SportSG), and MUIS—by delivering digital solutions that promote social cohesion, cultural vibrancy, and youth engagement.

Our growing suite of products include the following:

  • Community Engagement Platforms

Digital products that enable citizens to participate in grassroots and national events, including Volunteer Management, Community Event Registration, Feedback and Ideation products for civic engagement.

  • Cultural Participation and Arts Enablement

Event Discovery and Ticketing, Grant Application for Arts Funding, Digital Storytelling and Archival products.

  • Youth Development and Empowerment

Platforms for Youth Leadership and Volunteering Opportunities, Gamified Learning Tools for civic education, Co-creation Platforms for Youth Policy Input etc.

  • Sports and Active Lifestyle

Facility booking, Fitness tracking and Rewards, Data Platforms for Sports Policy and Performance Tracking

[What you will be working on]

You will own the design of CCYC’s community products across the full product lifecycle — from discovery through launch, optimisation and growth.

Own the Full Design Arc

Lead design from 0 to 1 to 100. This means shaping the initial product concept, designing and shipping the first version, and then continuously improving the experience based on data, feedback and evolving user needs. You do not hand off and move on — you stay accountable to the outcome.

Drive Product Thinking Through Design

Bring a product mindset to every design decision. You think about retention, activation, and adoption — not just usability. You use design as a lever for growth: improving onboarding flows, reducing friction in high-drop-off moments, and creating experiences that bring users back.

Conduct Lightweight, Continuous Research

Run user interviews, usability tests and contextual checks as a regular part of your workflow. Design Across the Full Stack of UX

From user flows and information architecture to interaction design, visual design and motion — you handle it all. You produce work to a high standard of craft and detail, with particular attention to microinteractions, accessibility and the nuances that separate a polished product from a functional one.

Maintain and Evolve the Design System

Take ownership of the CCYC product design system. Keep components consistent, well-documented and scalable as the product grows. You balance system rigour with the pragmatism needed to move fast in a live product environment.

Manage Stakeholders and Communicate Design Decisions

Work directly with MCCY stakeholders — community managers, grassroots leaders, operations teams — as well as internal product and engineering partners. You present your work clearly, advocate for the user, and navigate competing priorities without losing design integrity.

Contribute to Design Culture

As a senior IC, you set the quality bar. You give constructive feedback, contribute to shared design practices within DSP, and help elevate the standard of product design across the team.

  • Autonomy: Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity — you can manage your own workload, set priorities and deliver independently without close supervision.

We turn policy goals into working software. With a strong heritage in GovTech, our team has a long history of shipping national-scale digital products.

  • CrowdTaskSG: A crowdsourcing platform that empowers citizens to contribute to national policy and projects.

[What you will be working on]

You will be the design voice in a discovery squad, leading the human-centred work that shapes what gets built — and why.

Lead Design Research

Plan and execute mixed-method research (interviews, contextual inquiry, diary studies, surveys) to surface user needs, pain points and mental models. You synthesise findings into clear insights that the whole team — including non-designers — can act on.

Map Services End-to-End

Go beyond screens. Use service design tools — service blueprints, journey maps, ecosystem maps, stakeholder maps — to understand and articulate the full service experience across channels, touchpoints and backstage operations.

Frame Problems, Define Opportunities

Collaborate with Product Managers and policy teams to translate ambiguous briefs into clear problem statements and opportunity spaces. You bring the user's voice into strategy conversations and help teams avoid solving the wrong problem.

Co-Create and Prototype

Run ideation workshops and co-design sessions with stakeholders and users. Rapidly prototype concepts — from rough sketches to high-fidelity interactive mockups — to test assumptions early and validate direction before any code is written.

Produce High-Quality Design Artefacts

When the direction is clear, produce polished UI designs, interaction flows and design specifications that are ready for handover. Your production work sets the quality bar for what delivery teams will build.

Influence and Communicate

Present your work compellingly to senior government stakeholders and C-suite audiences. You translate complex user insights and service concepts into narratives that earn alignment and build confidence in the proposed direction.

Deliver Clarity Through Design

Your final output in discovery is a validated, well-articulated design direction — service concepts, UX principles, interaction patterns and a clear design vision — ready for seamless handover to a delivery team.

[What we are looking for]

We are looking for a Senior UX Designer with a generalist's range: someone equally at home facilitating a research session, mapping a complex service ecosystem, and crafting a pixel-perfect prototype. You are not a specialist researcher, and you are not a visual designer alone — you are someone who can do it all, and knows when to use each tool.

In this role, you will be embedded in discovery squads alongside Product Managers, Engineers and Policy teams. You will lead the design-side of the "0-to-0.5" phase — helping us ask better questions, see the full picture and define service concepts that are human-centred, viable and future-ready.

Note: This role is upstream of delivery. Once a direction is validated and handed over to implementation teams, you will move on to the next discovery challenge.

  • Experience: 5+ years of UX design experience, with a portfolio that demonstrates work across research, service design and UI.
  • Design Research: Proven ability to lead design research — planning studies, conducting fieldwork, synthesising insights and communicating findings to diverse audiences.
  • Service Design: Hands-on experience with service design tools: service blueprints, journey maps, ecosystem mapping and stakeholder alignment workshops.
  • Production Craft: Strong visual design and prototyping skills — you can go from whiteboard sketch to high-fidelity, interactive prototype with confidence.

GovTech’s Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC) partners with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — including the National Arts Council, People’s Association, Sport Singapore, and MUIS — to deliver digital products that strengthen community life across Singapore. Singaporeans across community engagement, cultural participation, youth development, and sports and active lifestyle.

This role sits within CCYC and will be working on MUIS products, specifically Muslim.SG.

MUIS (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura) is the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, the statutory body that looks after the interests of Singapore’s Muslim community. Muslim.SG is its Muslim lifestyle platform — available as a website and on iOS and Android — that aims to inspire and empower Singaporeans through Islamic religious content.

Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for a Senior UX Designer to own the end-to-end design of Muslim.SG — across the web portal and both mobile platforms — from discovery through to launch and continuous improvement.

This is a full product design role. You will conduct research, shape product direction, design the interface, and stay close to whether your work is actually landing with users. You will be the design voice your squad relies on, and the person accountable for the experience quality
of a platform that serves Singapore’s Muslim community every day.

You bring strong craft, clear product thinking, and the ability to navigate the particular design considerations of Muslim.SG — a platform where content is religiously and culturally significant, users span a wide range of digital literacy, and the relationship between the product and its community requires care and sensitivity.

[What you will be working on]

Own the Full Design Arc
Lead design from 0 to 1 to 100 across the Muslim.SG web and mobile products. This means shaping initial concepts, designing and shipping the first version of features, and continuously improving the experience based on data, user feedback, and evolving community needs. You stay accountable to the outcome — you do not hand off and move on.

Design Across Web and Mobile
Muslim.SG lives across three surfaces: a web portal and native apps on iOS and Android. You will maintain design coherence and quality across all three, understanding where the experiences should diverge — in navigation patterns, interaction models, and platform conventions — and where they must converge, in content hierarchy, information presentation, and community tone.

Conduct Continuous, Embedded Research
Run user interviews, usability tests, and contextual checks as a regular part of your workflow— not as a separate phase. Muslim.SG’s user base is genuinely diverse: different levels of digital confidence, different levels of religious literacy, different languages. You stay close to that reality and let it shape your design decisions rather than designing from assumptions.

Bring a product mindset to every design decision. Think about retention, activation, and adoption alongside usability. Use design as a lever for impact: improving onboarding, reducing friction in high-drop-off moments, and creating experiences that make the platform feel valuable enough to return to — especially for users who are developing their own digital habits.

Maintain and Evolve the Design System
Take ownership of the Muslim.SG design system across web and mobile. Keep components consistent, well-documented, and scalable as the platform grows. You balance system rigour with the pragmatism needed to move at product pace.

Manage Stakeholders and Communicate Design Decisions
Work directly with MUIS stakeholders — community officers, religious officers, operations teams — as well as internal product and engineering partners. Present your work clearly. Advocate for the user. Navigate competing priorities without losing design integrity. When you disagree, you say so with evidence, not volume.

As a senior IC, you help set the quality bar. You give constructive feedback, share what you know, and contribute to shared design practices within CCYC. The standard of work you produce, and how you work, shapes what the team collectively considers good.

[About Data Programme]

The mission of GovTech's Data Program is to deliver fit-for-purpose data assets and services for policy making, service delivery and operations across WOG.

We are seeking a Software Engineer to join our Data Program. The existing Government Data Architecture (GDA), launched in 2019, laid the groundwork for WOG data sharing via TCs, SSOTs and central platforms. As the data technology landscape is rapidly evolving and data/system requirements are becoming increasingly complex and interconnected, to better support agencies, the next phase of GDA (i.e. GDA 2.0) aims to consolidate, streamline, and elevate the products and initiatives within the WOG data landscape – this includes the development of the following products.

  • DataHive as the next-gen WOG Data Discovery & Request Platform to cater to a wider range of WOG requirements and use cases. DataHive has been further enhanced to support both data requestors and providers as follows.
    • Data requestors/consumers will experience a streamlined data search and request process, with options to access data via curated APIs and through an analytics workbench.
    • Data providers can expect more flexibility and control in the management of datasets on the platform itself.
  • Data products that compute and serve derived data for ops and service delivery for multiple agencies. By adopting the “Build Once, Use Many Times” approach for such data products, the intent is to achieve the benefit of cost-savings, better data quality and improving time-to-market for new services.

[What you will be working on]

As a software engineer, you will:

  • Build end-to-end data analytics products/platforms with your team

  • Design system architectures

  • Write production quality code

  • Manage deployments to cloud and (occasionally) on-premise infrastructure

  • Build prototypes to demonstrate technology opportunities

  • Learn and share knowledge in a multi-disciplinary team

  • Establish best practices

  • Share your expertise and mentor other engineers

  • Help with recruiting.

You are not just here to write code, but also to figure out what we should be building and how we should build it.

Your job will be to bring expertise and capability to the public sector. Sometimes this means coding new systems from scratch. Other times this means using the best solutions the community has to offer. We use cloud services, open source software, and commodity hardware as far as possible. Knowing what to build and what to reuse lets us avoid wasting time on solved problems and focus on delivering actual value.

[What it is like working here]

We build products that serve a variety of agency users, who use them to solve highly meaningful problems pertinent to our society, from transportation, to education, to healthcare. The public sector is full of opportunities where even the simplest software can have a big impact on people’s lives. We are here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government.

  • Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.

  • Reliable Productization - To scale an idea, a prototype or a Minimum Viable Product to a software product, we scrutinize and commit to its usability, reliability, scalability and maintainability.

  • Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having ideas on how things should be done and taking responsibility for seeing them through. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.

  • Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

[What we are looking for]

  • Have a demonstrated ability to build software - Prior work and personal projects count for much more than specific degrees.
  • Write code to solve abstract programming problems - Clear thinking, the ability to debug, and understanding the limits of an approach matter much more than getting the “correct” answer.
  • Talk and reason about code with other engineers - We work as a team, so you need to be able to not just solve problems, but have other people understand your solutions.
  • Take initiative to make things happen - Our job is to push for change in government, so we need to challenge the status quo and not wait for instruction.
  • Want to work for the public good - We are public servants; we serve the public. This sometimes means ignoring political pressures and misguided policies. We need people who will push back if something is not in public interest.

Overall, we look for people who have ability, initiative, good communication, and strong values.

Craft & Execution

You will deliver features and proofs of concept that span multiple components or modules, typically working across two to three areas within your team. While you will receive mentorship on architectural decisions and cross-component integration, you are expected to make thoughtful trade-offs between performance, security, and maintainability based on your understanding of the context. You will also take a deliberate approach to balancing short-term delivery speed with long-term code health, flagging when quick fixes introduce future risk, and applying organisational platform and compliance standards effectively.

After your work ships, you are expected to follow through on its impact — checking metrics, reviewing error rates, and addressing post-deployment issues proactively. You will actively participate in incident triage and resolution with team support, and escalate complex issues when needed.

You will also bring rigour to the use of AI-generated code, reviewing it for correctness, edge cases, security issues, and maintainability to the same standard as any human-authored contribution. Ownership

You will independently own your assigned tasks and projects, identifying and addressing issues proactively with minimal guidance. You will know when to seek help and from whom, and you will look for opportunities to recommend improvements to processes or outcomes within your own work.

jobDescription:
The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. To prepare the Public Service for these changes, we have begun the journey towards Public Sector Transformation (PST).

As part of the current phase of PST, ServiceSG aims to be on par with globally leading companies in our delivery of public services. A key transformation in the delivery of citizen services is to take a citizen-centric service journey approach to organising services in an integrated manner via a) a digital concierge via the LifeSG app, b) a physical concierge via an expanded network of Service Centres; and c) a national contact centre. Our aim is to transform the current citizen experience of having to navigate across different public agencies to an experience of the Public Service “knowing, understanding and interacting with me as One”.

There are currently hundreds of hotlines across the Whole of Government (WOG). The Contact Centre team in ServiceSG aims to work with agencies who own these hotlines to streamline and integrate these contact centres, especially those that provide related services. The goal is to establish a central ServiceSG contact centre that can address the queries of citizens across related citizen services, serving as a “outsourced shared service” for selected agencies. The team will also support surges in contact centre call loads for key agencies during peak periods, and act as the central call centre in a national pandemic or crisis.

[Specific Areas of Responsibilities]

• Ensure the contact centre meets performance KPIs for all stakeholder agencies’ service channels

• Ensure that vendor operates the contact centre according to PSD and stakeholder agencies’ requirements

• Set up processes and systems to enable contact centre to deliver omnichannel service with PSD’s service channels

• Plan and supervise the onboarding of stakeholder agencies’ contact centres, and new service channels

• Plan cross referral of government services to callers; develop cross-referral scripts, call handling and escalation process; rotate services to be cross referred for each hotline; and ensure that cross referral and service KPIs are met

• Supervise the development and maintenance of a central knowledge base that contains the information on query handling approaches to support the contact centre and service centres

• Drive the integration of technology in ServiceSG Contact Centre, such as voice chatbots among agency stakeholders

• Plan regular activities and updates to establish strong partnership agency stakeholders

• Manage and work closely with the outsourced vendor to resolve issues and challenges, including regular reviews to improve operations

• Ensure that all poorly rated calls and complaints are investigated and addressed during service recovery

• Work with appointed auditors to conduct annual audits on the contact centre

• Develop and implement improvement plans to address service lapses and issues at the contact centre

• Monitor and analyse contact centre data, and work with agency stakeholders to anticipate and manage ad hoc and seasonal volume surges

• Ensure that stakeholder agencies receive timely reports daily and monthly on the contact centre’s performance

• Handle procurement, contract management, finance and other administrative duties.
jobRequirements:

• [Customer Service and Case Management]: Demonstrate care and empathy in understanding citizen’s underlying needs and going the extra mile to help, and escalating issues/feedback to relevant agency stakeholders as part of the close-the-loop process for policies/services implementation. You should possess the ability to communicate effectively through written and oral presentation.

• [Customer Experience Strategy and Engagement]: Transform service delivery through identifying and translating new technologies to new ways of delivering contact centre services which are more customer-centric and productive. Reimagine the delivery of contact centre services from a customer-centric perspective, identify improvements and redesign the operational or service recovery processes.

• [Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements]: Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities. Able to work with ambiguity and loosely defined problem spaces and synthesise data points and ground realities to sense-make, propose and implement sound and timely solutions with stakeholders in mind.

jobDescription:
The Career Development and Transition (CDT) team in the Workforce Development (WD) cluster is responsible for strengthening public officers’ career resilience and successfully transit from job to job in their Public Service career. This includes developing a robust and forward-looking workforce; effective programmes for skills conversion; as well as a robust “life-course” career management for public officers, such as the expansion and provision of career coaching services within the Public Service.

Reporting to Deputy Director (Strategic Workforce Planning & Upskilling), you will be part of the CDT team.

[Career Coaching]

  • Coach and guide public service officers in navigating their career life stages, helping them identify their career interests and guiding them in career planning.
  • Be a case manager for high-touch cases end-to-end per year. This includes (non-exhaustively) facilitating career transitions and job placements for individuals with more complex needs, settling the relevant administrative processes and linking up with necessary stakeholders.
  • Serve as a Coach Buddy, to conduct mentoring sessions with new coaches and to uphold the professional standards set by the Public Service Career Coach Network (PSCCN).
  • Facilitate Coach Learning sessions annually to promote continuous peer learning and professional growth among coaches.
  • Support WOG and agency-level Brown Bag sessions organised by PSD to raise awareness on PSCCN and promote participation in career coaching.

[Training and Development]

  • Support the delivery of WOG Career Development Programmes annually, including CareerFitness foundational programme.
  • Support and co-facilitate Train-the-Trainer (TTT) sessions to equip agency-nominated officers with the capability to deliver inhouse CareerFitness foundational programme.
  • Guide newly inducted external and in-house trainers across agencies to deliver Career Development workshops, including CareerFitness foundational programme.
  • Train PSCCN coaches in foundational coaching skills tailored for public service supervisors.

[Advisory Role]

  • Provide advisory and programme development support to CDT team, focusing on the following areas:
    • Review and enhance WOG Career Development programmes, including interventions tailored for officers with extensive experience to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness.
    • Develop training programme to equip supervisors with basic coaching skills.
    • Review of the Public Service Retiree Network (PSRN), to incorporate new initiatives such as the Public Service alumni, and how to better use the PSRN to augment workforce needs during peacetime and crisis.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service.
